sourceDefinition: , aor. yaA^obaY , (S, M, Msb, K,) which is anomalous, (S, M, Msb,) because it has no faucial letter (S, Msb) for its second or third radical, (Msb,) and yaA^obiY , (M, Msb, K,) mentioned by IJ as sometimes said, (M,) agreeably with analogy, (TA,) and yiy^obaY , which is doubly anomalous, first because the pret. is of the measure faEala , and this pronunciation of the Y of the aor. is [regularly allowable only] in the case of a verb of the measure faEila , aor. yafoEalu , and secondly because it is only in an aor. like yiyojalu , (Sb, M,) i. e., of a verb of which the first radical letter is w or Y , (TA in art. wjl ,) and yiy^obiY , (IB, [who cites as an ex. a verse ending with the phrase Hat~aY tiy^obiyaho ,]) inf. n. A_ibaA='N (S, M, Mgh, Msb, K) and A_ibaA='a pN , (K,) or A_ibaApN , (so in a copy of the M,) or A_ibaAyapN , (so in the Msb,) He refused; or refrained, forbore, abstained, or held back; syn. AimotanaEa ; (S, Msb, MF, Bd in ii. 32, Kull p. 8,) voluntarily, or of his own free will or choice: (Bd ubi suprà, Kull:) [thus when used intransitively: and it is also used transitively:] you say, A^abaY AlA^amora he refused assent, or consent, to the thing, or affair; disagreed to it; and did not desire [ to do ] it: (Mtr in Har p. 483:) he did not assent to, consent to, approve, or choose, it; he disallowed it; rejected it: (Mgh:) and A^abay Al$~aYo 'a he disliked, was displeased with, disapproved of, or hated, the thing. (M, K.) Fr says that there is no verb with fet-h to its medial radical letter in the pret. and fut. [or aor.] unless its second or third radical is a faucial letter, except A^abaY : that AA adds rakana : but that one says rakana with yarokunu for its fut., and rakina with yarokanu for its fut.: (T:) so that the instance mentioned by AA is one of an intermixture of two dial. vars.: (TA:) Th adds qalaY and gasaA and $ajaA ; and Mbr adds jabaA : but most of the Arabs say yaqoliY and yagosuw and ya$ojuw and yajobiY . (T.) [Some other instances are mentioned by other authors; but these are verbs of which the aors. are rarely with fet-h, or are instances of the intermixture of two dial. vars.] A^abayota All~aEona is a greeting which was addressed to kings in the time of ignorance; meaning Mayest thou refuse, or dislike, (ISk, * S, * M, * Har p. 491,) to do a thing that would occasion thy being cursed! (ISk, S, M;) or, to do that for which thou wouldst deserve the being cursed! for it implies the meaning of a prayer; i. e., may God make thee to be of those who dislike the being cursed! and hence it occurs parenthetically. (Har ubi suprà.) You say also, A^abaY A^ano yuDaAma [ He refused, or did not submit, to be harmed, or injured ]. (T.) [And sometimes laA is inserted after A^ano , and is either redundant, or corroborative of the meaning of the verb, as in the case of A^ana laA or A^al~aA after manaEa .] It is said in the Kur ix. 32, wayaA^obaY All~hu A_il~aA A^ano yutim~a nawrahu , meaning But God will not consent or choose [ save to complete, or perfect, his light ]. (Bd.) And in the same xvii. 91, faA^abay A^akovaru AlnaAsa A_il~aA kufuwrFA , i. e. [ But the greater number of men have not consented to, or chosen, aught] save denying [its truth, or disbelieving it]; this phrase with A_il~aA being allowable because it is rendered by means of a negative. (Bd.) You also say, kaAna yaA^obaY All~aHoma [ He used to refuse, or dislike, flesh-meat ], (K,) or A^akola All~aHomi [ the eating of flesh-meat ]. (Mgh.) And A^abaY falaAnN AlmaA='i [ Such a one refused, or disliked, water, or the water ]: (S:) or A^abaY mino $urobi AlmaA='i [ he refused, or voluntarily refrained from, the drinking of water, or the water ]. (AAF, M.) And A^abaY Ealayohi AlA^amara , (Mgh, and Mtr. [author of the Mgh] in Har p. 483,) and Ealayohi ↓ taA^ab~aAhu , both signify He refused him his assent, or consent, to the thing, or affair. (Mtr ubi suprà, in Har.) Hence, (Mtr ubi suprà,) A^abaY Ealayohi , (Mgh, and Mtr ubi suprà,) and Ealayohi ↓ taA^ab~aY , (T, S, and Mtr ubi suprà,) He was incompliant, or unyielding, to him; he resisted him, withstood him, or repugned him; syn. AimotanaEa (T, S, Mgh, and Mtr ubi suprà) Ealayohi : (T:) thus explained because the objective complement ( AlA^amora ) is suppressed. (Mtr ubi suprà.) -A2- A^abiyotu AlT~aEaAma , (K,) or mina AlT~aEaAmi , and All~abani , (M, TA, [in a copy of the former of which the verb is written Abayotu , but this I suppose to be a mistranscription, on account of what here follows,]) like raDiyotu , (K,) inf. n. A^ab~aY , (M, and so in some copies of the K,) or A_ib~aY , (so in some copies of the K,) with kesr, and with the short final alif, (TA, [i.e. like riD~aY , but perhaps this may have been supposed to be the right reading only because the verb is likened to raDiytu , of which riD~aY is the most common inf. n.,]) I left, or relinquished, the food, (M, K,) and the milk, (M, TA,) without being satiated, or satisfied. (M, K.) ― -b2- A^abiYa AlfaSiylu , and A^ubiYa , inf. n. A^ab~aY , The young camel, or young weaned camel, suffered indigestion from the milk, and became affected with a dislike of food. (M, K.) -A3- A^abayotu as syn. with A^abawotu : see the latter.

definition: [in the CK, erroneously, A^abayotuhu ] I made him to refuse it;
sourceDefinition: [in the CK, erroneously, A^abayotuhu ] I made him to refuse it; or to refrain, forbear, abstain, or hold back, from it, voluntarily, or of his own free will or choice: (S: [this meaning being there implied, though not expressed:]) or I made him to dislike it, to be displeased with it, to disapprove of it, or to hate it: (M, K:) namely, water [&c.]. (S, M.) One says, fulaAnN baHorN laA buw^obiY , (ISk, S, K, * [in the CK, erroneously, lA yuw^obY ,]) i. e., laA yajoEaluka taA^obaAhu [ Such a one is like a sea, or great river, that will not make thee to refuse it, or dislike it, &c.]; (K;) i. e., that will not fail, or come to an end, (ISk, S, K,) by reason of its abundance. (ISk, S.) In like manner one says, of any water, maA='N laA yuw^obiY [ Water that will not fail, or come to an end ]. (TA.) And EinodanaA maA='N maA yuw^obiY With us, or at our abode, is water that does not become scanty, or little in quantity. (Lh, T, M.) And A=baY AlmaA='u The water decreased, or became deficient. (AA, from El-Mufaddal.) And qaliybN laA yuw^obiY A well that will not become exhausted: (IAar, M:) one should not say, yuw^obaY . (M, TA.) In like manner, also, one says, kalaA^a laA yuw^obaY Herbage, or pasture, that will not fail, or come to an end. (S.) And Einodahu daraAhimu laA tuw^obiY He has dirhems, or money, that will not fail, or come to an end. (TA.) And A=baY AlmaA='u signifies also The water [in a well] was, or became, difficult of access ( AimotanaEa ), so that no one was able to descend to it but by exposing himself to peril or destruction: (M:) if a drawer of water descend into the well, (T, TA,) and the water be altered for the worse in odour, (TA,) he expose himself to peril, or destruction. (T, TA.)

definition: A paucity, or deficiency, and revulsion, of the milk in the breast: (Fr, TS:) or a revulsion of the milk in the udder;
sourceDefinition: A paucity, or deficiency, and revulsion, of the milk in the breast: (Fr, TS:) or a revulsion of the milk in the udder; (K;) but the saying “in the udder” requires consideration. (TA:) You say to a woman, when she has a fever on the occasion of childbirth, A_in~amaA h*ihi AlHum~aY A_iboyapN vadoyika [ This fever is only occasioned by the paucity, or deficiency, and revulsion, of the milk in thy breast. ] (TA.)

definition: He took his A^adaApN [q.
sourceDefinition: He took his A^adaApN [q. v.]; (M;) he prepared himself; (M, K; [mentioned in the latter in art. AdY ;]) or equipped, or accoutred, himself; or furnished, or provided himself with proper, or necessary, apparatus, equipments, or the like; (M;) or he was, or became, in a state of preparation; (Yaakoob, T, S;) lils~afari for journeying, or the journey: (Yaakoob, T, S, M, K:) part. n. muw^dK . (Yaakoob, T, S.) And ↓ tA^d~Y He took his A^adaAp , [or prepared himself, &c.,] liloA^amori for the affair: (M:) or ↓ tA=dY he prepared, furnished, equipped, or accoutred, himself for the affair; (Ibn-Buzurj, Az, TA;) from AlA^adApu : (Az, TA:) or ↓ the former of these two verbs, (so in some copies of the S and K,) or ↓ the latter of them, (so in other copies of the S and K, and in the TA,) he took his A^adaAp [or equipments, &c., i. e. he prepared himself, ] for [ the vicissitudes of ] fortune: (S, K:) and ↓ taA=dawoA , inf. n. taA=dK , they took the apparatus, equipments, or the like, that should strengthen, or fortify, them against [ the vicissitudes of ] fortune &c.: (T:) [accord. to some,] Alt~aA=diY is [irregularly derived] from AlA=du , meaning “strength.” (TA.) ― -b2- He was, or became, completely armed; (T, TA;) part. n. as above; (T, S, M, Msb;) from AlA^adaApu : (T, TA:) or he was, or became, strong by means of weapons and the like; part. n. as above: (Msb:) or he was, or became, strong [in an absolute sense]; (S, K; [mentioned in the latter in art. AdY ;]) said of a man; from AlA^adaApu ; (S;) part. n. as above. (K.) -A2- A=dAhu is originally A^aEodaAhu ; the second A [in A= , for A^aA ,] being hemzeh substituted for E in the original; meaning He aided, or assisted, him: [or he avenged him: ] or it may be from AlA^adaApu ; meaning he made him to have, or gave him, or assigned to him, weapons, or arms. (Ham p. 387.) [In either case, it should be mentioned in the present art.; as AEdY belongs to art. Edw , and AlAdAp has for its pl. AlA^adawaAtu .] You say, A=dAhu EalaY ka*aA , aor. yuw^odiyhi , inf. n. A_iydaA='N , He strengthened him, and aided him, or assisted him, against such a thing, or to do such a thing. (S.) And A=dAhu EalaY fulaAnK , meaning A^aEodaAhu and A^aEaAnahu [ He avenged him of such a one; or he aided, or assisted, him against such a one ]. (M and K in art. EdY .) And mano yuw^diyniY EalaY fulaAnK Who will aid me, or assist me, against such a one? (S.) The people of El-Hijáz say, EalaY fulaAnK ↓ AsotaA^odayotuhu faA=daAniY Ealayohi , meaning AisotaEodayotuhu faA^aEodaAniY (T, S) and A^EaAnaniY (T) [ I asked of him (namely the Sultá, T, or the Emeer, S) vengeance of such a one, or aid against such a one, and he avenged me of him, or aided me against him ].

sourceDefinition: An instrument; a tool; an implement; a utensil: and instruments; tools; implements; utensils; apparatus; equipments; equipage; accoutrements; furniture; gear; tackling: syn. A=lapN : (T, S, M, Msb, K:) of any tradesman or craftsman; with which he performs the work of his trade or craft: and of war; A^adaApu AlHarobi signifying weapons, or arms: (Lth, T:) and for an affair [of any kind]: (M:) [applied also to the apparatus of a camel, or of a camel's saddle, &c.: (see HidojN :)] and ↓ A_idaAwapN signifies the same; (M, TA;) and ↓ A^adaAwapN : (TA:) and ↓ A^adiY~N , (S, TA,) like ganiY~N , (TA,) [in some copies of the S A=diY~N ,] signifies apparatus, equipments, equipage, accoutrements, furniture, gear, tackling, implements, tools, or the like; syn. A^uhobapN : (S, TA:) the pl. of A^adaAhN is A^adawaAtN . (T, S, Msb, K.) You say, A^axa*a A^adaAtahu [ He took his apparatus, &c.; or prepared, furnished, equipped, or accoutred, himself ]; (S, M, K;) liloA^amori [ for the affair ], and lils~afari [ for journeying, or the journey ], (M,) and lild~ahori [ for the vicissitudes of fortune ]: (T, S, K:) and it is related on the authority of Ks, that they said A^axa*a hadaAtahu ; substituting h for A^ . (Lh, M). And A^xa*otu li*`lika ↓ AlA^amor A^adiy~ahu i. e. A^uhobatahu [ I took for that affair its apparatus, &c.]. (S, TA.) And naHonu EalaY lilS~alaApi ↓ A^adiY~K We are in a state of preparation for prayer. (S, TA.) ― -b2- [Hence, in grammar, A particle; as being a kind of auxiliary; including the article Al , the preposition, the conjunction, and the interjection; but not the adverbial noun.]

definition: A limit, or boundary, (As, T, S, M, Mgh, Msb, K,) making a separation (Msb) between two pieces of land;
sourceDefinition: A limit, or boundary, (As, T, S, M, Mgh, Msb, K,) making a separation (Msb) between two pieces of land; (Msb, K;) a sign, or mark, (As, T, S, Mgh,) of the limits, or boundaries, between two pieces of land: (S:) and a separation between houses and estates: (M:) and a dam between two pieces of land sown or for sowing: (Th, M:) Yaakoob asserts that its f is a substitute for the v of A^urovapN [which is, however, less com- mon]: (M:) the pl. is A^urafN , (T, S, M, &c.,) signifying, accord. to Lh, like A^uravN , limits, or boundaries, between two pieces of land [&c.]; (T;) and it is said in a trad., that these cut off Al$~ufoEap [i. e. the right of preemption]; (T, S, Mgh;) meaning, in the language of the people of El- Hijáz, signs, or marks, and limits, or boundaries. (T.) Th relates that an Arab woman said, jaEala Ealay~a zawojiY A^urofapF laA A^ajuwzuhaA , i. e. My husband set me a sign, or mark, [or limit, ] beyond which I should not pass. (M.) And A^urofapu A^ajalK signifies An extreme limit of a period of existence. (TA, from a trad.) ― -b2- Also A knot. (Sgh, K.)

sourceDefinition: , aor. , inf. n. A^azomN and A^uzuwmN , He bit with the whole mouth, vehemently: (K:) or with the canine teeth: or you say, A^azamahu , and A^azama Ealayohi , meaning he bit it, and then repeated [ the action ] upon it, not letting it go: or he seized upon it with his mouth: (TA:) or A^azamahu signifies [simply] he bit it: (S:) and A^azama Ealayohi , aor. , inf. n. A^azomN ; and A^azima , aor. , inf. n. A^azamN ; the same; or he seized, or took hold, upon it with his teeth: (Msb:) and A^azamotu yada Alr~ajuli I bit the arm, or hand, of the man most vehemently. (TA.) A^azama bihaA occurs in a trad. as meaning He bit it, (referring to a ring of a coat of mail,) and held it between two of his central teeth. (AO.) And in another trad., A^azama fiy yadihi , meaning He bit his arm, or hand. (TA.) And you say, A^azama Alfarasu EalaY faA^osi All~ijaAmi The horse seized [ with his teeth, or champed, ] upon the fA^s [q. v.] of the bit. (K.) And A^azomN signifies also The cutting with the canine tooth, and with a knife, (K,) and with other things. (TA.) ― -b2- [And hence,] A^azama EalayonaA , (S, Msb, * K, *) aor. , inf. n. A^azomN (S) and A^uzuwmN , (TA,) said of a time, (S, Msb,) or a year, (K,) It was, or became, distressful, or afflictive, to us, [ as though it bit us, ] by drought, dearth, or scarcity; (S, Msb, K;) and scant in its good things; (S;) as also A^azima , aor. , inf. n. A^azamN . (Msb.) And A^aSaAbatohumo sanapN A^azamatohumo , (S, K, *) inf. n. A^azomN , (S,) A year, or year of dearth or drought or sterility, befell them, which extirpated them: (S, K: *) or, accord. to Sh, the verb in this sense is only with w . (TA. [See art. Arm .]) ― -b3- [Hence also,] A^azama bihi , (AZ, S, K,) inf. n. A^azomN , (TA,) He clave to him, namely, his companion; (AZ, S, K;) and to it, namely, a place. (K.) And A^azama Ealayohi , (K,) aor. , inf. n. A^azomN , (TA,) He kept, attended, or applied himself, constantly, perseveringly, or assiduously, to it; (K;) he clave to it. (TA.) And A^azama biDayoEatihi , or lahaA , (accord. to different copies of the K, the former being the reading in the TA,) and EalayohA , (TA,) inf. n. A^uzuwmN , (AZ, TA,) He kept, attended, or applied himself, constantly, perseveringly, or assiduously, to his DyEp [or land, &c.]. (AZ, K, TA.) ― -b4- A^azama , (Nh, K,) inf. n. A^azomN , (Nh, TA,) also signifies He held his teeth together, one upon another: (Nh:) [and he compressed, or put together, his lips: (see A=zimN :)] and he closed, or locked, a door. (K, TA.) It is said in a trad., Als~iwaAku tasotaEomiluhu Einoda tagay~uri Alfami mina AlA^azomi The stick for cleaning the teeth, thou shalt use it on the occasion of the mouth's becoming altered in odour from the holding of the teeth together. (Nh.) ― -b5- [And hence,] A^azama , (S, Nh, Msb,) inf. n. A^azomN , (Msb, K,) He held, refrained, or abstained, (S, K, *) Eani Al$~aYo'i from the thing: (S, TA:) and he held, refrained, or abstained, from desiring much: (TA:) and from food (Msb, K *) and drink; (Msb;) as also A^azima , aor. , inf. n. A^azamN : (Msb:) and from speech; (Nh, K; *) like as does the faster from food: and hence, (Nh,) or from the next preceding signification, (Msb,) HimoyapN [meaning as explained in what follows] is termed A^azomN : (Nh, Msb:) but accord. to the relation commonly known, of a trad. in which A^azama is said to occur in the last of the senses explained above, the word is A^aram~a , with r and with teshdeed in the case of the m . (Nh.) It is related in a trad., that 'Omar having asked El-Hárith Ibn-Keledeh, the Tabiyb of the Arabs, “What is the [best] remedy?” (S,) or having asked him respecting [the best] medical, or curative, treatment, (Msb,) the latter said, AlA^azomu , meaning AlHimoyapu ; (S, Msb;) both these words here meaning The practising abstinence; (PS;) or the abstaining, or desisting, from eating: (TA:) or, in this instance, (TA,) AlA^azomu signifies the not putting in food upon food: and (some say, TA) the being silent: (K, TA:) and it signifies also strength. (TA.) ― -b6- A^azama Al$~aYo'u The thing became contracted; became drawn together, or compressed; as also A^azima , aor. . (K.)

A^alowN (T, M, Mgh, K) and A^uluw~u (K, TA [in a copy of the M A^aluw~N ]) and A^uliY~N ; (K, TA; [in a copy of the M A^aliY~N , and in a copy of the Mgh written with fet-h and damm to the A^ ;]) and ↓ A^al~aY , (S, M, K,) aor. yuw^al~Y , inf. n. taA^oliyapN ; (S;) and ↓ Ay^tlY [written with the disjunctive alif AiytalaY ]; (S, M, K;) [and ↓ taA^al~Y , as appears from an ex. in a verse cited in art. n$b , q. v.;] He fell short; or he fell short of doing what was requisite, or what he ought to have done; or he flagged, or was remiss; syn. qaS~ara : (S, M, K; and Fr, IAar, T, Mgh, in explanation of the first of these verbs:) and he was slow, or tardy: (M, K; and AA, T, S, in explanation of the second verb:) or he flagged, or was remiss, or languid, and weak. (A Heyth and T in explanation of all of the above-mentioned verbs except the last.) You say, A^alaA fiY AlA^amori , (Mgh,) and ↓ Ay^tlY fiyhi , (S,) He fell short, &c., ( qaS~ara ,) in the affair. (S, Mgh.) In the saying, lam yaA^olu A^ano yaEodila fiY *lika , i. e. He did not fall short, &c., ( lamo yuqaS~aro ,) in acting equitably and equally in that, fiY is suppressed before An : but in the phrase, lamo yaA^oluw mina AlEadoli , as some relate it, [the meaning intended seems to be, They did not hold back, or the like, from acting equitably; for here] the verb is made to imply the meaning of another verb: and such is the case in the saying, laA A=luwka nuSoHFA , meaning I will not refuse to thee, nor partially or wholly deprive thee of, sincere, honest, or faithful, advice: (Mgh:) or this last signifies I will not flag, or be remiss, nor fall short, to thee in giving sincere, honest, or faithful, advice. (T, S. *) It is said in the Kur [iii. 114], laA yaA_oluwnakumo xabaAlFA , meaning They will not fall short, or flag, or be remiss, in corrupting you. (IAar, T.) And the same meaning is assigned to the verb in the saying A^uwluw AlofaDoli minokumo ↓ walaA yaA^otali , in the Kur [xxiv. 22], by A'Obeyd: but the preferable rendering in this case is that of A Heyth, which will be found below: see 4. (T.) Ks mentions the phrase, A^aqobala biDarobapK laA yaA^olu [ He came with a blow, not falling short, &c.], for lA yaA^oluw ; like laA A^adori [for lA A^adoriY ]. (S, M: [but in the copies of the former in my hands, for biDarobapK , I find yaDoribuhu .]) ↓ A^al~aY [with teshdeed] is also said of a dog, and of a hawk, meaning He fell short of attaining the game that he pursued. (TA.) And of a cake of bread, meaning It was slow in becoming thoroughly baked. (IAar, IB.) [See also the phrase laA daryota walaA Ay^otalyota in a later part of this paragraph.] ― -b2- You say also, maA A^alawotu Al$~ayo'a , (K,) or maA A^alawotu A^ano A^afoEalahu , (M,) inf. n A^alwN (M, K) and A^uluw~N , (K, TA, [in a copy of the M A^ulowN ,]) meaning I did not leave, quit, cease from, omit, or neglect, (M, K,) the thing, (K,) or doing it. (M.) And fulaAnN laA yaA^oluw xayorFA Such a one does not leave, quit, or cease from, doing good. (M.) And maA A^alawotu jahodFA I did not leave, omit, or neglect, labour, exertion, effort, or endeavour: and the vulgar say, maA A=luwka jahodFA ; but this is wrong: so says As. (T. [See, however, similar phrases mentioned above.]) -A2- A^alaA , aor. as above, (TA,) inf. n. A^alowN , (IAar, T, TA,) also signifies He strove, or laboured; he exerted himself, or his power or ability; (IAar, T, TA;) as also ↓ taA^al~aY : (T, TA:) the contr. of a signification before mentioned; i. e. “he flagged;,” or “was remiss, or languid, and weak.” (TA.) You say, A^ataAniY fiY HaAjapK faA^alawotu fiyhaA He came to me respecting a want, and I strove, or laboured, &c., to accomplish it. (T.) ― -b2- And A^alaAhu , aor. as above, (T, S,) inf. n. (T.) And it is said in a trad., A=lay mino nisaAy^ihi $ahorFA He swore that he would not go in to his wives for a month: the verb being here made trans. by means of mn because it implies the meaning of AimotinaAE , which is thus trans. (TA.) (TA.) -A2- A=lato , inf. n. as above, She (a woman) took for herself, or made, or prepared, a miy^olaAp , q. v. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: , (so in some copies of the S, and so in the K in the last division of that work, and in the CK in art. Al , [and thus it is always pronounced,] but in some copies of the K in art. Al it is written A^uluwna , [as though to show the original form of its termination,]) or A^uwluw , (so in the M, and in some copies of the S, [and thus it is generally written,]) i. q. *awuw [ Possessors of; possessed of; possessing; having ]; a pl. which has no sing. (S, M, K) of its own proper letters, (S, K,) its sing. being *uw : (S:) or, as some say, a quasi-pl. n., of which the sing. is *uw : (K:) the fem. is A^ulaAtu , (so in some copies of the S and K, [and thus it is always pronounced,]) or A^uwlaAtu , (so in other copies of the S and K, [and thus it is generally written,]) of which the sing. is *aAtu : (S, K:) it is as though its sing. were A^ulN , (M, K, [in the CK AlN ,]) the [final] w [in the masc.] being the sign of the pl., (M,) for it has w [for its termination] in the nom. case, and Y in the accus. and gen. (M, K.) It is never used but as a prefixed noun. (M, K.) The following are exs. of the nom. case: naHonu A^uwluw quw~apK waA^uwluw baA^osK $adiydK [ We are possessors of strength, and possessors of vehement courage ], in the Kur [xxvii. 23]; and A^uwluw AloA^aroHaAmi baEoDuhumo A^awolaY bibaEoDK [ The possessors of relationships, these have the best title to inheritance, one with respect to another ], in the same [viii. last verse and xxxiii. 6]; (TA;) and jaA='a niY A^uwluw AlA^alobaAbi [ The persons of understandings came to me ]; and A^uwlaAtu AlA^aHomaAli [ Those who are with child; occurring in the Kur lxv. 4]: (S:) and the following are exs. of the accus. and gen. cases: wa*aroniY waAlomuka*~abiyna A^uwliY Aln~aEomapi [ And leave thou me, or let me alone, with the beliers, or discrediters, (i. e., commit their case to me,) the possessors of ease and plenty ], in the Kur [lxxiii. 11]; and latanuw'u biAloEuSobapi A^uwliY Alquw~api [ Would weigh down the company of men possessing strength ], in the same [xxviii. 76]. (TA.) waA^uwliY AloA^amori minokumo , in the Kur [iv. 62], [ And those, of you, who are possessors of command ], (M, K, *) accord. to Aboo-Is-hák, (M,) means the companions of the Prophet, and the men of knowledge their followers, (M, K,) and the possessors of command, who are their followers, when also possessors of knowledge and religion: (K:) or, as some say, [simply] the possessors of command; for when these are possessors of knowledge and religion, and take, or adopt and maintain, and follow, what the men of knowledge say, to obey them is of divine obligation: and in general those who are termed A^uwluw AlA^amori , of the Muslims, are those who superintend the affairs of such with respect to religion, and everything conducing to the right disposal of their affairs. (M.)

sourceDefinition: , accord. to Sb, is originally with w in the place of the [ Y , i. e. the final] alif; and so is EalaY ; for the alifs [in these two particles] are not susceptible of imáleh; [i. e., they may not be pronounced ilè and 'alè;] and if either be used as the proper name of a man, the dual [of the former] is A_ilawaAni and [that of the latter] EalawaAni ; but when a pronoun is affixed to it, the alif is changed into yé, so that you say A_ilayoka and Ealayoka ; though some of the Arabs leave it as it was, saying A_ilaAka and EalaAka . (S.) It is a prep., or particle governing a noun in the gen. case, (S, Mughnee, K,) and denotes the end, as opposed to [ mino , which denotes] the beginning, of an extent, or of the space between two points or limits; (S, M;) or the end of an extent (T, Mughnee, K) of place; [signifying To, or as far as; ] as in the phrase [in the Kur xvii. 1], mina Almasojidi AlHaraAmi A_ilaY Almasojidi AlA^aqoSaY [ From the Sacred Mosque to, or as far as, the Furthest Mosque; meaning from the mosque of Mekkeh to that of Jerusalem]; (Mughnee, K;) or in the saying, xarajotu mina Alkuwfapi A_ilaY mak~apa [ I went forth from El-Koofeh to Mekkeh ], which may mean that you entered it, [namely, the latter place,] or that you reached it without entering it, for the end includes the beginning of the limit and the furthest part thereof, but does not extend beyond it. (S.) [In some respects it agrees with Hat~aY , q. v. And sometimes it signifies Towards; as in naZara A_ilaY~a He looked towards me; and maAla A_ilayohi He, or it, inclined towards him, or it. ― -b2- It also denotes the end of a space of time; [signifying To, till, or until; ] as in the saying [in the Kur ii. 183], vum~a A^atim~uwA AlS~iyaAma A_ilaY All~ayoli [ Then complets ye the fasting to, or till, or until, the night ]. (Mughnee, K.) [Hence, A_ilaY A^ano (followed by a mansoob aor.) Till, or until: and A_ilaY mataY Till, or until, what time, or when? i. e. how long? and also to, till, or until, the time when. See also the last sentence in this paragraph.] ― -b3- [In like manner it is used in the phrases A_ilaY gayori *lika , and A_ilaY A=xirihi , meaning, ( And so on, ) to other things, and to the end thereof; equivalent to et cœtera. ] ― -b4- Sometimes, (S,) it occurs in the sense of maEa , (T, S, M, Mughnee, K,) when a thing is joined to another thing; (Mughnee, K;) as in the phrase [in the Kur iii. 45 and lxi. 14], mano A^anoSaAriY A_ilaY All~`hi [ Who will be my aiders with, or in addition to, God? ], (S, Mughnee, K,) accord. to the Koofees and some of the Basrees; (Mughnee;) i. e. who will be joined to God in aiding me? (M, TA;) and as in the saying [in the Kur iv. 2], walaA taA^okuluwA A^amowaAlahumo A_ilaY A^amowaAlikumo [ And devour not ye their possessions with, or in addition to, your possessions ]; (T, S;) and [in the same, ii. 13,] waA_i*aA xalawoA A_ilaY $ayaA Tiynihimo [ And when they are alone with their devils ]; (S;) and in the saying, Al*~awodu A_ilaY Al*~awodi A_ibilN [ A few she-camels with, or added to, a few she-camels are a herd of camels ], (S, Mughnee, K,) a prov., meaning (assumed tropical:) a little with a little makes much; (S and A in art. *wd , q. v.;) though one may not say, A_ilaY zayodK maAlN meaning maEa zayodK maAlN : (Mughnee:) so too in the saying, fulaAnN HaliymN A_ilaY A^adabK wafiqohK [ Such a one is clement, or forbearing, with good education, or polite accomplishments, and intelligence, or knowledge of the law ]; (M, TA;) and so, accord. to Kh, in the phrase, A^aHomadu All~`ha A_ilayoka [ I praise God with thee: but see another rendering of this phrase below]. (ISh.) In the saying in the Kur [v. 8], faAgosiluwA wujuwhakumo waA^ayodiyakumo A_ilaY AlmaraAfiqi , it is disputed whether [the meaning be Then wash ye your faces, and your arms with the elbows, or, and your arms as far as the elbows; i. e., whether] the elbows be meant to be included among the parts to be washed, or excluded therefrom. (T.) A context sometimes shows that what follows it is included in what precedes it; as in qaraA^otu AlquroA=na mino A^aw~alihi A_ilaY A=xirihi [ I read, or recited, the Kurán, from the beginning thereof to the end thereof ]: or that it is excluded; as in vum~a A^atim~uwA AlS~iyaAma A_ilaY All~ayoli [explained above]: when this is not the case, some say that it is included if it be of the same kind [as that which precedes]; some, that it is included absolutely; and some, that it is excluded absolutely; and this is the right assertion; for with the context it is in most instances excluded. (Mughnee.) ― -b5- It is also used to show the grammatical agency of the noun governed by it, after a verb of wonder; or after a noun of excess importing love or hatred; [as in maA A^aHab~ahu A_ilaY~a How lovely, or pleasing, is he to me! (TA in art. Hb ,) and maA A^abogaDahu A_ilaY~a How hateful, or odious, is he to me! (S in art. bgD ;) and] as in the saying [in the Kur xii. 33], rab~i Als~ijonu A^aHab~u A_ilaY~a [ O my Lord, the prison is more pleasing to me ]. (Mughnee, K.) [This usage is similar to that explained in the next sentence.] ― -b6- It is syn. with Einoda ; (S, M, Mughnee, Msb, K;) as in the phrase, huwa A^a$ohaY A_ilaY~a mino ka*aA [ It is more desirable, or pleasant, in my estimation than such a thing ]; (Msb;) and in the saying of the poet, A^amo laA sabiyla A_ilaY Al$~abaAbi wa*ikoruhu A^a$ohaY A_ilaY~a mina Alr~aHiyqi Als~alosali [ Is there no way of return to youth, seeing that the remembrance thereof is more pleasant to me, or in my estimation, than mellow wine? ] (Mughnee, K:) and accord. to this usage of A_ilaY in the sense of Einoda may be explained the saying, A^anoti TaAliqN A_ilaY sanapK , meaning Thou art divorced at the commencement of a year. (Msb.) ― -b7- It is also syn. with li ; as in the phrase, waAlA^amoru A_ilayoka [ And command, or to command, belongeth unto Thee, meaning God, as in the Kur xiii. 30, and xxx. 3], (Mughnee, K,) in a trad. respecting supplication: (TA:) or, as some say, it is here used in the manner first explained above, meaning, is ultimately referrible to Thee: and they say, A^aHomadu All~`ha A_ilayoka , meaning, I tell the praise of God unto thee: (Mughnee:) [but see another rendering of this last phrase above:] you say also, *aAka A_ilayoka That is committed to thee, or to thy arbitration. (Har p. 329.) ― -b8- It also occurs as syn. with EalaY ; as in the saying in the Kur [xvii. 4], waqaDayonaA A_ilaY baniY A_isoraAy^iyla [ And we decreed against the children of Israel ]: (Msb:) or this means and we revealed to the children of Israel (Bd, Jel) decisively. (Bd.) ― -b9- It is also syn. with fiY ; (M, Mughnee, K;) as in the saying [in the Kur iv. 89 and vi.12], layajomaEan~akumo A_ilaY yawomi AlqiyaAmapi [ He will assuredly collect you together on the day of resurrection ]: (K:) thus it may be used in this instance accord. to Ibn-Málik: (Mughnee:) and it is said to be so used in the saying [of En-Nábighah, (M, TA,)] falaA tatorukan~iY biAlwaEiydi kaA^an~aniY A_ilay Aln~aAsi maToliY~N bihi AlqaAru A^ajorabu [ Then do not thou leave me with threatening, as though I were, among men, smeared with tar, being like a mangy camel]; (M, Mughnee;) or, accord. to some, there is an ellipsis and inversion in this verse; AlY being here in dependence upon a word suppressed, and the meaning being, smeared with pitch, [like a camel,] yet being united to men: or, accord. to Ibn-'Osfoor, mTlY~ is here considered as made to import the meaning of rendered hateful, or odious; for he says that if AlY were correctly used in the sense of fY , it it would be allowable to say, zayodNA_ilaY Alkuwfapi : (Mughnee:) [or the meaning may be, as though I were, compared to men, a mangy camel, smeared with pitch: for] I'Ab said, after mentioning 'Alee, EilomiY A_ilaY Eilomihi kaAlqaraArapi fiY AlmuvuEanojari , meaning My knowledge compared to his knowledge is like the qrArp [or small pool of water left by a torrent ] placed by the side of the middle of the sea [or the main deep ]. (K in art. vEjr .) It is also [said to be] used in the sense of fY in the saying in the Kur [1xxix. 18], halo laka A_ilaY A^ano tazak~aY [ Wilt thou purify thyself from infidelity?] because it imports the meaning of invitation. (TA.) ― -b10- It is also used [in a manner contr. to its primitive application, i. e.,] to denote beginning, [or origination,] being syn. with mino ; as in the saying [of a poet], taquwlu waqado EaAlayotu biAlkuwri fawoqahaA A^ayusoqay falaA yarowaY A_ilaY~a Abonu A^aHomaraA [ She says, (namely my camel,) when I have raised the saddle upon her, Will Ibn-Ahmar be supplied with drink and not satisfy his thirst from me? i. e., will he never be satisfied with drawing forth my sweat?]. (Mughnee, K.) ― -b11- It is also used as a corroborative, and is thus [syntactically] redundant; as in the saying in the Kur [xiv. 40], faAjoEalo A^afoy^idapF mina Aln~aAsi tahowaY A_ilayohimo , with fet-h to the w [in thwY ], (Mughnee, K,) accord. to one reading, (Mughnee,) meaning tahowaAhumo [i. e. And make Thou hearts of men to love them ]: (K:) so says Fr: but some explain it by saying that thwY imports the meaning of tamiylu ; or that it is originally tahowiY , with kesr, the kesreh being changed to a fet-hah, and the yé to an alif, as when one says raDaA for raDiYa , and naASaApN for naASiyapN : so says Ibn-Málik; but this requires consideration; for it is a condition in such cases that the Y in the original form must be movent. (Mughnee.) [See art. hwY .] ― -b12- Aall~`hum~a A_ilayoka , occurring in a trad., [is elliptical, and] means O God, I complain unto Thee: or take Thou me unto Thee. (TA.) ― -b13- And A^anaA minoka waA_ilayoka means I am of thee, and related to thee. (TA.) ― -b14- You say also, Ai*ohabo A_ilayoka , meaning Betake, or apply, thyself to, or occupy thyself with, thine own affairs. (T, K. *) And similar to this is the phrase used by El-Aashà, faA*ohabiY maA A_ilayoki . (TA.) And A_ilayokumo [alone is used in a similar manner, elliptically, or as an imperative verbal noun, and] means Betake, or apply, yourselves to, or occupy yourselves with, your own affairs, ( Ai*ohabuwA A_ilayokumo ,) and retire ye, or withdraw ye, to a distance, or far away, from us. (ISk.) And A_ilayoka Ean~iY means Hold, or refrain, thou from me: (T, K:) or remove, withdraw, or retire, thou to a distance from me: Alyk used in this sense is an imperative verbal noun. (Har p. 508.) Sb says, (M,) or Akh, (Har ubi suprà,) I heard an Arab of the desert, on its being said to him A_ilayoka , reply, A_ilaY~a ; as though it were said to him Remove, withdraw, or retire, thou to a distance, and he replied, I will remove, &c. (M.) Aboo-Fir' own says, satirizing a Nabathæan woman of whom he asked for water to drink, A_i*aA Talabota AlmaA='i qaAlato layokaA [ When thou shalt demand water, she will say, Retire thou to a distance ]; meaning, [by lykA , i. e. layoka with an adjunct alif for the sake of the rhyme,] A_ilayoka , in the sense last explained above. (M.) ― -b15- One also says, A_ilayoka ka*aA , meaning, Take thou such a thing. (T, K.) ― -b16- When A_ilaY is immediately followed by the interrogative maA , both together are written A_ilaAma [meaning, To what? whither? and till, or until, what time, or when? i. e. how long? ]; and in like manner one writes EalaAma for EalaY maA , (S * and K voce mA ,) and Hat~aAma for Hat~aY . (S voce Hat~aY .)

definition: [ A falling short;
sourceDefinition: [ A falling short; or a falling short of what is requisite, or what one ought to do; or a flagging, or remissness; and slowness, or tardiness: ] a subst. from A^alaA as signifying qaS~ara and A^aliy~apF . (M.) Hence the prov., (M,) A_il~aA HaDiy~apF falaA A^aliy~apF , i. e. If I be not in favour, and high estimation, I will not cease seeking, and labouring, and wearying myself, to become so: (M, K: *) or if thou fail of good fortune in that which thou seekest, fall not short, or flag not, or be not remiss, in showing love, or affection, to men; may-be thou wilt attain somewhat of that which thou wishest: originally relating to a woman who becomes displeasing to her husband: (S in art. HZw :) it is one of the proverbs of women: one says, if I be not in favour, and high estimation, with my husband, I will not fall short, or flag, or be remiss, in that which may render me so, by betaking myself to that which he loveth: (T and TA in art. HZw :) Meyd says that the two nouns are in the accus. case because the implied meaning is A_il~aA A^akuno HaZiy~apF falaA A^akuno A^aliy~apF ; the latter noun being [accord. to him] for ↓ A=liyapN , for which it may be put for the sake of conformity [with the former]; and the former having the signification of the pass. part. n. of A^aHoZaY , or that of the part. n. of HaZiYa [or HaZiyato ]. A^alaAyaA . (S, Mgh.) A poet says, (namely, Kutheiyir, TA,) qaliyluA AlA^alaAyaA HaAfiZN liyamiynihi waA_ino sabaqato minohu AlA^aliy~apu bar~ati [ A person of few oaths, who keeps his oath from being uttered on ordinary or mean occasions; but if the oath has proceeded from him at any former time, or hastily, it proves true ]: (S, TA:) or, as IKh relates it, qaliylu AlA_ilaA='i ; meaning, he says, qaliylu AlA_ylaA='i ; the Y being suppressed: see 4. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: (S, Msb, K) and A_iwaz~apN , (S,) or the latter is the n. un. of the former, [which is a coll. gen. n.,] (Msb,) i. q. baT~N [The goose, or geese; and the duck, or ducks; but Awz~ is generally applied to the former of these birds; and bT~ , to the latter; agreeably with a statement in the Jm, that baT~N is applied by the Arabs to the small, and A_iwaz~N to the large ]; (S, K;) as also waz~N , of which the n. un. is waz~apN : (Msb:) A_iwaz~N is of the measure fiEal~N : (Msb:) [but see what follows:] the pl. is A_iwaz~uwna , (S, Msb, K,) a form which is sometimes used, (S, Msb,) and which is anomalous. (Msb.) [See also kurokiY~N .] ― -b2- [Hence,] A_iwaz~N also signifies (assumed tropical:) Short and thick: (K:) fleshy without being tall: (Lth, TA:) fem. with p . (TA.) El-'Okberee asserts that the A^ is augmentative, because it is followed by three radical letters: (MF, TA:) but ISd says that it is of the measure fiEal~N , and may not be of the measure A_ifoEalN , [i. e., originally A_iwozazN ,] because this does not occur as the measure of an epithet. (TA.) [It seems, however, that Awz~ is in this case a subst. used tropically as an epithet, after the manner of many nicknames.] ― -b3- Also, applied to a man, and to a horse, and to a camel, Firm in make: (AHei in the Expos. of the Tes-heel, and TA:) or, applied to a horse, compact and strong in make. (TA.)

(TA.)

sourceDefinition: , aor. yaw^uwlu , (T, S, M, &c.,) inf. n. A^awolN (T, M, Mgh, Msb, K) and maA=lN (M, K) and A_iyaAlN , which last is used as a subst. in relation to objects of the mind, (Msb,) and A^ayoluwlapN [like dayomuwmapN ], (TA,) He, or it, returned; syn. rajaEa ; (T, S, M, Mgh, Msb, K;) and EaAda ; (T;) [and he resorted; (see an instance voce A_iy~alN ;)] A_ilayohi to it; (M, K;) namely a thing [of any kind; the thing, or place, whence he, or it, originated, or came; his, or its, origin, or source; his, or its, original state, condition, quantity, weight, &c.; any place; and a former action, or saying, or the like: see rajaEa , by which, as the explanation of A=la , may be meant to be implied some other significations, here following, which these two verbs have in common]: (M:) and A=la Eanohu he (a man, M) returned, or reverted, from it. (M, K.) ― -b2- From A=la as syn. with rajaEa is the phrase, fulaAnN yaw^uwlu A_ilaY karamK [meaning either Such a one returns to generosity, or, as karamN is used in the sense of kiraAmN , is referable to generous, or noble, ancestors ]. (TA.) [And hence the phrase,] A=la A_ilayohi binasabK [ He bore a relation to him, as a member to a head, by kindred ], and bidiynK [ by religion ]. (Ibn-'Arafeh.) And the saying, in a trad., mano SaAma Ald~ahora falaA SaAma wa laA A=la , i. e. (tropical:) [ He who fasts ever, or always, may he neither fast] nor return to what is good. (TA.) [In the Mgh, art. dhr , for A=l I find A^afoTara ; and it is there said that this is an imprecation uttered by the Prophet, lest a man should believe this kind of fasting to be ordained by God; or, through impotence, should become insincere; or because, by fasting all the days of the year, he would do so on the days on which fasting is forbidden. See other readings voce A^alaA in art. Alw .]) ― -b3- Hence also the saying, A=lti AlD~arobahu A_ilaY Aln~afosi , meaning (assumed tropical:) The blow, or stroke, resulted in destroying life; in slaying, or killing. (Mgh.) ― -b4- Hence also, A=la AlA^amoru A_ilaY ka*aA [ The affair, or case, became ultimately reduced to such a state, or condition; came to such a result; came to be thus ]. (Msb.) ― -b5- Hence also, Tabaxotu Al$~araAba faA=la A_ilaY qadori ka*aA I cooked the wine, or beverage, and it became reduced ( rajaEa ) to such a quantity. (S.) And Tabaxahu Hat~aY A=la A_ilaY Alv~uluvi A^awiAlr~ubEi He cooked it (namely nabiy* [i. e. must, or mead, or wort,]) until it became reduced ( rajaEa ) to the third, or to the fourth: (T:) or, said of the same, (Mgh,) or of medicine, (TA,) Hat~aY A=la Alman~aAni man~aA waAHidFA , (Mgh,) or A_ilaY man~K waAHidK , (TA,) until twice the quantity, or weight, of a man~ became [ reduced to ] ( SaAra ) one man~ . (Mgh.) ― -b6- [Hence also, majaAzu AlA^awoli The proleptic, or anticipative, trope; as faSiylN applied to “a young camel” before it is weaned, because it is to be weaned.] ― -b7- [And hence also, app.,] A=la Al$~aYo'u , inf. n. maA=lN , The thing [ became reduced in quantity or size; ] decreased; diminished; or became defective, or deficient. (M, K.) And A=la laHomu Aln~aAqapi The flesh of the she-camel went away, so that she became lean, or slender and lean, or lean and lank in the belly. (T, K.) ― -b8- A=la , (T, S, M, K,) inf. n. A^awolN (T, M, K) and A_iyaAlN , (M, K,) is also said of tar, (T, S, M,) and of honey, (S,) and of milk, (M,) and of wine, or beverage, (TA,) and of urine, (M,) or of the urine of camels that have been contented with green pasture instead of water, at the end of their being in that state, (T,) and of oil, (M, K,) and other things, (K,) as meaning It became thick: (T, S, M, K:) said of milk, it thickened and coagulated: (M:) said of wine, or beverage, it thickened, and became intoxicating in its utmost degree: (Az, TA:) and said of oil, it attained its full perfume, or sweetness of odour, by being well prepared or compounded. (T.) ― -b9- maA laka taw^uwlu A_ilaY katifayoka [written in the TA without any vowel-signs, app. meaning (tropical:) What aileth thee that thou shruggest thy shoulders? lit., drawest thyself together to thy two shoulder-blades? ] is said [to a man] A_i*aA A@noDam~a A_ilayohimaA waA@jotamaEa [when he draws himself together to them, and contracts himself]; and is a tropical phrase: so says Z. (TA.) ― -b10- A=la mino fulaAnK He escaped, or became safe or secure, from such a one: a dial. var. of waA^ala : (T, K:) of the dial. of the Ansár. (TA.) ― -b11- You say also, A=la , aor. yaw^uwlu ; (T, Msb;) or A^awila , aor. yaA^owalu ; (K;) meaning He, or it, preceded; went before; was, or became, before, beforehand, first, or foremost; (T, Msb, K;) and came: (Msb:) with this, also, waA^ala is syn.; and from it [says Az] is most probably derived A^aw~alu , so that its original form is A^aA^owalu : [or, as Fei says,] hence is derived the phrase, used by the vulgar, AlEa$oru AlA^aw~alu with fet-h to the hemzeh [as meaning “the first, or preceding, ten (nights of the month),” for AlA^uwalu , pl. of AlA^uwlaY , fem. of AlA^aw~alu ; but this is generally regarded as being originally AlA^awoA^alu , from waA^ala ]. (Msb.) -A2- A=lahu : see 2. ― -b2- Accord. to Lth, (TA,) A^ulotuhu , (M, K,) aor. A^aw^uwluhu , inf. n. A^awolN , (TA,) signifies I made it (namely, milk, M, or oil &c., K) to thicken, (M, K,) and to coagulate; (M;) the verb being both intrans. and trans.: (K:) but Az says that it is not known as trans., in this sense, in the language of the Arabs [of the classical ages]. sourceDefinition: , (M, K,) inf. n. taA^owiylN , (TA,) He returned it (namely, a thing, M) to him, or it; he made it, or caused it, to return to him, or it; syn. rajaEahu : (M, K: in the CK raj~aEahu :) and ↓ A=lahu also signifies the same; syn. rad~ahu . (TA.) You say, A^aw~ala A@ll~`hu Ealayoka DaAl~ataka May God restore to thee thy stray; (T, * TA;) cause it to return to thee; (TA;) bring together thee and it. (T.) And A^aw~alotuhu A_ilaY ka*aA I caused him, or it, to come to such a state or condition; brought, or reduced, him, or it, thereto; syn. Say~arotuhu A_ilayohi . (T.) ― -b2- See also 1, near the end of the paragraph, in two places. ― -b3- taA^owiylN also signifies The discovering, detecting, revealing, developing, or disclosing, or the explaining, expounding, or interpreting, that to which a thing is, or may be, reduced, or that which it comes, or may come, to be: (S, O, TA:) you say, A^aw~alotuhu , inf. n. taA^owiylN ; and ↓ taA^aw~alotuhu , inf. n. taA^aw~ulN ; in one and the same sense: and hence the saying of El-Aashà: Hub~ihaA ↓ EalaY A^an~ahaA kaAnato taA^aw~ulu riboEiY~i Als~iqaAbi faA^aSoHabaA ↓ taA^aw~ula (S:) or Hub~ahA ↓ tAw~al : (so in a copy of the T: [the former word being, accord. to this reading, a contraction of tataA^aw~alu ; but this does not altogether agree with what here follows:]) AO says, taA^aw~ulu Hub~ihaA means tafosiyruhu wamarojiEuhu : [i. e., the explanation of her love, or of the (poet's) love of her, and the state, or condition, to which it eventually came, is this:] (S:) it was small in his heart, and ceased not to grow until it became great; like as the little young camel [born in the season called rbyE , or in the beginning of the breeding-time,] ceases not to grow until he becomes great like his mother, (T, * S,) and has a son accompanying him: (S:) [or] A^w~lhu and ↓ tA^w~lhu , (M, K,) inf. n. of the former as above, (K,) when said of language, signify dab~arahu waqad~arahu wafas~arahu [ he considered its end, or what it might be to which it led or pointed, and compared one part of it with another, and then explained, or expounded, or interpreted, it ]: (M, K:) hence, [if the explanation in the M and K be meant to denote three distinct meanings, which I do not think to be the case,] it would seem as though taA^owiylN and tafosiyrN were syn.; but accord. to other authorities, they differ: (TA:) [Az says,] accord. to Ahmad Ibn-Yahyà, these two words and maEonFY are all one: but tA^wyl seems to me to signify the collecting the meanings of dubious expressions by such expression as is clear, or plain, without dubiousness: or, accord. to Lth, it is the interpreting of language that has different meanings; and this cannot be rightly done but by an explanation which changes the expression; as also ↓ tA^aw~ulN : (T:) or the turning a verse of the Kur-án from its apparent meaning to a meaning which it bears, or admits, when the latter is agreeable with the Scripture and the Sunneh: for instance, in the words of the Kur [vi. 95, &c.], yuxoriju A@loHaY~a mina Almay~iti , if the meaning be [thus explained] “He produceth the bird from the egg,” this is tfsyr : and if [it be explained as meaning] “He produceth the believer from the unbeliever,” or “the knowing from the ignorant,” this is tA^wyl : so says Ibn-El-Kemál: (TA:) [hence, although it may often be rendered by interpretation, like tfsyr , it more properly signifies the rendering in a manner not according to the letter, or overt sense; explaining the covert, or virtual, meaning; interpreting in a manner not according to the obvious meaning: ] or the reducing a thing to its ultimate intent, whether it be a saying or an action: (Er-Rághib, TA:) or tfsyr signifies the “discovering, detecting, revealing, or disclosing, what is meant by a dubious expression;” and tA^wyl , the reducing one of two senses, or interpretations, which an expression bears, or admits, to that which suits the apparent meaning: (L and K in art. fsr , and TA in that and in the present art.:) or the former signifies the “expounding, explaining, or interpreting, the narratives which occur collected without discrimination in the Kur-án, and making known the significations of the strange words or expressions, and explaining the occasions on which the verses were revealed;” and the latter, the explaining the meaning of that which is muta$aAbihi , [or what is equivocal, or ambiguous, ] i. e., what is not understood without repeated consideration. (TA: [in which are some further explanations; but these add nothing of importance.]) ― -b4- [Hence, A^w~l lafoZFA , in grammar, He rendered a word, or an expression, or a phrase, in grammatical analysis, by another word, or expression, or phrase. ] ― -b5- And [hence likewise,] taA^owiylN signifies also The interpretation, or explanation, of a dream; the telling the final sequel, or result, thereof: (M, K:) as in the Kur xii. 101. (M.) ― -b6- It is also used [as a simple subst.] to signify The end, issue, result, or final sequel, of a thing; syn. EaAqibapN ; (Bd in iv. 62 and xvii. 37;) or ↓ maA=lN ; (Jel in the same places;) or marojiEN , and maSiyrN ; as in the Kur [iii. 5], wamaA yEolamu taA^owiylahu A_il~aA A@ll~`hu [ But none knoweth the end, &c., thereof, except God ]: (A'Obeyd, T:) or this phrase means, but none knoweth when will be the resurrection, and to what the case will eventually come, (T, M,) when the hour shall arrive, (TA,) except God: (T, M:) so says Aboo-Is-hák: (T:) and in like manner, [in the Kur vii. 51,] halo yanoZuruwna A_il~aA taA^owiylahu means Do they wait for aught save the result to which their case will come by the resurrection? (Aboo-Is-hák, T, M:) or, the result to which it will come (Bd, Jel) in the manifestation of its truth by the appearance of the promises and threats of which it has told? (Bd:) in like manner, also, the saying, taqowy A@ll~`hi A^aHosanu taA^owiylFA means The fear of God is best in respect of result; syn. EaAqibapF . (TA.)

(TA: [in which are some further explanations; but these add nothing of importance.]) ― -b4- [Hence, A^w~l lafoZFA , in grammar, He rendered a word, or an expression, or a phrase, in grammatical analysis, by another word, or expression, or phrase. ] ― -b5- And [hence likewise,] taA^owiylN signifies also The interpretation, or explanation, of a dream; the telling the final sequel, or result, thereof: (M, K:) as in the Kur xii. 101. (M.) ― -b6- It is also used [as a simple subst.] to signify The end, issue, result, or final sequel, of a thing; syn. EaAqibapN ; (Bd in iv. 62 and xvii. 37;) or ↓ maA=lN ; (Jel in the same places;) or marojiEN , and maSiyrN ; as in the Kur [iii. 5], wamaA yEolamu taA^owiylahu A_il~aA A@ll~`hu [ But none knoweth the end, &c., thereof, except God ]: (A'Obeyd, T:) or this phrase means, but none knoweth when will be the resurrection, and to what the case will eventually come, (T, M,) when the hour shall arrive, (TA,) except God: (T, M:) so says Aboo-Is-hák: (T:) and in like manner, [in the Kur vii. 51,] halo yanoZuruwna A_il~aA taA^owiylahu means Do they wait for aught save the result to which their case will come by the resurrection? (Aboo-Is-hák, T, M:) or, the result to which it will come (Bd, Jel) in the manifestation of its truth by the appearance of the promises and threats of which it has told? (Bd:) in like manner, also, the saying, taqowy A@ll~`hi A^aHosanu taA^owiylFA means The fear of God is best in respect of result; syn. EaAqibapF . (TA.)

definition: A man's A^ahol [or family ];
sourceDefinition: A man's A^ahol [or family ]; (T, S, M, Msb, K;) i. e. his relations: (Msb:) his Ea$iyrap [or kinsfolk; or nearer, or nearest, relations by descent from the same father or ancestor; &c.]; from A^awolN as signifying rujuwEN , because recourse is had to them in all affairs: (Har p. 578:) and his household; (S, TA;) the people of his house: (Msb:) and his followers; (S, Msb, K;) including soldiers: (S, TA:) and his A^awoliyaA=' [i. e. friends, and the like ]: (K:) those who bear a relation to him, as members to a head, ( mano A=la A_ilayohi ,) by religion or persuasion or kindred; as in the Kur iii. 9 and viii. 54 and 56 &c.: (Ibn-'Arafeh:) [or in these and many other instances, it may be rendered people: ] but in general it is not used save in relation to that in which is eminence, or nobility; so that one does not say, A=lu AlA_isokaAfi , like as one says A^aholuhu : (K:) and it is peculiarly used as a prefix to the proper names of rational beings; not to indeterminate nouns, nor to nouns of places or of times; so that one says, A=lu fulaAnK ; but not A=lu rajulK , nor A=lu zamaAni ka*aA , nor A=lu mawoDaEi ka*aA , like as one says, [ A^aholu rajulK , and A^aholu zamaAni ka*aA , and] A^aholu baladi ka*aA and mawoDiEi ka*aA : (TA:) Ks disallows its being prefixed to a pronoun; so that one should not say, A=luhu , but A^aholuhu ; but his opinion in this matter is not correct: it is originally A^awalN ; the w being changed into A , (M, * Msb,) as in qaAla [which is originally qawala ]: so say some: (Msb:) or it is originally A^aholN , (T, M, Msb, K,) then A^aA^olN , and then A=lN : (K:) so say some, arguing thus from its having A^uhayolN for its dim.: (T, Msb:) but accord. to Ks, it assumes the form ↓ A^uwayolN as a dim.: (T:) or each of these is its dim. (M, K.) By the A=l of the Prophet are meant, accord. to some persons, His followers, whether relations or others: and his relations, whether followers or not: (Ahmad Ibn-Yahyà, T:) or, as some say, his family ( A^aholuhu [q. v.]) and his wives: [but it seems to be indicated that what I have rendered “and his wives” is meant as an explicative adjunct to Ahlh :] or, as some say, the people of his religion: (Esh-Sháfi'ee, T:) being himself asked who were his A=l , he answered all pious persons: (Anas, TA:) but in a trad. in which it is said that the poor-rates are prohibited to him and to his A=l , by this is meant those to whom was appropriated the fifth [of the spoils] instead of the poor-rates; and these were the genuine descendants of Háshim and El-Muttalib. (Esh-Sháfi'ee, T.) ― -b2- yaA lazayodK and yaAla zayodK , accord. to the Koofees, are contractions of yaA A=la zayodK [ O family of Zeyd ]. (Mughnee, on the letter l ; and El-Ashmoonee on the Alfeeyeh of Ibn-Málik, section AlAstgAvp . [See the letter l .]) ― -b3- [See also A_iylapN .] -A2- (tropical:) I. q. $axoSN [meaning The body, or corporeal form or figure or substance, (of anything, as is said in the T,) which one sees from a distance; or, in this case, often, though not always, the person, or self ]; (AA, T, S, M, K;) of a man: a metaphorical application, from A=lN as signifying A^aholN and Ea$iyrapN ; because comprising the members and the senses. (Har p. 578.) ― -b2- Sometimes, it is redundant, or pleonastic; [being only used for the sake of metre in verse, or to give more force to an expression;] as in the following instance: A^ulaAqiY mino ta*ak~uri A=li layolaY kamaA yaloqaY Als~aliymu mina AlEidaAdi [ I experience, from remembrance of Leylà, or of Leylà's person or self, the like of what the person bitten or stung by a venomous reptile experiences from the paroxysm of pain occasioned by the bits or sting ]. (TA.) [See also another ex., voce jaA^obN ; and another, voce mizomaArN .] ― -b3- [Like $axoSN , it seems to be sometimes applied to Any material thing that is somewhat high, and conspicuous: and hence, perhaps, the signification next following.] ― -b4- maA A^a$orafa mina AlbaEiyri [app. meaning The overtopping, or higher, part, or parts, of the camel ]. (M, K.) ― -b5- A [ tent of the kind called ] xayomap . (M.) ― -b6- The poles of the xayomap ; (M, K;) as also ↓ A=lapN ; of which the pl. is A=lAtN : (K:) or ↓ A=lapN is the sing. of A=lN and A=laAtN , [or n. un. of the former and pl. of the latter,] which signify the pieces of wood ( xa$abaAt ) upon which the xymp is raised, or constructed: and hence Kutheiyir likens the legs of his she-camel to four A=lAt of the [wood of the tree called] TaloH . (S.) ― -b7- The pieces of wood ( xa$ab , T, M, K) of xayom [or tents], (M,) stripped [ of the tent-cloths ]. (T, TA.) ― -b8- Also, [app. because rising from the general surface of the ground,] The extremities and sides of a mountain. (M, K. *) -A3- The saraAb [or mirage ]: (As, T, M, K:) or peculiarly applied to that which is in the first part of the day, (K,) as though raising figures seen from a distance ( $uxuwS ), and making them to quiver: (TA:) or that which one sees in the first part of the day, and in the last part thereof, as though raising figures seen from a distance ( $xwS ); not the same as the srAb : (S:) or what resembles the srAb : (Msb:) or, as some say, that which is in the DuHaY [or early part of the day when the sun is yet low ], like water between the sky and the earth, [ in appearance ] raising figures seen from a distance ( $xwS ), and making them to quiver; whereas the srAb is that which is at mid-day, [apparently] cleaving to the ground, as though it were running water: Th says, the A=l is in the first part of the day: (M:) As says that the A=l and the srAb are one: but others say that the former is from the DuHaY [see above] to the declining of the sun from the meridian; whereas the srAb is after the declining of the sun from the meridian to the prayer of the EaSor ; and in favour of their assertion they urge, that the former [ in appearance ] raises everything so that it becomes what is termed A=l , i. e. $axoS ; for the A=l of everything is its $xS ; and that the srAb [in appearance] lowers every $xS in it so that it becomes [as though it were] cleaving to the ground, having no $xS : Yoo says, the Arabs say that the A=l is from the gudowap [or period between the prayer of daybreak and sunrise ] to the time when the sun is very high, or near the meridian; then it is called srAb for the rest of the day: ISk says, the A=l is that which [ in appearance ] raises figures seen from a distance ( $xwS ), and is in the DuHaY [explained above]; and the srAb is that which is upon the surface of the ground, as though it were water, and is at midday: and this, I [namely Az] say, is what I have found the Arabs in the desert to say: (T:) El- Hareeree speaks of the glistening of the A=l ; app. using this word in the sense of srAb ; for it is the latter that glistens; not the former: (Har p. 363:) the word is masc. and fem. (Msb, K.) The phrase yarfaEu A@loA=laA , ending a verse (S, M) of En-Nábighah, (M, TA,) i. e. Edh-Dhubyánee, (TA,) or El-Jaadee, (S,) [variously cited in the S and M and TA,] is an instance of inversion; the meaning being yarofaEuhu A@loA=lu [ The A=l raising it ]: (S, TA:) or the meaning is, making the A=l conspicuous more than it would otherwise be; the agent of the verb being a prominent portion of a mountain, which, being itself raised [in appearance] by the A=l , has the effect of doing this. (M.) -A4- See also the next paragraph. -A5- And see A^alayaAnN , in art. Aly .

definition: i. q. A^adaApN [i. e. An instrument; a tool; an implement; a utensil: and instruments; tools; implements; utensils; apparatus; equipments; equipage; accoutrements; furniture; gear; tackling; ] (S, M,...
sourceDefinition: i. q. A^adaApN [i. e. An instrument; a tool; an implement; a utensil: and instruments; tools; implements; utensils; apparatus; equipments; equipage; accoutrements; furniture; gear; tackling; ] (S, M, K) with which one works, for himself or for another: it is both sing. and pl.: (M, K:) or, (K,) as some say, (M,) it is a pl. having no sing. (M, K) as to the letter: (M:) [but it is very often used as a sing.:] and the pl. is A=laAtN . (S, K.) In the saying of 'Alee, yasotaEomilu A=lapa Ald~iyni fiY Talabi Ald~unyaA [lit. He makes use of the instrument of religion in seeking the goods of the present world ], (assumed tropical:) science, or knowledge, is meant; because thereby only is religion. (M.) ― -b2- [ A musical instrument; ] a lute; a musical reed, or pipe; the [ kind of mandoline called ] Tunobuwr . (TA.) ― -b3- The male organ of generation. (TA.) ― -b4- The bier of a corpse. (Abu-l-'Omeythil, S, M, K.) Thus, accord. to some, in the following verse, (S, * M,) of Kaab Ibn-Zuheyr: kul~u A@boni A^unovaY waA_ino TaAlto salaAmatuhu yawomFA EalaY A=lapK HadobaA='a maHomuwlu [ Every son of a female, though his health, or safety, long continue, is one day borne upon a gibbous bier: for the bier of the Arabs of the desert was generally composed of two poles connected by a net-work of cords upon which the corpse lay depressed]: (S, M:) or, as some say, [ in a distressing state, or condition; for, they say,] A=lap here signifies Halap . (TA.) ― -b5- See also A=lN , in two places, near the middle of the paragraph. -A2- A state, or condition; i. q. HaAlapN [as mentioned above]: (T, S, M, K:) pl. [or rather coll. gen. n.] ↓ A=lN . (T, S.) You say, huwabiA=lpi sawo'K [ He is in an evil state or condition ]. (S.) ― -b2- I. q. $i*~apN [ Straitness; difficulty; distress; &c.]. (M, K.)

definition: [act. part. n. of 1 in all its senses: and thus, particularly,] Thickening, or thick; (T, S, M, TA;) applied to the urine of camels that have been contented with green pasture instead of water, at...
sourceDefinition: [act. part. n. of 1 in all its senses: and thus, particularly,] Thickening, or thick; (T, S, M, TA;) applied to the urine of camels that have been contented with green pasture instead of water, at the end of their being in that state; (T;) or to milk, (S, M, TA,) and to oil, and other things, such as tar, and honey, and wine, or beverage: (TA:) pl. ↓ A^uy~alN : (S, M:) which last word [in one copy of the M written A_iylN , but this I think a mistranscription,] signifies also the remains of thickening, or thick, milk; or, as some say, the [ seminal ] water in the womb: (M:) or this same word ( A^uy~alN ) has the last of these significations; and also, [as a sing. epithet,] the first of the meanings explained in this paragraph; as also A=y^ilN , applied to milk; (K;) or to milk thickening, or thick, and mixed; not excessively thick, but in a somewhat good degree, and changed in its flavour: (AHát, TA:) or it [app. A^uy~alN , as in the TK,] signifies the vessel, or receptacle, thereof; (K;) [a meaning assigned in the M to A_iyaAlN ;] in which milk thickens: (TA:) Sh says that ↓ A_iy~alN signifies the milk of the A^ayaAy^il [pl. of A_iy~alN ]; and so says AA: but AHeyth says that this is absurd; and that the right word is ↓ A^uy~alN , having the signification first explained in this paragraph, i. e. thickening, or thick, milk: En-Nadr says that ↓ A_iy~alN signifies thick urine of she-goats of the mountain; which, when drunk by a woman, excites her venereal faculty: (T:) or this last word is used to signify milk of an A_iy~al , which is said to strengthen in the venereal faculty, and to fatten, as Ibn-Habeeb asserts; and ↓ A^uy~alN , which he affirms to be wrong, is a dial. var. thereof; and it may also be a quasi-pl. n. thereof: (M:) as a pl. [of A=y^ilN ], applied to milk, ↓ A=uy~alN is extr. in two respects; as a pl., of this form, of an epithet not applied to an animal; and as being regularly A^uw~alN . (IJ, M.) -A2- A_in~ahu laA=y^ilu maAlK and maAlK ↓ A^ay~ilu Verily he is a good manager, or tender, of cattle, or camels, or the like. (M, TA.)

definition: An evidence, or a proof: (T, S, Msb, K, and Ham p.
sourceDefinition: An evidence, or a proof: (T, S, Msb, K, and Ham p. 7:) and a demonstration; i. e. the manifestation of an evidence or proof: (Msb:) or a decisive and manifest evidence or proof: (TA:) or the firmest, strongest, or most valid, evidence or proof; which is such as ever necessarily implies truth, or veracity, as its consequence, or concomitant; for evidences, or proofs, are of five sorts; whereof this is one; another is that which ever necessarily implies falsity, or falsehood, as its consequence, or concomitant; another, that which is nearer to truth, or veracity; another, that which is nearer to falsity, or falsehood; and another, that which is intermediate between these two: (Er-Rághib, TA:) [pl. baraAhiynu :] some say that the n in this word is augmentative; (Msb, and Ham p. 7;) that it is of the measure fuEolaAnN , from Albrh [app. Albarohu ] signifying the “act of cutting:” (Ham ubi suprà:) others, that it is radical: Az mentions both of these opinions: J confines himself to the latter opinion: Z, to the former, saying, on the authority of IAar, that the word is derived from barahorahapN , meaning “white,” [or “fair in complexion,”] applied to a girl: (Msb:) Abu-l-Fet-h [i. e. IJ] says that he holds it to be of the measure fuEolaAlN , like quroTaAsN and quronaAsN , the n not being augmentative, as is shown by the verb above mentioned: (Ham ubi suprà:) but [it has been stated above that] this verb is said, on the authority of IAar, to be post-classical. (Msb, TA.)

sourceDefinition: [inf. n. of bazaga ] signifies The beginning to rise, or come forth: this is the primary meaning: mentioned by Zj. (TA.) ― -b2- Hence, (TA,) bazaga , said of a tush, or tusk, or canine tooth, (A,) or of the tush of a camel, (S, Msb, K,) [aor. ,] inf. n. buzuwgN , (Msb,) It came forth; (S, Msb, K;) it clave the flesh, and came forth. (A.) ― -b3- And hence, (A, TA,) bazagati Al$~amosu , (JK, S, A, Msb, K,) aor. , (TK,) inf. n. as above (JK, S, K) and bazogN , (K,) The sun began to rise; (JK, TA;) as though it clave the darkness with its light: (A, TA:) or rose, (S, Msb, K,) with spreading light: (TA:) or buzuwgN has the meaning first explained above; the beginning to rise, or come forth. (K.) And in like manner one says, bazaga Alqamaru [ The moon began to rise: or rose ]. (A, TA.) -A2- bazaga , (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) aor. , (Msb,) inf. n. bazogN , (JK, Msb,) He (a cupper, and a farrier,) scarified, (S, Msb, K,) and made the blood to flow: (Msb:) he (a farrier) scarified a beast (JK, Mgh, TA) in its A^a$oEar [or part next the hoof (in the TA, erroneously, $Er )], (JK,) with a mibozaE (JK, Mgh, TA) of iron; (JK;) as also ↓ bz~g , inf. n. taboziygN : (JK, * TA:) Aboo- 'Adnán says that taboziygN and taEoriybN signify the same, namely, the making a slight incision, or stab, such as does not reach the sinews, or tendons. (TA.) ― -b2- And He made his blood to flow. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: (inf. n. of basala , M) is The act of preventing, hindering, withholding, debarring, forbidding, or prohibiting; syn. manoEN ; the primary meaning; (Bd in vi. 69;) and A_iEojaAlN (M, K) and HabosN ; (AA, K;) [both syn. with manoEN ;] and ↓ A_ibosaAlN [inf. n. of 4, q. v. infrà,] signifies the same. (Bd ubi suprà.) You say, basalaniy Eano HaAjatiY , inf. n. as above, He prevented me from accomplishing my want; syn. A^aEojalaniY . (M.) -A2- basala , (M, K,) aor. , (M,) inf. n. busuwlN , He (a man, TA) frowned, contracted his face, or looked sternly or austerely or morosely; or, doing so, grinned, or displayed his teeth; or contracted the part between his eyes; ( Eabasa ;) by reason of courage, or of anger; as also ↓ tbs~l : (M, K:) and [so in the M, but in the K “or” ] ↓ tbs~l wajohuhu , (M, and so in some copies of the K,) or ↓ tbs~l [alone], (so in other copies of the K, and in the TA,) His face, or he, was, or became, odious, and excessively foul or unseemly or hideous, in aspect: (M, K:) and liY ↓ tbs~l He (a man) was displeasing, or odious, in aspect to me. (TA.) ― -b2- And [hence], (M, K,) inf. n. busuwlN , (TA,) said of milk, and of nabiy* [or must &c.], (tropical:) It was, or became, strong: (K: [in the CK, bas~ala is here erroneously put for basala ; and wabas~alahu , which should next follow, is omitted:]) or, said of the former, it was, or became, displeasing, or odious, in taste, and sour; and, said of the latter, it was, or became, strong, and sour. (M, TA.) Also, said of vinegar, (assumed tropical:) It, having been left long, became altered, or corrupted, in flavour. (Az in art. H*q , TA.) And, said of flesh-meat, (assumed tropical:) It stank, or became stinking. (AHn, M, TA.) -A3- bisula , [aor. ,] inf. n. basaAlapN (S, M, Msb, K) and basaAlN , [respecting which latter see what follows in the next sentence,] (M, K,) He was, or became, courageous, or strong-hearted, on the occasion of war, or fight: (S, M, Msb, K:) from basolN meaning “forbidden,” or “prohibited;” because he who has this quality defends himself from his antagonist, as though it were forbidden to him [the latter] to do him a displeasing, or an evil, deed. (Ham p. 13.) El-Hoteíah says, waA^aHolaY mina Alt~amori AljaniY~i wa fiyhimu basaAlapu nafosK A_ino A^uriyda basaAluhaA [ And sweeter than fresh-gathered dates, and in them is courageousness of soul, if courageousness thereof be desired ]: but bsAlhA may be here altered by curtailment from basaAlanuhaA . (M.) You say, maA A^aboyana basaAlatahu [ How manifest is ] his courage! (TA.) ― -b2- See also 4.

sourceDefinition: [inf. n. of Absl ] i. q. basolN as explained in the first sentence of this art. ; i. e., The act of preventing, hindering, withholding, debarring, (Bd in vi. 69,] forbidding, or prohibiting. (S, K, and Bd ubi suprà.) -A2- Abslhu (inf. n. as above, TA) He pledged, or gave in pledge, him, or it, (M, Msb, K,) lika*aA [and bika*aA , as will be shown below, both meaning for such a thing ]: and he gave in exchange, or as an equivalent, him, or it, lika*aA [and app. bika*aA also, as above, for such a thing ]; syn. Ear~aDahu : (M, K:) and he gave him up, delivered him, delivered him over, or consigned him, to destruction, (S, K,) or to punishment. (Az, TA.) 'Owf Ibn-El-Ahwas says, waA_ibosaAliy baniY~a bigayorijuromK baEawonaAhu wa laA bidamK muraAqi [ And my giving in pledge, or as an equivalent, or giving up to destruction, my sons, not for a crime that we have committed, nor for blood that has been shed by us]: (S, M, TA:) for he had given his sons in pledge for others, seeking peace, or reconciliation. (S, TA.) A^ano tubosala bimaA kasabato , in the Kur [vi. 69], means Lest a soul should be given up, or delivered, &c., (AO, S, Bd, Jel, TA.) to destruction, (Bd, Jel, TA,) or to punishment, (Az, TA,) for that which it hath done, (Az, Bd, Jel, TA,) of evil: (Bd:) or be given in pledge. (Bd, TA.) (TA [app. from ISd].)

(TA in art. gmr .) ― -b3- [Hence also,] bal~a raHimahu , (T, S, M, K,) aor. , (T, M,) inf. n. bal~N (with fet-h, TA [in the CK it has kesr]) and bilaAlN , (M, K,) (tropical:) He made close [or he refreshed ] his ties of relationship by behaving with goodness and affection and gentleness to his kindred; syn. waSalahaA , (T, S, M, K,) and nad~aAhaA : (T:) for, as some things are conjoined and commixed by moisture, and become disunited by dryness, bal~N is metaphorically used to denote conjunction, as above, and yubosN to denote the contrary. (TA.) A poet says, waAlr~iHoma fA@bolulohaA bixayori Albul~aAno faA_inahaAA@$otuq~ato mini A@somi Alr~aHom`no [(tropical:) And the ties of relationship, make thou them close &c. by the best mode, or modes, of doing so; for the name thereof is derived from the name of the Compassionate ]: here ↓ Albul~aAn may be a noun in the sing. number, like guforaAnN , or it may be pl. of balalN , which may be either a subst. or an. inf. n., for some inf. ns. have pls., as $ugolN and EaqolN and maraDN . (M.) And it is said in a trad., bul~uwA A^aroHaAmakumo walawo biAls~alaAmi (tropical:) Make ye close [or refresh ye ] your ties of relationship &c., though but, or if only, by salutation; syn. SiluwhaA , (M,) or nad~uwhaA biAlS~ilapi . (S.) definition: is a particle of digression: (Mughnee, K:) or, accord.
sourceDefinition: is a particle of digression: (Mughnee, K:) or, accord. to Mbr, it denotes emendation, wherever it occurs, in the case of a negation or an affirmation: (T, TA:) or it is a word of emendation, and denoting digression from that which precedes; as also bano , in which the n is a substitute for the l , because bl is of frequent occurrence, and bn is rare; or, as IJ says, the latter may be an independent dial. var. (M.) When it is followed by a proposition, the meaning of the digression is either the cancelling of what precedes, as in waqaAluwA A@t~axa*a A@lr~aHom`nu waladFA suboHaAnahu balo EibaAdN mukoramuwna [ And they said, “ The Compassionate hath gotten offspring: ” extolled be his freedom from that which is derogatory from his glory! nay, or nay rather, or nay but, they are honoured servants (Kur xxi. 26)], or transition from one object of discourse to another, as in qado A^afolaHa mano tazak~aY wa *akara A@soma rab~ihi faSal~aY balo tuw^oviruwna A@loHayaApa A@ld~unoyaA [ He hath attained felicity who hath purified himself, and celebrated the name of his Lord, and prayed: but ye prefer the present life (Kur lxxxvii. 14-16)]: (Mughnee, K: *) and in all such cases it is an inceptive particle; not a conjunctive. (Mughnee.) When it is followed by a single word, it is a conjunction, (S, * Msb, * Mughnee, K,) and requires that word to be in the same case as the word before it: (S:) and if preceded by a command or an affirmation, (Mughnee, K,) as in AiDorabo zayodFA balo EamorFA [ Beat thou Zeyd: no, 'Amr ], (Msb, Mughnee, K,) and qaAma zayodN balo EamorNw [ Zeyd stood: no, 'Amr ], (M, Mughnee, K,) or jaA='aniY A^axuwka balo A^abuwka [ Thy brother came to me: no, thy father ], (S,) it makes what precedes it to be as though nothing were said respecting it, (S, * Msb, * Mughnee, K,) making the command or affirmation to relate to what follows it: (S, * Msb, * Mughnee:) [and similar to these cases is the case in which it is preceded by an interrogation: see A^amo as syn. with this particle:] but when it is preceded by a negation or a prohibition, it is used to confirm the meaning of what precedes it and to assign the contrary of that meaning to what follows it, (Mughnee, K,) as in maA qaAma zayodN EamorNw [ Zeyd stood not, but 'Amr stood ], (Mughnee,) or maA raA^ayotu zayodFA balo EamorFA , [ I saw not Zeyd, but I saw 'Amr ], (S,) and laA yaqumo zayodN balo EamorNw [ Let not Zeyd stand, but let 'Amr stand]. (Mughnee.) Mbr and 'Abd-El-Wárith allow its being used to transfer the meaning of the negation and the prohibition to what follows it; so that, accord. to them, one may say, maAzayodN qaAy^imFA balo qaAEidFA [as meaning Zeyd is not standing: no, is not sitting ], and balo qaAEidN [ but is sitting ]; the meaning being different [in the two cases]. (Mughnee, K. *) The Koofees disallow its being used as a conjunction after anything but a negation [so in the Mughnee, but in the K a prohibition,] or the like thereof; so that one should not say, Darabotu zayodFA balo A_iy~aAka [ I beat Zeyd: no, thee ]. (Mughnee, K.) Sometimes laA is added before it, to corroborate the meaning of digression, after an affirmation, as in the saying, wajohuka Albadoru laA bali Al$~amosu lawo lamo yuqoDa lil$~amosi kasofapN wa A^ufuwlu [ Thy face is the full moon: no, but it would be the sun, were it not that eclipse and setting are appointed to happen to the sun ]: and to corroborate what precedes it, after a negation, as in wa maA hajarotuka laA balo zaAdaniY $agafFA hajorN wa baEodN taraAxaY laA A_ilaY A^ajali [ And I did not abandon thee, or have not abandoned thee: no, but abandonment and distance, protracted, not to an appointed period, increased, or have increased, my heart-felt love ]. (Mughnee, K. *) ― -b2- Sometimes it is used to denote the passing from one subject to another without cancelling [what precedes it], and is syn. with wa , as in the saying in the Kur [lxxxv. 20 and 21], waA@ll~`hu mino , wa raAy^ihimo muHiyTN balo huwa quroA=nN majiydN [ And God from behind them is encompassing: and it is a glorious Kur-án: or here it may mean A_in~a , as in an ex. below]: and to this meaning it is made to accord in the saying, lahu EalaY~a diynaArN balo dirohamN [ I owe him a deenár and a dirhem ]. (Msb.) ― -b3- In the fol- lowing saying in the Kur [xxxviii. 1], waA@loquroA=ni *iY A@l*~ikoribali A@l~a*iyna kafaruwA fiY Eiz~apK wa$iqaAqK , it is said to signify A_in~a ; [so that the meaning is, By the Kur-án possessed of eminence, verily they who have disbelieved are in a state of pride and opposition; ] therefore the oath applies to it. (Akh, S.) ― -b4- Sometimes the Arabs use it in breaking off a saying and commencing another; and thus a man commences with it a citation, or recitation, of verse; in which case, it does not form any part of the first verse, but is a sign of the breaking off, or ending, of what precedes. (Akh, S.) ― -b5- Sometimes it is put in the place of rub~a , (S, Mughnee,) as in the saying of the rájiz, balo mahomahK qaTaEotu baEoda mahomahK [ Many a far-extending desert have I traversed, after a far-extending desert ]. (S: [and a similar ex. is given in the Mughnee.]) ― -b6- What is deficient in this word [supposing it to be originally of three letters] is unknown; and so in the cases of halo and qado : it may be a final w or Y or they may be originally bal~ and hal~ and qad~ . (Akh, S.)
