definition: Strength; [app. in a camel, such as renders fit for the saddle, or for journeying; ] and fleetness, or swiftness, and excellence: (TA:) [and ↓ riHolapN has a similar meaning, as appears from what...
sourceDefinition: Strength; [app. in a camel, such as renders fit for the saddle, or for journeying; ] and fleetness, or swiftness, and excellence: (TA:) [and ↓ riHolapN has a similar meaning, as appears from what follows:] or excellence of pace of a camel. (S voce HiDaArN .) You say baEiyrN *uw ruHolapK and ↓ riHolapK , and ↓ miroHalN , like minobarN , (K,) or ↓ muroHilN , and ↓ raHiylN , so in the T, (TA,) A strong he-camel: (T, K:) and (so in the K [but properly “ or ”]) bEyr *w ruHolapK (CK) or ↓ riHolapK (K accord. to the TA) or both, and ↓ miroHalN , with kesr to the m (O,) and ↓ jamalN raHiylN , (AA, S, S, O, K, TA,) and ↓ naAqapN raHiylapN (S, O) or raHiylN , (TA,) and *aAtu ruHolapK , (S,) a he-camel, (S, O, K,) and a she-camel, (S, O,) strong to journey; (S, O, K, TA;) so says Fr: (O:) or strong to be saddled: (TA:) and ↓ naAqapN raHiylapN and raHiylN and ↓ muroHilapN , accord. to the “ Nawádir el-Aaráb, ” a she-camel that is excellent, generous, of high breed; or strong, light, and swift; (TA;) and so ↓ musotaroHilapN . (K, TA. [See also raAHilapN .]) ― -b2- See also the next paragraph, in seven places.

definition: The act of saddling of camels: (K, * TA:) [and also, agreeably with analogy, a mode, or manner, of saddling of camels:] so in the saying, A_in~ahu laHasanu Alr~iHolapi [ Verily he is good in respect...
sourceDefinition: The act of saddling of camels: (K, * TA:) [and also, agreeably with analogy, a mode, or manner, of saddling of camels:] so in the saying, A_in~ahu laHasanu Alr~iHolapi [ Verily he is good in respect of the saddling, or the mode or manner of saddling, of camels]. (K.) ― -b2- Also A removal, departure, or journey; (AZ, S, Msb, K;) and so ↓ ruHolapN , (Lh, Msb, K,) and ↓ raHiylN : (S, K: [the last said in the Msb to be and inf. n.:]) you say danato riHolatunaA (S) or qarubato riHolatunaA (Msb) [ Our removal, &c., drew near, or has drawn near ]: and A_in~ahu la*uw riHolapK A_ilaY Almuluwki and ↓ riHolap Verily he is one who journeys, or has journeyed, to the kings: (Lh, TA:) and in like manner ruHolapN is used in the Kur cvi. 2: (TA:) ― -b3- or ↓ riHolapN with damm, (S, Msb, K,) signifies The thing to which one removes, departs, or journeys; (AZ, Msb;) or the direction, or point, or object, to which one desires to repair, or betakes himself: (AA, S, Msb, K:) and also, (K,) or ruHolapN , (TA,) a single journey; (K, TA;) as ISd says: (TA:) you say, ↓ mak~apu ruHolatiY Mekkeh is the point, or object, to which I desire to remove, or depart, or journey: (TA:) and ↓ A^anotumo ruHolatiY Ye are they to whom I remove, or depart, or journey: (S, TA:) and ↓ A^anota ruHolatunaA Thou art the object to which we repair, or betake ourselves. (Msb.) And hence ↓ ruHolapN is applied to signify A noble, or an exalted, person, or a great man of learning, to whom one journeys for his [ the latter's ] need, or want, or for his [ the former's ] science. (TA.) ― -b4- See also the next preceding paragraph, in three places.

definition: A saroj [or horse's saddle ]: (K:) or a saroj of skins, (S, M, Msb, K,) in which is no wood;
sourceDefinition: A saroj [or horse's saddle ]: (K:) or a saroj of skins, (S, M, Msb, K,) in which is no wood; used for vehement running [ of the horse ]: (S, M, K:) ISd says also that it is one of the vehicles [or saddles ] of women, like the raHol : but Az says that it is one of the vehicles [or saddles ] of men, exclusively of women, i. e. not of women; as is also the raHol : and some say that it is larger than the saroj , covered with skins, and is for horses, and for excellent, or strong and light and swift, camels: (TA:) pl. raHaAy^ilu . (S.) When a man is hasty in doing evil to his companion, one says to him, Aisotaqodamato riHaAlatuka [lit. Thy saddle has got before thee, or shifted forwards ]: (S in the present art.:) it is a prov., meaning that has preceded than which another was more fit to do so. (S in art. qdm .) definition: A she-camel that is fit to be saddled;
sourceDefinition: A she-camel that is fit to be saddled; (S, Msb, K;) thus some say; (Msb;) as also ↓ raHuwlN (S, K) and ↓ raHuwlapN : (K:) or [generally a saddle-camel, or] a camel that is ridden, male or female: (S, Msb:) accord. to IKt, a she-camel that is strong to journey and to bear burdens; and such as a man chooses for his riding and his saddle on account of excellence, or generousness, or high breed, or of strength and lightness and swiftness, and of perfectness of make, and beauty of aspect: but this explanation is wrong: (Az, TA:) it signifies a he-camel, and a she-camel, that is excellent, or generous, or high-bred, or strong and light and swift: (Az, Mgh, TA:) the she-camel is not more entitled to this appellation than the he-camel: (Az, TA:) the p is added to give intensiveness to the signification; as in daAhiyapN and baAqiEapN and Eal~aAmapN , epithets applied to a man: or, as some say, the she-camel is so called because she is saddled; and it is like Eiy$apN raADiyapN meaning maroDiy~apN , and maA='N daAfiqN meaning madofuwqN : or, as others say, because she is *aAtu raHolK [ one having a saddle ]; and in like manner, Eiy$apN raADiyapN means *aAtu raDFY , and maA='N daAfiqN means *uw dafoqK : (TA:) the pl. is rawaAHilu . (S, Msb.) It is said in a trad., tajiduwna Aln~aAsa baEodiY kaA_ibilK miAy^apK layosa fiyhaA raAHilapN [ Thou wilt find the people, or mankind, after me, like a hundred camels among which there is not a rAHlp ]: (Mgh, * TA:) because the rAHlo among a herd of camels is conspicuous and known. (TA.) ― -b2- ma$ato rawaAHiliY , a phrase used by the poet Dukeyn, means (tropical:) I have become hoary and weak: or, as some say, I have forsaken my ignorant, or foolish, behaviour, and have restrained myself from foul conduct, and become obedient to my censurers; like as the rAHlp obeys her chider, and goes. (TA.)

definition: (tropical:) A horse white in the back;
sourceDefinition: (tropical:) A horse white in the back; (S, Mgh, K;) because it is the place of the raHol [or rather of the riHaAlap ]; (Mgh, TA;) the whiteness not reaching to the belly nor to the rump nor to the neck: (TA:) and a sheep or goat black in the back: accord. to Abu-l-Ghowth, the fem., raHolaA='u , applied to a mare, has the former meaning only: (S:) but $aApN raHolaA='u means a sheep or goat, or a ewe or she-goat, white in the back, and black in the other parts; and likewise black in the back, and white in the other parts: (S, K: *) so says Abu-l-Ghowth: (S:) and it is also explained as meaning black, but white in the place of the saddle, from the hinder parts of the shoulderblades: also as meaning white, but black in the back: Az adds that such as is white in one of the hind legs is termed rajolaA='u [with jym ]. (TA.)

It is said in a trad., mini A@qotiraAba Als~aAEapi A^ano yakuwna AlfaYo'u rifodFA [One of the signs] of the approach of the hour of resurrection shall be, that the tribute shall be a gratuity bestowed according to men's natural desires, and not according to right, or desert. definition: [ A kind of pad, or stuffed thing, beneath a saddle;
sourceDefinition: [ A kind of pad, or stuffed thing, beneath a saddle; ] a thing like the jadoyap of a horse's saddle, (S, Mgh, K,) for a beast: (K:) a support for the saddle of a horse or camel &c.: (M, L:) it is put beneath a horse's saddle in order that it may become raised thereby. (Lth, T.) ― -b2- A piece of rag with which a wound, (S, K,) &c., (S,) is furnished as a compress ( yurofadu bihaA ). (S, K.) ― -b3- A contribution which the tribe of Kureysh made among themselves in the Time of Ignorance, for the purpose of purchasing for the pilgrims wheat, and raisins (S, M, K) for [ the beverage called ] nabiy* : (S, M:) each gave according to his ability, and thus they collected a great sum, in the days of the assembling of the pilgrims; and they continued to feed the people until the end of those days: (M:) the rifaAdap and siqaAyap [i. e. the supplying these provisions and this beverage] pertained to the Benoo-Háshim; and the sidaAnap [or service of the Kaabeh], and the liwaA=' [or banner], to the Benoo-'Abd-ed-Dár: (S:) the term rifaAdapN used in relation to the feeding of the pilgrims is from rafadahu signifying “ he aided him by a gift ” &c.: (Mgh:) the first who performed this custom was Háshim Ibn-'Abd-Menáf. (T.) ― -b4- One says also, huwa rifaAdapu SidoqK liY and SidoqK ↓ rafiydapu , meaning (tropical:) [ He is an excellent ] aider, or helper, or assistant, to me. (A.)

sourceDefinition: , (M, A,) inf. n. taromiydN , (S,) He put ashes into it, (M, * A,) or upon it; (M;) namely, roast meat: (M, A:) or he put it (a thing) into ashes. (S.) It is said in a prov., $awaY A^axuwka Hat~aY A_i*aA A^anoDaja ram~ada [ Thy brother roasted, until, when he had thoroughly cooked the meat, he put ashes into it, or put it into the ashes ]: (T, S, M, A:) meaning (tropical:) Thy brother did a good deed and then marred it: (A:) [i. e.] it is applied to him who mars, or corrupts, that which he has put into a good, or right, state: (T:) or to him who does a kind act, and then mars it by reproach, or cuts it short. (IAth.) ― -b2- Also He put it (namely, flesh-meat to be roasted,) into live coals. (M.) ― -b3- See also 1. -A2- ram~adato , (AZ, T, S, M, K,) inf. n. taromiydN ; (S) and ↓ Armdt ; (S, K;) said of a ewe, or she-goat, (AZ, T, S, M,) and of a she-camel, (S, M, K,) and of a cow, (S,) She secreted milk in her udder a little before her bringing forth; syn. A^aDoraEato : (S, K:) or she showed herself to be pregnant, and became large in her udder; as also A^aDoraEato : (AZ, T:) or she secreted a little milk at the time of bringing forth: (T:) or she showed herself to be pregnant, and became large in her belly and swollen in her udder and her vulva: or she secreted somewhat [ of milk ] at the time of bringing forth, or a little before it: the epithet applied to her in this case is ↓ muram~idN [without p ]. (M.) [See also rab~adato .] One says, ram~adati AlD~aA^onu farab~iqo rab~iqo [ The ewes have secreted milk in their udders, &c.]: (I Aar, T, S:) therefore prepare thou the A^arobaAq : prepare thou the ArbAq : [i. e., the loops into which their heads are to be inserted: ] for the ewes secrete milk in their udders only EalaY raA^osi Alwaladi [i. e. at the time of bringing forth, or when about to produce the young]. (S.) And [in like manner,] ram~adati AlmiEozaY faran~iqo ran~iq . (IAar, T. [See also arts. rmq and rnq .])

definition: Ashes; i. e. charcoal reduced to particles T, M) by being burnt; (T;) burnt coals that have become mixed with dust, and extinguished, and reduced to particles: (M:) and ↓ rimodidaA='u signifies the...
sourceDefinition: Ashes; i. e. charcoal reduced to particles T, M) by being burnt; (T;) burnt coals that have become mixed with dust, and extinguished, and reduced to particles: (M:) and ↓ rimodidaA='u signifies the same; (S, M, K;) as also ↓ A^aromidaA='u , like A^arobiEaA='u , (so in some copies of the K, and in a copy of the S,) or ↓ A^aromadaA='u , like A^arobaEaA='u , (so in other copies of the K,) or ↓ A_iromidA='u ; (so in two copies of the S, there said to be like A_irobiEaA='u , and so in the M;) as some say; or ↓ A^aromidaA='u is a pl. of ramaAdN , as is also A^aromdapN ; and ↓ A_iromidaA='u , which is mentioned on the authority of Kr, and which is [said to be] the only word of its measure, [though A_irobiEaA='u also is mentioned by IHsh,] is a quasi-pl. n.: (M:) [ ramaAdN is a coll. gen. n.;] and ↓ ramaAdapN [is its n. un., and as such] signifies a portion thereof. (M.) [Hence] one says, fulaAnN kaviyru ramaAdu Alqidori [lit. Such a one has many ashes of the cooking-pot ]; meaning (assumed tropical:) such a one is very hospitable; has many guests: (Mgh in art. ErD :) [and so huwa kaviyru Alr~amaAdi :] and huwa EaZiymu Alr~amaAdi (assumed tropical:) he has many guests: because the ashes become much in quantity in consequence of cooking. (L, from a trad.) And sufiYa Alr~amaAdu fiY wajohihi [lit. Ashes were blown and scattered in his face ]; meaning (tropical:) his face became altered. (A, TA.) ― -b2- [ maA='u Alr~amaAdi is a term applied in the present day to Lixivium, or lye; i. e. water infused with wood-ashes. ]

definition: Perdition, destruction, or a state of destruction;
sourceDefinition: Perdition, destruction, or a state of destruction; (S, Msb;) as also ↓ ramodN (T, S.) Hence, (S Msb,) EaAmu Alr~amaAdapi The year of perdition or destruction, (S, Msb. K,) or of drought, (A,) in the days of 'Omar, (S, Msb, K,) the seventeenth or eighteenth year of the Flight, (TA,) in which men perished (S, M, Msb, K) in great numbers, (M,) and cattle also, (S, K,) in consequence of drought (S, Msb) long con- tinuing, (S,) wherefore it was thus called, (S, M,) because the earth became like ashes by reason of the drought; (Msb;) or, as some say, because the drought continued so as to render the earth and the trees like the colour of ashes: but the first reason assigned above, for its being thus called, is preferable. (M.) ― -b2- See also ramaAdN .

definition: , (IAar, Az, S, Msb, K, *) aor.
sourceDefinition: , (IAar, Az, S, Msb, K, *) aor. yaruwEu (Mgh,) inf. n. rawoEN (Msb, TA) and ruwEN and ruwuwEN and ruw^uwEN , (IAar, TA,) [ He, or it, affected his ruwE , i. e. heart, or mind, with fright, or fear; ] fear of it (namely an affair or event) reached his ruwE ; (Az, TA;) he, or it, (a man, S, or an affair or event, IAar, TA, or a thing, Msb,) frightened him; put him in fear; made him afraid; (S, Mgh, Msb, K;) as also ↓ rw~Ehu , (S, Msb, K, *) inf. n. tarowiyEN : (TA:) or its beauty and abundance or multitude frightened him: (Lth, TA:) and ↓ the latter also, it frightened him by its abundance or multitude, or its beauty. (TA.) Hence the saying, in a trad., A_i*aA $amiTa lA_inosaAnu fiY EaAriDayohi fa*`lika Alr~awoEu , as though meaning [ When the man becomes grizzled in the hair of the two sides of his face, that is ] the warning of death. (TA.) You say also, [using the pass. form,] riyEa , aor. yuraAEu , (TA,) inf. n. rawoEN , (S, K,) He was, or became, frightened, or afraid; or he feared; (S, * K, * TA;) as also ↓ ArtAE , and ↓ trw~E . (S, K, TA.) And raAEa minohu , aor. yaruwEu , inf. n. rawoEN , He was, or became, frightened at it, or afraid of it; or he feared it. (TK. [But I know of no authority on which this is founded, except a prov. (cited in art. jEr ) , in which some read ruwEiY jaEaAri instead of ruwgiY .]) To a man, you say, laA turaEo [ Be not thou frightened; ] fear not thou; let not fear overtake thee: and to a woman, laA turaAEiY . (S, TA.) And hence the saying, in a trad., lano turaAEawoA maA raA^ayonaA mino $aYo'K [ Ye shall not be frightened, or afraid: we saw not, or have not seen, anything ]. (TA.) You also say, minohu ↓ ArtAE and lahu He was, or became, frightened at, or afraid of, him, or it; or he feared him, or it. (TA.) ― -b2- (tropical:) [ It affected his ruwE , i. e. heart, or mind, with a sudden surprise; it took him by surprise. ] One says, maA raAEaniY A_il~aA majiyw^uka meaning (tropical:) [ Nothing took me by surprise but thy coming; i. e. I was surprised by thy coming; or] I knew not save thy coming; as though he said, nothing struck my ruwE but thy coming. (TA.) And xarajotu wa maA raAEaniY A_il~aA fulaAnN liAlbaAbi (assumed tropical:) [ I went forth, and nothing took me by surprise but such a one at the door ]; which is equivalent to saying, and lo, such a one was at the door. (Har p. 207.) And it is said in a trad. of I'Ab, falamo yaruEoniY A_il~aA rajulN A=xi*N bimanokibiY , i. e. I knew not [ save a man taking hold of, or seizing, my shoulder-joint ]; as though he came upon him suddenly, or unexpectedly, without any previous appointment, and without knowledge, and so that event frightened him. (TA.) ― -b3- [ It affected his ruwE , i. e. heart, or mind, with admiration, or pleasure; ] it excited his admiration and approval; it pleased him, or rejoiced him; (S, Msb, K;) said of beauty [&c.]. (Msb.) It is said in a trad., describing the people of Paradise, fayaruwEuhu maA Ealayohi mina All~ibaAsi And what is upon him, of apparel, excites his admiration &c., by its beauty. (TA.) ― -b4- [ It (drink) cooled it, (namely, the heart,) or allayed its thirst. ] A poet says, saqatoniY $arobapF raAEato fuw^aAdiY saqaAhaA A@ll~`hu mino HawoDi Alr~asuwli [ She gave me to drink a draught that cooled, or allayed the thirst of, my heart: may God give her to drink from the pool of the Apostle in Paradise]. (TA.) You say also, h`*ihi $arobapN raAEa bihaA fuw^aAdiY [which may be rendered This is a draught by which he has cooled, or allayed the thirst of, my heart; and it is implied in the TA that this is the right meaning: or it means] this is a draught by which the thirst, or vehement thirst, of my heart has been allayed: (so accord. to the pointing in the copies of the K:) mentioned by Az. (TA.) -A2- The verb from rawaEN [q. v. infrà] is one and the same [whether trans. or intrans.; i. e., you say raAEahu , aor. yaruwEu , inf. n. rawoEN , meaning “He,” or “it, excited his admiration and approval,” &c., as expl. above; and raAEa , app. with the same aor. and inf. n., meaning He possessed the quality of exciting admiration and approval by his beauty and the pleasingness of his aspect, or by his courage, &c.; and in like manner, raAEato , said of a woman]; the trans. verb [in this case] being like the trans. [in other cases], and the intrans. [in this case] like the intrans. [in other cases]: but the regular form, accord. to Az, of the [intrans.] verb hence derived is rawiEa , aor. yarowaEu , inf. n. rawaEN . (TA.) -A3- raAEa fiY yadiY ka*aA : see art. ryE . ― -b2- And raAEa , aor. yaruwEu , and yariyEu , inf. n. of the former ruwaAEN , and of the latter rayoEN : see art. ryE .

And xarajotu wa maA raAEaniY A_il~aA fulaAnN liAlbaAbi (assumed tropical:) [ I went forth, and nothing took me by surprise but such a one at the door ]; which is equivalent to saying, and lo, such a one was at the door. (Har p. 207.) And it is said in a trad. of I'Ab, falamo yaruEoniY A_il~aA rajulN A=xi*N bimanokibiY , i. e. I knew not [ save a man taking hold of, or seizing, my shoulder-joint ]; as though he came upon him suddenly, or unexpectedly, without any previous appointment, and without knowledge, and so that event frightened him. (TA.) ― -b3- [ It affected his ruwE , i. e. heart, or mind, with admiration, or pleasure; ] it excited his admiration and approval; it pleased him, or rejoiced him; (S, Msb, K;) said of beauty [&c.]. (Msb.) It is said in a trad., describing the people of Paradise, fayaruwEuhu maA Ealayohi mina All~ibaAsi And what is upon him, of apparel, excites his admiration &c., by its beauty. [in other cases], and the intrans. [in this case] like the intrans. [in other cases]: but the regular form, accord. to Az, of the [intrans.] verb hence derived is rawiEa , aor. yarowaEu , inf. n. rawaEN . definition: [see 1, of which it is an inf.
sourceDefinition: [see 1, of which it is an inf. n. ― -b2- ] Fright, or fear; (S, K;) as also ↓ rawEN [accord. to some, but this seems to be little known]. (TA.) Hence the saying, A^aforaxa rawoEuhu His fright, or fear, departed. (S.) Az says, All the lexicologists whom I have met say A^aforaxa rawoEuhu , with fet-h to the r [in rwEh ], except El-Mundhiree, who informs me that AHeyth used to say, It is only ↓ Afrx rawoEuka , with damm. (TA.) Accord. to different relations of a trad., you say, ↓ A^aforaxa ruwEuka , meaning Fright, or fear, hath departed from thy heart; or may fright, or fear, depart from thy heart; (K, TA;) thus expl. by AHeyth; (TA;) and Afrx rawoEuka , with fet-h; or this latter, only, is the right, and means what thou fearest hath quitted thee, and departed from thee, and become removed; or may what thou fearest quit thee, &c.; as though it were taken from the young bird's going forth from the egg, (K, TA,) and the darkness' becoming removed from it; thus expl. by Aboo-Ahmad El-Hasan Ibn-' Abd-Allah Ibn-Sa'eed El-' Askeree; and AO says that Afrx rwEk [thus in the TA, without any syll. signs,] means let thy fright, or fear, depart, for the case is not as thou fearest it to be. (TA.) It is also said, in a trad. of Mo'áwiyeh, that he wrote in a letter to Ziyád, ↓ liyuforixo ruwEuka , with damm; (K, TA;) but the opinion commonly obtaining with the leading lexicologists is, that it is with fet-h; except AHeyth, who relates it thus, with damm; (TA;) meaning Dismiss thou the rawoE from thy ruwE ; (K, TA;) i. e., the fright, or fear, from thy heart: (TA:) for you say A^aforaxati AlbayoDapu when the young bird quits the egg; and rawoE is fright, or fear, which does not depart from itself, but from its place, which is the ruwE , with damm; (AHeyth, K;) the rawoE in the ruwE being like the young bird in the egg: in like manner also one says A^aforaxa fuw^aAdu Alr~ajuli when a man's fright, or fear, departs: but Dhu-r-Rummeh, though knowing the meaning, has made an inversion, saying, qado A^aforaxato Eano ruwEihi Alkurabu [for qado A^aforaxa Eani Alkurabi ruwEuhu His heart had freed itself from griefs ]. (AHeyth, TA.) AHeyth adds, (TA,) one also says, Eani AlA^amori ↓ A^aforixa ruwEaka , or EalaY AlA^amori , [accord. to different copies of the K, the latter being the reading in the TA, but the former probably the right,] meaning [ Free thy heart from the affair; i. e.] be thou tranquil, and without fear. (K, TA.) Az observes, What AHeyth says is clear; but I am averse from it because of his being alone in his saying; though sometimes later authorities correct things in which the earlier have erred; therefore the correctness of AHeyth may not be [absolutely] denied in this matter, seeing that he had an ample share of knowledge. (TA.) [See also art. frx , in several places.] ― -b3- Also (tropical:) War, or battle; as in the phrase, $ahida Alr~awoEa (tropical:) [ He witnessed, or was present at or in, war, or battle ]. (TA.) [See also an ex. in a verse cited voce saEafN .]

definition: and ruwaAEapu Alfuw^aAdi , applied to a she-camel, Quick, spirited, vigorous;
sourceDefinition: and ruwaAEapu Alfuw^aAdi , applied to a she-camel, Quick, spirited, vigorous; sharp in spirit; syn. $ahomapN *akiy~apN : (K:) and [in like manner] ↓ rawoEaA='u , applied to a she-camel and a mare, (S, K,) but not to a male [in this sense, i. e. its masc. form, A^arowaEu , is not thus used], (S,) sharp in spirit; syn. Hadiydapu Alfuw^aAdi : (S, K:) in the T, ruwaAEN , without p , is applied as an epithet to a mare: and IAar says that ↓ rawoEaA='u , thus applied, is not from raAy^iEapN , but means one that is as though she were fearful, by reason of her sharpness, and briskness, or lightness, of spirit: he says also, that ↓ A^arowaEu , applied to a horse, is like this epithet applied to a man; and IB says, in art. Ejs , that, applied to a man, it signifies quickly frightened or afraid: it is also applied to a heart, meaning that is frightened, [or startled, ] by reason of its sharpness, at everything that is heard or seen; and so ruwaAEN . (TA.) [See also raAy^iEN , and A^arowaEu mentioned and expl. therewith.]

definition: [act. part. n. of raAEahu , q. v.,] Frightening; putting in fear; making afraid; [and particu- larly] by its beauty and abundance or multitude. (Lth, TA.) ― -b2- Applied to beauty, That excites...
sourceDefinition: [act. part. n. of raAEahu , q. v.,] Frightening; putting in fear; making afraid; [and particu- larly] by its beauty and abundance or multitude. (Lth, TA.) ― -b2- Applied to beauty, That excites admiration and approval in the ruwE [i. e. heart, or mind, ] of him who beholds it, and pleases him, or rejoices him. (TA.) Applied to a man, (K, * TA,) as also ↓ A^arowaEu (S, K, TA) so applied, (S, TA,) Who excites admiration and approval by his beauty (S, K, TA) and pleasingness of aspect, (K, TA,) with generousness, or nobleness, and excellence, and lordly condition; (TA;) or by his courage: (K, TA:) or the former, beautiful in countenance, who excites admiration and approval by his pleasingness of aspect and by the goodliness of his form or figure or state of apparel and the like: or, as some say, who frightens men by his aspect, inspiring reverence or awe: but the former explanation is the more reasonable: and ↓ the latter epithet, a beautiful man, who excites admiration and approval in him who beholds him: or, as some say, sharp; lively in spirit, and sharp in intellect: (TA:) [see also the next preceding paragraph:] the fem. of the former is with p : (TA:) that of the latter, ↓ rawoEaA='u : (S:) the pl. of raAy^iEN is A^arowaAEN , (K, * TA,) applied to men, like as rawaAy^iEu [the pl. of raAy^iEapN ] is to women: (TA:) and the pl. of A^arowaEu and rawoEaA='u is ↓ ruwEN , (K, TA,) applied to men and to women. (TA.) You say also, farasN raAy^iEN A beautiful horse, that frightens ( yuruwEu , i. e. yuxaw~ifu , [or rather startles, but better rendered excites admiration and approval in, or pleases, or rejoices, ]) the beholder by his beauty: (Mgh:) and farasN raAy^iEapN , and ↓ rawoEaA='u , [but see, respecting the latter, a remark of IAar in the next preceding paragraph,] a mare that excites admiration and approval, or pleases, or rejoices, ( taruwEu ,) by her generousness, or excellence, or high blood, and her description. (TA.) [See also art. ryE , to which, as well as to the present art., raAy^iEN , applied to a horse, is said, in the TA, to belong.] And ziynapN raAy^iEapN Beautiful ornament. (TA.) And kalaAmN raAy^iEN (tropical:) Surpassing, or excelling, speech, or language. (TA.) -A2- Also Frightened, or afraid; and so ↓ rawiEN , with the w unaltered, as though it were of the measure faEiylN : [or both signify having fright or fear: for] each is a possessive epithet: or the former may be of the measure faAEilN in the sense of the measure mafoEuwlN [and therefore have the signification first given]. (TA.)

definition: Saliva; syn. ruDaAbN ; (S, K, TA;) i. e. (TA) the water of the mouth; (JK, Msb, K, TA;) its luEaAb : (TA:) or the water of the mouth in the early morning, or first part of the day; (Lth, TA: [but...
sourceDefinition: Saliva; syn. ruDaAbN ; (S, K, TA;) i. e. (TA) the water of the mouth; (JK, Msb, K, TA;) its luEaAb : (TA:) or the water of the mouth in the early morning, or first part of the day; (Lth, TA: [but this rendering is often inapplicable:]) or the water of the mouth while it is therein; for when it has gone forth from the mouth it is termed buSaAqN and buzaAqN and busaAqN : (K in art. bSq :) and ↓ riyqapN signifies the same, in poetry: (Msb, TA:) or this has a more particular meaning; (S, Msb, * K;) [i. e. it means somewhat of saliva; or a little saliva: ] the pl. is A^aroyaAqN [a pl. of pauc.] (S, K, TA) and riyaAqN [a pl. of mult.]. (TA.) [Hence,] one says, A^aboliEoniY riyqiY [ Suffer thou me to swallow my saliva; ] give thou me time to swallow my saliva: (K and TA in art. blE :) or (assumed tropical:) grant thou me some delay, or let me alone for a while, that I may say, or do, such a thing. (Har p. 164.) [And AibotalaEa riyqah He swallowed his saliva: meaning (assumed tropical:) he restrained his anger: see 1 in art. blE .] And $uriba EalaY Alr~iyqi [ It was drunk in the state of fasting; before breakfast ]: (S, K:) and in like manner A^ukila [ It was so eaten ]. (K.) And huwa EalaY Alr~iyqi , (AO, S, K,) or EalaY riyqihi , (TA,) and ↓ huwa ray~iqN , (AO, S, K,) of the measure fayoEilN , (S,) and ↓ raAy^iqN , (K,) i. e. [ He is fasting; ] he has not breakfasted. (TA.) And A^atayotuhu EalaY riyqK (ISk, S) and EalaY riyqi nafosiY , (S, TA,) and ↓ A^atayotuhu ray~iqFA and ↓ raAy^iqFA , I came to him [ fasting, ] not having eaten anything. (ISk, S, TA.) [Hence also riyqu Al$~amosi , likewise called luEaAbu Al$~amosi and muxaATu Al$~amosi and riyqu Al$~ayaATiyni and muxaATu Al$~ayoTaAni , (tropical:) The fine filmy cobwebs termed gossamer: see arts. lEb and mxT .] ― -b2- Also Strength: and the remains of life, or of the spirit, or of the soul: syns. quw~apN and ramaqN [which latter, it should be observed, has both of these meanings, so that possibly only the former meaning may be here intended]. (K.) You say, kaAna h`*aA AlA^amoru wabinaA riyqN This event happened when there was in us strength. (TA.)

definition: Fresh butter with dates;
sourceDefinition: Fresh butter with dates; (M, K;) in the dial. of Ifreekeeyeh: (M, TA:) or a certain food of the Arabs, in which are dates and fresh butter. (S.) ― -b2- Also Any deadly food. (Th, TA.) ― -b3- The food of the people of the fire [ of Hell ]. (ISd, K.) A certain tree in Hell: (K:) [respecting which] I'Ab says that when the saying [in the Kur xliv. 43 and 44] A_in~a $jarapa A@lz~aq~uwmi TaEaAmu A@loA^aviymi [ Verily the tree of Alz~aq~uwm shall be the food of the sinner ] was revealed, Aboo-Jahl said, “Dates and fresh butter: we will swallow it leisurely:” therefore God revealed [these other words of the Kur, xxxvii. 62 and 63,] A_in~ahaA $ajarapN taxoruju fiY A^aSoli A@lojaHiymi TaloEuhaA kaA^an~ahu ruw^uwsu A@l$~ayaATiyni [ Verily it is a tree coming forth in the bottom of Hell, the fruit thereof being as though it were the heads of the devils, or of terrible serpents, foul in aspect, having manes, as expl. by Bd]: (S:) it is thus called after a tree of which a description here follows. (K.)

sourceDefinition: see 1. ― -b2- Aizodahara bihi , (originally Aizotahara , TA,) He took care of it, (S, A, K,) and was mindful of it: (A:) or (so in the TA, but in the K “ and ”) he rejoiced in it; (IAth, K) his face became shining by reason of it: (IAth:) or he was mind ful of it: or [ Aizodahiro bihi signifies be thou vigorous, sedulous, earnest, energetic, or diligent, in it; meaning, in the thing that I command thee to do; for] AlAizodihaAru bi$aYo'K means [by implication] thy commanding thy companion to be vigorous, sedulous, earnest, energetic, or diligent, in the thing which thou commandest him to do: (K:) all which significations are from zahorapN in the sense of “ beauty, and brightness. ” (TA.) (TA.)

definition: (S, Mgh, K, written with the conjunctive hemzeh, Msb in art.
sourceDefinition: (S, Mgh, K, written with the conjunctive hemzeh, Msb in art. Ast ) and ↓ satahN (S Mgh, K) and ↓ satohN (K) and ↓ sitohN (CK [but not in my MS. copy of the K nor in the TA, and of doubtful authority, as will be seen from what follows,]) signify the same, (S, * Mgh, * K,) i. e. The podex, buttock or buttocks, posteriors, rump, or croup; and sometimes the anus; (S;) ↓ satahN being the original form, as is shown by the pl., (S, Mgh,) which is A^asotaAhN ; (S, Mgh, K;) like jamalN and A^ajomaAlN : it may not be [↓ sitohN and ↓ sutohN ] like ji*oEN and qufolN , of which the pls. are also of the measure A^afoEaAlN , because, when you restore the ' which is the final radical, and reject the medial radical [which is t ], you say sahN , with fet-h, (S, Mgh, *) which has both of the meanings expl. above, as also suhN , (K,) but [SM says,] this last, mentioned by the author of the K, is strange, and I have not seen it on the authority of any one [else]: (TA:) and some say satN , (IKh, S, Mgh, TA,) suppressing the final radical [of satahN ], (S,) i. e., without h at the end and without hemzeh [or A ] at the beginning. (TA.) [All are of the fem. gender.] It is said in a trad., AlEayonu wikaA='u Als~ahi , or, as some relate it, Als~ati , (S, Mgh, TA,) [ The eye is the tie of the anus, ] meaning that when one [closes the eye and] sleeps, the tie of the sah becomes loosed, and the excrement and wind issue. (TA.) And A^abuw AlA^asotaAhi means He who has large posteriors. (Az, TA.) biA@soti fulaAnK is a phrase of the Arabs significant of reviling; (S;) said when holding one in contempt; meaning laSiqa AlEaAru biA@soti fulaAnK (assumed tropical:) [ May disgrace cleave to the Ast of such a one ]. (Mgh.) And yaA A@bona A@sotihaA (tropical:) [ O son of her Ast ], (K, TA,) a prov. of the Arabs, (TA,) is an allusion to one's father's A_iHomaAD [see 2 in art. HmD ] of the former's mother; (Z, TA;) and is said to mean A^an~ahu wulida mini A@sotihaA : (TA:) and the Arabs called the sons of the female slave banuw A@sotihaA . (Sh, TA.) And one says to a man who is deemed abject and weak, Aisotu A^um~ika A^aDoyaqu [lit. Thy mother's Ast is too contracted ], and Aisotuka A^aDoyaqu mino A^ano tafoEala ka*aA wa ka*aA [ Thine Ast is too contracted, meaning (assumed tropical:) thine ability is too small, for thy doing such and such things ]: (TA: [see also Freytag's Arab. Prov., i. 607:]) and A^anotumo A^aDoyaqu A^asotaAhFA mino A^ano tafoEaluwhu [in like manner] is an allusion to inability [meaning (assumed tropical:) Ye are unable to do it ]. (K.) The saying of a poet, wa A^anota makaAnuka mino waAy^ilK makaAnu AlquraAdi mini A@soti Aljamalo (tropical:) [ And thou, thy place in the tribe of Wáïl is like the place of the tick in the rump of the camel, ] is tropical; for they do not [properly] say Aisotu Aljamali , but Eajuzu Aljamali . (S.) One says also to a man who is deemed low, or base, A^anota AlAisotu Als~ufolaY , (TA,) and Ant Alsb~ahu Als~ufolaY , meaning (assumed tropical:) Thou art among others in the condition of the Ast of mankind: (S, TA:) and of low, or base, men, one says, h`w^ulaA='i AlA^asotaAhu ; and of such as are excellent, h`w^ulaA='i AlA^aEoyaAnu , and Alwujuwhu . (TA.) And one says, laqiytu minohu A@sota Alkalobapi , (A, K,) a prov., (TA,) meaning (assumed tropical:) I experienced from him, or it, what I disliked, or hated. (A, K, TA. [See also Freytag's Arab. Prov., ii. 445.]) And Aisotu AlbaAy^ini A^aEorafu , or A^aEolamu : see art. byn . And maA laka A@sotN maEi A@sotika (assumed tropical:) Thou hast no one [ with thee ] to assist thee: (A, K, TA:) another prov., related on the authority of AZ as said to one who has no large amount of property, nor number of men. (Sgh, TA.) And tarakotuhu biA@soti AlA^aroDi , another prov., (TA,) meaning (assumed tropical:) I left him destitute, poor, (K, TA,) possessing nothing: (TA:) or tarakotuhu biA@soti Almatoni (assumed tropical:) I left him on the hard ground, alone. (Meyd.) And maA laka fiY h`*aA AlA^amori A@sotN wa laA famN (assumed tropical:) Thou hast not in this thing, or affair, root nor branch: Jereer says, famaA lakumu A@sotN fiY AlEalaA='i wa laA= famu [ And ye have not any root in eminence, nor branch ]. (TA.) And kaAna *`lika EalaY A@soti Ald~ahori (tropical:) That was in the beginning of time: (A, K, TA:) or in the olden time; (AO, S, TA;) as also EalaY A_is~i Ald~ahori . (AO, TA.) See also art. Ast . [And see other exs. in Freytag's Arab. Prov. i. 355 and 378 (a variation of a prov. mentioned in the preceding page) and 607 and 622 and 729-730.]

definition: A shovel, or spade, of iron;
sourceDefinition: A shovel, or spade, of iron; (MA, PS;) an implement (S, Msb, K) like the mijorafap , except that it is of iron, (S, Msb,) with which clay, soil, or mud, is cleared away (Msb, K) from the surface of the earth: (Msb:) a misoHaAp [ for digging, i. e. a spade, ] has a cross piece of wood upon which the digger presses his foot: K, voce EitorN :) and there is a curved kind, [app. a sort of hoe, ] such as is called in Pers. kananod : (S:) pl. masaAHK . (S, Msb.) Ru-beh likens the toes, or extremities of the fore parts of the hoofs, of horses, to masaAHK ; because with them they pare the ground: so in the T: or, accord. to the M, he likens thereto the hoofs of asses. (TA.) ― -b2- misoHaApu Aln~aAri means [ The fire-shovel; ] a thing with which the fire is stirred. (TA voce miHoraAvo .)

sourceDefinition: , (A, K,) inf. n. tasoriyjN , (K,) (tropical:) He rendered it beautiful; (A, K;) namely, a person's face; said of God: (A:) (assumed tropical:) he adorned, ornamented, decorated, or embellished, it; namely, a thing. (TA.) ― -b3- One says also, ↓ sr~j EalaY~a A^usoruwjapF (tropical:) [ He forged against me a lie ]. (A, TA.) And EalaY~a ↓ tsr~j (tropical:) He lied, or lied purposely, against me. (A, TA. definition: a word of well-known meaning;
sourceDefinition: a word of well-known meaning; (S, O, K;) i. q. miSobaAHN [i. e. A lamp, or its lighted wick, (the latter of which meanings is assigned to both of these words by Jel in xxiv. 35,)] (L, Msb, TA) that gives light by night: (L, TA:) or, properly, a lighted wick; its employment to signify the place thereof [i. e. a lamp, generally a vessel of glass having in its bottom a small glass tube into which the lower part of the wick is inserted, ] being a well-known tropical application: (MF, TA:) pl. surujN . (O, Msb, TA.) (A, TA.) So too is the Prophet. (Kur xxxiii. 45.) 'Omar, also, is called in a trad. siraAju A^aholi Aljan~api (assumed tropical:) [ The lamp of the people of Paradise ]. (TA.) And one says, AlhudiY siraAjN Almuw^ominiyna (tropical:) [ The Kur-án is the lamp of the believers ], (A,) or siraAju Almuw^omini [ the lamp of the believer ]. (TA.) ― -b3- Also, metaphorically, (tropical:) The eye; because of its being often likened to a siraAj . (Har p. 554.)

definition: , (S, MA, Msb,) aor.
sourceDefinition: , (S, MA, Msb,) aor. ; (Msb;) and safuha , [aor. ;] (S, Msb;) inf. n. safahN and safaAhapN (S, MA, Msb, K *) and safaAhN , (S, MA, K, *) [all mentioned in the MA as of the former verb, and so in the TA when that verb is trans., but properly] the first is of the former verb, and the second is of the latter verb, (S, Msb,) and so is the third; (S;) He (a man, S) was, or became, such as is termed safiyh ; (S, TA;) [i. e.] he was, or became, unwise, witless, or destitute of wisdom or understanding, or [rather] lightwitted. (MA.) ― -b2- The phrase safiha nafosapu , [of which an instance occurs in the Kur ii. 124, and] to which gabina raA^oyahu and baTira Eayo$ahu and A^alima baTonahu and wafiqa A^amorahu and ra$ida A^amorahu are similar, was originally safihato nafosu zayodK [or rather safihato nafosuhu i. e. Himself, or his mind, was, or became, lightwitted, &c.]; but when [the dependence of] the verb became transferred [from the nfs ] to the man, what followed the verb was put in the accus. case by being its objective complement, for the phrase became identical in meaning with nafosahu ↓ saf~aha [ he made himself, or his mind, lightwitted, &c.]: so say the Basrees and Ks; and it is allowable with them to make this accus. to precede [the verb]; like as it is allowable to say, gulaAmahu Darab zayodN : (S, TA:) accord. to the K, the verb thus used has three forms; (TA;) you say safiha nafosahu and raA^oyahu , (K, TA,) and Hilomahu , (TA,) and safuha , and safaha , meaning Hamalahu EalaYAls~afahi [which is virtually the same as saf~ahahu i. e. he made himself, or his mind, lightwitted, or unwise, &c., and in like manner his judgment, or opinion, and he made his gravity, or forbearance, or the like, to become levity, or hastiness, &c.]: or he attributed safah [i. e. lightwittedness, &c., to himself, or his mind, and to his judgment, or opinion ]: or he destroyed it; (K, TA;) agreeably with the meaning assigned to safiha nafosahu by AO: (TA:) or this means he held himself in mean, or light, estimation; (MA, and Ksh and Bd in ii. 124;) and rendered himself low, base, or contemptible: (Bd ibid.:) but Lh says that safiha nafosahu , with kesr [to the f ], inf. n. safahN and safaAhapN and safaAhN , means Hamalahu EalaY Als~afahi [or HamalahaA ], and is the approved form, and that some say safuha , which is rare: and accord. to J and others, (TA,) when they say sfh nafosahu , and raA^oyahu , they do not say it otherwise than with kesr [to the f ], because faEula is not trans.: (S, TA:) so that the three forms of the verb mentioned in the K require consideration: (TA:) accord. to Fr, when [the dependence of] the verb in the phrase safiha nafosahu became transferred from the nfs to the possessor thereof, what followed the verb became an explicative, to indicate that the safah [or lightwittedness, &c.,] was therein; and by rule it should be safiha zayodN nafosFA , for the explicative should not be otherwise than indeterminate; but it was left in its state of a prefixed noun, and put in the accus. case in the manner of an indeterminate noun as being likened thereto; [the meaning, therefore, accord. to him, is he was, or became, lightwitted, &c., as to his mind; ] it is not allowable, however, in his opinion, to make this accus. to precede [the verb], because the explicative may not precede; and similar to this is the phrase Diqotu bihi *aroEFA , and Tibotu bihi nafosFA , meaning DaAqa *aroEiYbihi and TaAbato nafosiY bihi : (S, TA:) but this saying [of Fr] is disallowed by the grammarians; for they say that explicatives are indeterminate, and that determinate nouns may not be used as indeterminate: some of the grammarians say that A_il~aAmano safiha nafosahu in the Kur [ii. 124] means Al~A mn safiha fiYnafosihi [ but he who is lightwitted, &c., in his mind ], i. e., who becomes safiyh ; [the prep.] fY being suppressed [and the noun therefore put in the accus. case agreeably with a general rule]: Zj holds that the approvable saying is, that it means A_il~aA mano jahila nafosahu , i. e., but he who is [ ignorant or silly or foolish or] unreflecting in his mind: and in like manner, safiha raA^oyahu means jahilahu [i. e. he was ignorant, &c., in his judgment, or opinion ]; and his judgment, or opinion, was unsound, without rectitude: and safiha nafosahu signifies also he lost himself, or his own soul. (TA.) safiha AlHaq~a is likewise expl. as meaning AlHaq~a ↓ saf~aha [ He made the truth, or right, to be foolishness, or the like ]; and Yoo held the one to be a dial. var. of the other, and the measure of the former verb to denote intensiveness; and accord. to this explanation one may say, safihotu zayodFA meaning zayodFA ↓ saf~ahotu [ I pronounced Zeyd lightwitted, &c.]: or the meaning is jahila AlHaq~a [ he ignored the truth, or right ], and he did not see it to be the truth, or right: (TA:) or he regarded the truth, or right, as foolishness, or ignorance. (S and TA in art. gmT .) See also 2. ― -b3- safiha Ealayohi signifies jahila [i. e., when thus trans. by means of EalaY , He feigned ignorance to him ]; as also safuha , (K, TA,) and ↓ tsAfh . (K.) ― -b4- And safihotu naSiybiY [and it is implied in the K that one says safahotu nSybY also, but only the former is authorized by the TA,] I forgot my share, or portion. (Th, K, TA.) ― -b5- And safaha SaAHibahu , aor. , He overcame his companion in what is termed musaAfahap [inf. n. of 3, q. v.]. (K.) You say, ↓ saAfahahu fasafahahu . (TA.) ― -b6- safihati AlT~aEonapu , (JK, K, TA,) inf. n. safahN , (TA,) (tropical:) The spear-wound, or the like, emitted blood which came from it quickly (JK, K, TA) and dried up ( wajaf~a [in the TK wixf ]): (K, TA:) so in the A. (TA.) ― -b7- safiha Al$~araAba , (S, K,) inf. n. safahN , (TA,) He drank much of the beverage, or wine, without having his thirst satisfied thereby. (S, K, TA.) See also 3. And safiha AlmaA='a (tropical:) He drank the water immoderately. (TA.) ― -b8- And safihotu and safahotu signify $ugilotu , (so in the CK,) in [some of] the copies of the K $agalotu , but the right reading is $ugilotu [i. e. I was occupied, or busied, or diverted from a thing]: or, accord. to the copies of the K, ta$ag~alotu ; but correctly, or $agalotu [i. e. I occupied, or busied, or diverted from a thing]. (TA.)

definition: [ Having the quality termed safahN ;
sourceDefinition: [ Having the quality termed safahN ; i. e., accord. to the explanation of the primary signification of the latter, above, Light; and in a state of motion, commotion, or agitation: ] applied to a camel's nose-rein, (S, K,) light: (S:) or quivering; (K, TA;) because of the she-camel's shaking it, and contending in pulling it. (TA: but there said to be, when thus applied, tropical.) Dhu-rRummeh says, EalaY Zahori miqolaAtK safiyhK jadiyluhaA i. e. [ Upon the back of a she-camel that had brought forth but once and not conceived after, ] whose nose-rein was light. (S. In the TA, zimaAmuhaA is here put in the place of jadiyluhaA .) And one says also naAqapN safiyhapu AlzimaAmi , (K, TA,) meaning [ A she-camel whose nose-rein is light, or quivering: or] light, or agile, in pace or going. (TA: in which this, also, is said to be tropical.) ― -b2- Also Lightwitted; light of intellect or understanding; (TA;) deficient in intellect or understanding; (Msb;) ignorant; (Mujáhid, K, TA;) weak; foolish, stupid, unsound in intellect or understanding, dull therein, or having little, or no, intellect, or understanding; (Mujáhid, TA;) and ↓ saAfihN , also, [which is syn. with safiyhN in all the senses mentioned above,] is expl. by IAar as having this last meaning of foolish, stupid, &c.: (TA:) the fem. is safiyhapN : (Msb, K:) and the pl. of the masc., (K,) or of the masc. and fem., (Msb, TA,) is sufahaA='u , (Msb, K, TA,) and of both, sifaAhN , and of the fem., safiyhaAtN also and safaAy^ihu and suf~ahN . (K, TA.) In the Kur ii. 282, safiyhFA means, accord. to Ibn-'Arafeh, Ignorant of the ordinances, or statutes; one who does not dictate well, and knows not what dictation is; for he who is ignorant in all his circumstances may not deal with another upon credit: accord. to ISd, ignorant or Sagiyr [meaning under the age of puberty ]; not ignorant of dictating, as Lh asserts it to mean, because it is added, “ or not able to dictate, himself: ” this, says Er-Rághib, denotes safah in respect of worldly matters: in the Kur lxxii. 4, safiyhunaA denotes safah in religion. (TA.) In the Kur iv. 4, the pl. Als~ufahaA=' is said to mean Women, and young children; because they are ignorant of the proper object of expense: and I'Ab is related to have said that women are termed Als~uf~ahu and Als~ufahaA='u : (Lh, TA:) Az, also, says that a woman is termed safiyhapN because of the weakness of her intellect, and because she does not manage well her property; and in like manner are termed children as long as they are not known to be characterized by maturity of intellect, and rectitude of actions, and good management of affairs. (TA.) ― -b3- vawobN safiyhN (tropical:) A garment, or piece of cloth, badly woven; thin, flimsy, unsubstantial, or scanty in the yarn. (K, * TA.)

sourceDefinition: , (S, A, Mgh, Msb, K, &c.,) as also ↓ saliHN (accord. to the K) or ↓ siloHN (accord. to the Msb) and ↓ suloHaAnN , (K,) [the last mentioned in the L as a pl.,] A weapon, or weapons; i. e. an instrument, or instruments, of war; (A, K;) the thing [or things ] with which one fights in war, and repels, or defends oneself; (Msb;) anything with which one repels the enemy, as a sword and spear &c.: (Ham p. 73:) or a weapon, or weapons, of iron: (Lth, Mgh, K:) it is of the masc. gender, (S, Msb, TA,) accord. to the more approved usage, (TA,) or that which most prevails, (Msb,) because in the pl. it takes the form of A^asoliHapN , which is a pl. form of a masc. n., (S, Msb, *) as in the instances of A^aHomirapN , pl. of HimaArN , and A^arodiyapN , pl. of ridaA='N , (S,) but it is also fem., (S, Msb, K,) and has also for pls. suluHN and suloHaAnN , (L,) and the pl. fem. is silaAHaAtN . (Msb.) You say rajulN *uw silaAHK [ A man having a weapon or weapons ]. (K.) And qawomN *awuw silaAHK [ A people, or party, having weapons, or arms ]. (S, A, K.) And labisa Als~ilaAHa [ He wore, or put on, the weapon, or the weapons, or arms ]. (S, A, K.) And A^axa*a Alqawomu A^asoliHatahumo The people, or party, took their weapons, or arms, each taking his. (Msb.) ― -b2- A sword (Az, Mgh, K) alone is sometimes termed silaAHN . (Az, Mgh.) ― -b3- And A bow without a string (K) is likewise thus termed. (TA.) ― -b4- And A staff, or stick. (K.) ― -b5- silaAHu lv~awori means (assumed tropical:) The horns of the bull. (S, * TA.) ― -b6- *uw Als~ilaAHi is (tropical:) an appel-lation of Als~amaAku Alr~aAmiHu [i. e. The star Arcturus ]. (A, TA.) ― -b7- And A^axa*ati AlA_ibilu silaAHahaA and biA^asoliHatihaA mean (tropical:) The camels became fat, and of goodly appearance; (A, L, TA;) i. e. their fat became as though it were weapons with which they prevented their being slaughtered: (L, TA:) and the like has been mentioned before, [voce rumoHN ,] in art. rmH . (TA.)

definition: A certain plant, the pasturing upon which causes the milk (S, K) of the camels (S) to become abundant: (S, K:) or a certain kind of tree, or shrub, that has this effect: (L:) [see also A_isoliyxN :]...
sourceDefinition: A certain plant, the pasturing upon which causes the milk (S, K) of the camels (S) to become abundant: (S, K:) or a certain kind of tree, or shrub, that has this effect: (L:) [see also A_isoliyxN :] it was said to an Arab woman of the desert, “ What is thy father's tree? ” and she answered, $ajarapu A^abiY AlA_isoliyHo rugowapN waSariyHN wasanaAmN A_iToriyHo [ The tree of my father is the isleeh: froth upon the milk, and milk free from froth; and a long, or tall, hump: these are the consequences of pasturing upon it]: (S, * L:) or it is a certain herb, or leguminous plant, of those that are slender and soft ( mino A^aHoraAri Albuquwli ), growing in the winter, that causes the camels to void sulaAH [or thin excrement ] when they eat much of it: or a certain herb ( Eu$obap ), resembling the jirojiyr [or rocket ], growing upon tracts of sand such as are termed Huquwf : or a certain kind of plant, growing conspicuously in plain, or soft, tracts, having a thin and delicate leaf, and a pericarp ( sinofap ) stuffed with grains, or seeds, like those of the poppy; which is one of the plants of the rain of the Sayof [here meaning spring (see zamanN )], and which causes the cattle to void sulaAH : n. un. with p : Aboo-Ziyád says that the places in which the AslyH grows are sands. (L.)

definition: A vagor [or frontier of a hostile country ]: (K:) or a place of arms or weapons, (Mgh,) like a vagor and a maroqab [which is an elevated place of observation ], (S, Mgh, TA,) wherein are parties that...
sourceDefinition: A vagor [or frontier of a hostile country ]: (K:) or a place of arms or weapons, (Mgh,) like a vagor and a maroqab [which is an elevated place of observation ], (S, Mgh, TA,) wherein are parties that watch the enemy, lest they should make an invasion at unawares, and , when they see them, inform their companions, in order that they may prepare themselves for them: (Nh, TA:) pl. masaAliHu . (S, Mgh.) ― -b2- Also, [in one of my copies of the S erroneously written musal~aHap ,] A people, or party, having arms, or weapons; an armed people or party; (S, A, K, TA;) composing a numerous body, in a place of observation, with the keeping of which they are entrusted, at the frontier of an enemy's country; a single person of whom is termed ↓ masolaHiY~N ; (A, * L;) and masolaHapN [also] is thus applied to a single person in a saying of 'Omar: (Mgh:) they are thus called because of their having weapons, or because of their occupying the place called masolaHapN : (Nh:) or the mslHp of the army are a party of capturers that go before the army, exploring for them the way, and searching as spies to learn news of the enemy, lest the enemy should make a sudden assault upon them; not suffering any one of the enemy to enter the territory of the Muslims, and warning the Muslims of the approach of an army. (ISh.)

sourceDefinition: , (S, Msb, K, *) aor. , (K,) inf. n. samoEN (S Msb, K) and simoEN , or this latter is a simple subst., (Lh, K,) and samaAEN , (S, K,) or this last [also] is a simple subst., (Msb,) and samaAEapN and samaAEiyapN (K) and masomaEN , (TA,) [ He heard it, (namely, a thing, as in the S,) or (tropical:) him; ] and ↓ tsm~E , (Msb, K,) also written and pronounced Ais~am~aEa ; (K, TA;) and ↓ AstmE ; (Msb;) are syn. with samiEa (Msb,K) as trans. By itself; (Msb;) and AstmE [also] in sys. With samiEa [ as trans. by itself]: (Ham p. 694, where occurs a usage of its act. part. n. showing the verb to be trans. by itself:) or ↓ AstmE denotes what is intentional, signifying only he gave ear, hearkened, or listened: but samiEa , [as also ↓ tmsm~E and ↓ AstsmE ,] what is unintentional, as well as what is intentional. (Msb.) You say, samiEa Al$~aYo'a [ He heard or listened to, the thing ] (S.) And AlS~awota ↓ tsm~E [ He listened to, or heard, the sound ]. (TA.) [And samiEotu lahu SawotFA I heard him, or it, utter, or produce, a sound; lit. I heard a sound attributable to him, or it. And samiEahu minohu He heard it form him. And samiEahu Eanohu He heard it as related from him; he heard it on his authority. And samiEahu yaquwlu ka*aA He heard him say such a thing. ] And samiEa bihi [ He heard of it; for samiEa Alt~akal~uma bihi , or the like]. (Kur xii. 31 and xxviii. 36 and xxxviii. 6, S, K, TA.) [When trans. by means of li alone, or A_ilaY , it denotes what is intentional.] You say, samiEotu lahu , (S, Msb, TA,) and A_ilayohi , (S, TA,) meaning I gave ear, hearkened, or listened, to him, or it; (S, Msb, * TA;) and lh ↓ tsm~Et (Msb,) or Alyh , and Ais~am~aEotu , (S, TA,) signify the same; (S, Msb, TA;) and so lh ↓ AstmEt , (S, Msb, K,) and Alyh . (K.) It is said in the Kur [xxxvii. 8], accord. to different readings, laA yasomaEuwna A_ilaY AlmalaA_i AlA^aEolaY , and ↓ laA yas~am~aEuwna , They shall not listen [ to the archangels ]: (S:) or the former has this signification, they shall not listen to the angels (Bd, Jel) in heaven, (Jel,) or the exalted angels: (Bd:) and ↓ the latter, they shall not seek, or endeavour, to listen &c. (Bd.) And in the same [xvii. 50], ↓ naHonu A^aEolamu bimaA yasotamiEuwna bihi A_i*o yasotamiEuwna A_ilayoka [ We are cognizant of that on account of which they hearken when they hearken to thee ]; bh meaning bisababihi , (Bd, Jel,) and liA^ajolihi , (Bd,) alluding to scoffing, or derision. (Bd, Jel.) [For various usages of samoEN and other inf. ns., whether employed as inf. ns. or as simple substs., see those words below.] ― -b2- It also signifies He understood it; (TA;) he understood its meaning; i. e., the meaning of a person's speech. (Msb.) You say, lamo tasomaEo maA qulotu laka Thou didst not understand what I said to thee. (TA.) And such is the most obvious meaning of the verb in the saying, A_ino kaAna yasomaEu AlxaTiyba [ If he understand the words of the preacher ]; for this is the proper meaning in this case: but it may be rendered tropically, (tropical:) if he hear the voice of the preacher. (Msb.) ― -b3- Also He knew it: as in the saying, samiEa A@ll~`hu qawolaka [ God knew thy saying ]. (Msb.) ― -b4- Also (assumed tropical:) He accepted it; namely, evidence, and praise: or, said of the latter, (assumed tropical:) he recompensed it by acceptance: (Msb:) (tropical:) he paid regard to it, and answered it; namely, prayer: (tropical:) he answered, or assented to, or complied with, it; namely, a person's speech. (TA.) The saying samiEa A@ll~`hu limano Hamidahu means May God accept the praise of him who praiseth Him: or, accord. to IAmb, may God recompense by acceptance the praise of him who praiseth Him: (Msb:) or may God answer the prayer of him who praiseth Him. (TA, as on the authority of IAmb.) ― -b5- Also (assumed tropical:) He obeyed him: as in the saying in the Kur [xxxvi. 24], A_in~iY A=manotu birab~ikumo faA@somaEuwni (assumed tropical:) [ Verily I believe in your Lord, and do ye obey me ]. (TA.) ― -b6- Lth says that the phrase samiEato A^u*uniY zayodFA yafoEalu ka*aA waka*aA means (assumed tropical:) My eye saw Zeyd doing such and such things: but Az says, I know not whence Lth brought this; for it is not of the way of the Arabs to say smEt A*nY as meaning my eye saw: it is in my judgment corrupt language, and I am not sure but that it may have been originated by those addicted to innovations and erroneous opinions. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: [inf. n of sm~E , as also tasomiEapN , q. v. infrà, voce sumoEapN ,] is syn. with ↓ A_isomaAEN [The making one to hear ]. (K.) You say, sm~Ehu AlS~awota and ↓ AsmEhu [ He made him to hear the sound ]. (S.) And sm~Ehu AlHadiyva (TA) and ↓ AsmEhu (S, TA) [ He made him to hear the narra- tive ]; both signifying the same. (TA.) [And sm~E bihi He made to hear of it, or him. ] It is said in a trad., mano sam~aEa Aln~aAsa biEamalihi sam~aEa A@ll~`hu bihi A^asaAmiEa xaloqihi waHaq~arahu waSag~arahu (S, * Mgh, TA) [ Whoso maketh men to hear of his deed, ] God will make the ears of his creatures to hear of him on the day of resurrection; (TA;) or whoso maketh his deed notorious, that men may see it and hear of it, God will make notorious his hypocrisy, and fill with it the ears of his creatures, and they shall be generally acquainted with it, [ and He will render him contemptible, and small in estimation, ] so that he will become disgraced; (Mgh;) or the meaning may be, God will manifest to men his internal state, and fill their ears with the evilness of his secret intentions, in requital of his deed: or, as some relate it, [for A^asaAmiEa xaloqihi ] we should say, saAmiEu xaloqihi , which is an epithet applied to God; so that the meaning is, Go [ the Hearer of his creatures ] will disgrace him: (TA:) [for] ― -b2- sm~E bh , (S, Mgh, Msb,) inf. n. tasomiyEN , (S, Mgh, K,) signifies [also] He rendered him, or it, notorious, and infamous: (S, Mgh, K: *) or he spread it abroad, for men to speak of it. (Msb.) ― -b3- Also He raised him from obscurity to fame. (S, K. *) ― -b4- And He made him to hear what was bad, evil, abominable, or foul, and he reviled him: (AZ, T and L in art. nd :) and ↓ AsmEhu [also] has the latter of these two significations. (S, K.)

sourceDefinition: inf. n. of samiEa , (S, Msb, K,) like ↓ samaAEN , (S, K,) [&c.,] or the latter is a simple subst. [used in the abstract sense of the former]. (Msb.) You say, samoEFA waTaAEapF , [for A^asomaEu samoEFA waA^uTiyEu TaAEapF , an emphatic mode of expression, meaning I hear and I obey, or for samiEotu samoEFA waA^aTaEotu TaAEapF , which means the same, but more emphatically; TaAEapF being a quasi-inf. n. for A_iTaAEapF ;] the verb [of each] being understood: and samoEN waTaAEapN , meaning A^amoriY *`lika [i. e. A^amoriY samoEN waTaAEapN My affair is hearing and obeying ]. (K.) You say also, [in like manner,] Aall~`hum~a samoEFA laA balogFA , (K,) and samoEN laA balogN : (TA:) see simoEN . And samoEu A^u*uniY fulaAnFA yaquwla *`lika , (K,) [said to be] the only instance of the kind among inf. ns. of trans. verbs except raA^oYu EayoniY , (TA in art. rA^Y ,) [in a copy of the M, in art. rA^Y , written samoEa A*nY and raA^oYa EynY ,] and A*nY ↓ simoEu , and A*nY ↓ samoEapu , and A*nY ↓ simoEapu [ My ear heard (lit. my ear's hearing ) such a one say that ]. (K) ― -b2- [As a simple subst., it signifies] The sense of the ear; (K;) [i. e., of hearing; ] the faculty in the ear whereby it perceives sounds. (TA.) sourceDefinition: i. q. samoEN , either as an inf. n. or as a a simple subst. (Lh, K.) (TA.) You say also, simoEu A^u*uniY fulaAnFA yaquwlu *`lika : see samoEN . ― -b2- Also i. q. sourceDefinition: : see saAmiEN , in six places. ― -b2- It is also syn. with musomiEN [ Making to hear; &c.]. (S, K.) Az remarks its being wonderful that persons should explain it as having this meaning in order to avoid the assigning to God the attribute of hearing, since that attribute is assigned to Him in more than one place in the Kur-án, though his hearing is not like the hearing of his creatures: he, however, adds, I do not deny that, in the language of the Arabs, smyE may be syn. with saAmiEN or musomiEN ; but it is mostly syn. with saAmiEN , like as EaliymN is with EaAlimN , and qadiyrN with qaAdirN . (TA.) ― -b3- Also [ Made to hear; or] told; applied to a man. sourceDefinition: [pass. part. n. of 4, q. v.]. waA@somaEo gayora musomaEK , in the Kur [iv. 48], means [ And hear thou without being made to hear; i. e.] mayest thou not be made to hear: (Ibn-'Arafeh, K:) or mayest thou not hear, (Akh, S, Bd, Jel,) by reason of deafness, or of death; (Bd;) said by way of imprecation: (Az, Er-Rághib:) or hear thou without being made to hear speech which thou wouldest approve: or not being made to hear what is disliked; accord. to which explanation, it is said hypocritically: or hear thou speech which thou wilt not be made [ really ] to hear; because thine ear will be averse from it; accord. to which explanation, what follows the verb is an objective complement: or hear thou without having thine invitation assented to: (Bd:) or without having what thou sayest accepted. (Mujáhid, K.)

definition: (assumed tropical:) Striped;

sourceDefinition: , aor. , (K, TA,) inf. n. $abokN ; (TA;) and ↓ $b~khu , inf. n. ta$obiykN ; He infixed, (K, TA,) and inserted, (TA,) one part thereof into another, or parts thereof into others: (K, TA:) so in the M: (TA:) [but the latter more usually signifies he infixed, and inserted, many parts thereof into others: (see 8, first sentence, respecting its quasipass.:) and hence, he made it reticulated, retiform, like a net; and like a lattice, or trellis, or grating, or cage: and both signify also he made it commingled in its several parts, intricate, complicated, perplexed, or confused; either properly, as when the object is a fabric, or anything made by art, or created; or tropically, as when the object is ideal:] primarily, (TA,) Al$~aboku signifies AlxaloTu [i. e. the mixing together a thing or things]; and [implies] Alt~adaAxulu [i. e. the entering of one part of a thing into another part, or of parts of a thing or things into other parts; or the being intermixed, or intermingled ]. (S, TA.) Hence, AlA^aSaAbiEi ↓ ta$obiyku , (S, TA,) meaning The inserting of some of the fingers [i. e. those of one hand ] amid the other fingers; (Msb, TA;) which it is forbidden to do in prayer: (TA:) one says, [ $b~k A^aSaAbiEahu , or] $b~k bayona A^aSaAbiEihi , He inserted, or interserted, his fingers together [ so as to conjoin his two hands ]: (MA:) or, as some interpret it, ta$obiyku AlA^aSaAbiEi which is forbidden in prayer is (assumed tropical:) the mixing, and entering, into contentions, or altercations. (TA.) [Hence also,] ↓ kaAnati Alr~iyHu $ab~akatohumo , a saying of Mohammad Ibn-Zekereeyà, meaning (assumed tropical:) The wind had made them like the $abakap [or net ], in the interkniting and contraction of the limbs. (Mgh.) ― -b2- $abakahu Eanohu , inf. n. as above, means (assumed tropical:) He, or it, diverted him, or occupied him so as to divert him, from him, or it. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: The $arakap [meaning net ] of the Say~aAd [i. e. fisherman, and fowler or sportsman ]; (K;) the miSoyadap , (Lth, O, TA,) or instrument of AlS~ayod , (S,) that is used in the water [i. e. for catching fish ] and on the land [i. e. for catching fowls or wild animals ]; (Lth, O, * TA;) applied by some peculiarly to the miSoyadap of the water; (TA;) and ↓ $ub~aAkN signifies the same: (K:) pl. of the former $ibaAkN (S, Msb, K) and $abakaAtN (Msb) and [coll. gen. n.] ↓ $abakN : (Msb, K:) and the pl. of ↓ $ub~aAkN is $abaAbiyku (K.) ― -b2- And A certain thing for the head; (Lth, O;) [ a small net, for the head, a veil of net-work, in order that the face may not be known. (Golius, on the authority of Meyd.)] -A2- Also Wells near together, (K, TA,) of which the water is near [ to the mouths ], communicating [app. by filtration ] one with another: so accord. to El-Kutabee: (TA:) or wells separate, one from another: (M and L in art. mA^d :) and, (K,) or as some say, (TA,) wells (O, K, TA) that are open to view, (K, TA,) dug in a rugged place, of the depth of the stature of a man, and twice and thrice that measure, in which the rain-water becomes retained: so called because of their mutual proximity, and confusedness: a single one of them is not called $abakapN ; for this is only a name for a plural number; but the pl. $ibaAkN is applied to aggregates thereof in sundry places: (O, TA:) or $ibaAkN , (S,) or $abakapN , (Msb,) signifies wells that are numerous and near together in a [ tract of ] land; (S, Msb;) form Ai$otibaAku Aln~ujuwmi : (Msb:) or, accord. to As, $abakapN signifies wells, or other pits or hollows dug in the ground, that are numerous; and the pl. is $ibaAkN . (IDrd, O.) ― -b2- And A [ tract of ] land in which are many wells, (K, TA,) not tracts that exude water and produce salt, nor such as give growth to plants, or herbage: (TA:) or [the pl.] $ibaAkN signifies places, of the earth, that are not such as exude water and produce salt, nor such as give growth to plants, or herbage; such as the $ibaAk of El-Basrah. (Lth, O.) ― -b3- And The burrow of the [field-rat called] jura* : (K, TA:) or the burrows thereof, which are near together: pl. $ibaAkN . (TA.)

sourceDefinition: [ A condition; a term; a stipulation; said to signify] the imposition of a thing as obligatory [ upon a person ], and the taking it upon oneself as such, in a sale and the like; (K;) [but this is a loose explanation, as is observed in the TK; the meaning being a thing imposed upon a person as obligatory, and taken upon oneself as such: in the S, it is merely said to be well known:] and ↓ $ariyTapN signifies the same: (S, Msb, K:) pl. of the former, $uruwTN : (S, Msb, K:) and of the latter, $araAy^iTu . (Msb, TA.) It is said in a trad., laA yajuwzu $aroTaAni fiY bayoEK [ Two conditions in a sale are not allowable ]; as when one says, “ I sell to thee this garment, or piece of cloth, for ready money for a deenár, and on credit for two deenárs. ” (TA.) And it is said in a prov., Al$~aroTu A^amolaku Ealayoka A^amo laka (TA) The condition is most valid, or binding, [whether it be against thee or in thy favour: ] (Mgh in art. mlk :) relating to the keeping of conditions between brothers. (Sgh, TA.) [ $aroTN also relates to other things beside sales and the like: for instance, you say, $aroTu AlmaSodari ka*aA waka*aA , meaning What is required to justify the application of the term mSdr is such a thing, and such a thing. ] -A2- $aroTaA nahorK The two banks of a river. (TA.) ― -b2- [The pl.] $uruwTN also signifies Roads leading in different directions. (TA.) -A3- See also $araTN , in two places.

definition: A sign, token, or mark, (S, Msb, K,) which men appoint between them;
sourceDefinition: A sign, token, or mark, (S, Msb, K,) which men appoint between them; (TA;) as also ↓ $aroTN : (TA:) pl. of the former, A^a$oraATN . (Msb, K.) And hence, (Msb,) A^a$oraATu Als~aAEapi The signs of the resurrection, or of the time thereof; (S, Msb, TA;) mentioned in the Kur [xlvii. 20]: or the small events prior thereto, which men deny: (El-Khattábee:) or the means thereof, exclusive of the main circumstances thereof, and of the event itself. (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence also,] Al$~araTaAni The two stars [a and b] which are the two horns of Aries; (S, K, Kzw;) the brighter whereof is called Aln~aATiHu ; (Kzw;) [ and the other, Aln~aToHu ;] the First Mansion of the Moon: (Kzw:) to- wards the north of them is a small star which some of the Arabs reckon with those two, saying that it ( namely this mansion, K) consists of three stars, and calling them AlA^a$oraATu : (S, K:) IAar mentions an instance of the use of the sing., Al$~araTu ; but the dual is more approved, and more commonly known: (TA:) the two stars above mentioned are the first asterism of the spring. (ISd, Z.) [See manaAzilu Alqamari , in art. nzl .] Hassán Ibn-Thábit says, fiY nadaAmaY biyDi Alwujuwhi kiraAmK nub~ihuwA baEoda hajoEapi AlA^a$oraATi meaning [ Among fair-faced, generous cup-companions, roused from sleep after ] the setting of the A$rAT : though another meaning, which see below, has been assigned to the last word. (Sgh.) ― -b3- And hence, (ISd, Z,) $araTN also signifies (assumed tropical:) The beginning of a thing; (ISd, * Z, * K;) as also ↓ mi$oraATN : (Ibn-'Abbád, K:) pl. of the former, A^a$oraATN , which is applied to the beginnings of any event that happens because the $araTaAn are the first asterism of the spring: (ISd, Z:) the pl. of ↓ m$rAT in the sense here expl. is ma$aAriyTu . (K.) Hence, accord. to some, A^a$oraATu Als~aAEapi , expl. above. (TA.) -A2- The refuse, (S, Msb, K, TA,) such as the galled in the back, and the emaciated, (TA,) and the young, (K,) and the bad, (A'Obeyd,) of camels or the like, (S, K,) or of goats, (Msb,) or of goats also: (S:) used alike as sing. and pl. and masc. and fem.: and applied particularly to the young of camels, as a pl. and as a sing.: also, to a she-camel and to a he-camel: and to such, of camels, as is brought, or driven, from one place to another for sale; as the aged she-camel, and the camel that is galled in the back: (TA:) also the same, not ↓ $aroTN as in the K, [without restriction of its application,] low, base, vile, or mean; (K, * TA;) and so ↓ A^a$oraTu : (TA:) pl. A^a$oraATN , (S, K,) and pl. pl. A^a$aAriyTu . (S,* TA.) You say, Alganamu A^a$oraATu AlmaAli [ Sheep, or goats, are the refuse, or meanest sort, of beasts that people possess ]. (S.) And $araTN is also applied to men; (S, TA;) $araTu Aln~aAsi signifying The refuse, or lowest or basest or meanest sort, pf mankind or people. (TA.) definition: A thing which one has made a condition.

(TA.)

sourceDefinition: , and $akarahu , (S, Mgh, K,) but the former is the more chaste, (S,) and the latter is for $akara niEomatahu , (A,) aor. , (TA,) inf. n. $ukorN and $ukoraAnN (S, A, * Msb, K) and $ukuwrN , (S, K) which last, in the Kur lxxvi. 9, may be either an inf. n. or pl. of $ukorN [used as a simple subst.], (S,) He thanked him; or praised, eulogized, or commended, him, for a benefit or benefits: (S:) he was grateful, or thankful, to him; or he acknowledged his beneficence, and spoke of it largely: (S, * K: [but in the S, the verb in the former sense has $ukorN only for its inf. n., and it is implied that in the latter sense it has for its inf. n. only $ukoraAnN , as will be seen below:]) and $akara lil~`hi , and $akara A@ll~`ha , (Lh, Msb, K,) which latter is less common than the former, and even disallowed by As in prose, though allowed by him in verse, (Msb,) and $akara biA@ll~`hi and $akara niEomapa A@ll~`hi , and $akara biniEomapi A@ll~`hi , (Lh, K,) and $akara lil~`hi niEomatahu , (A,) inf. n. $ukorN and $ukoraAnN (Msb) [and $ukuwrN ], He thanked, or praised, God for his beneficence: (A:) he was grateful, or thankful, to God; or acknowledged his beneficence, and spoke of it largely: (K:) he acknowledge the beneficence of God, and acted in the manner incumbent on him in rendering Him obedience and abstaining from disobedience; so that $ukor is in word and in deed: (Msb:) and lahu ↓ ta$ak~ara signifies the same as $akara lahu : (S, A, Msb, K:) you say, lahu maA SanaEa ↓ ta$ak~arotu [ I thanked him, &c., for what he did ]: (A:) and lahu balaA='ahu ↓ t$k~r [ He was grateful to Him, &c., i. e. to God, for his probation ]: (K:) and A^a$okuru A_ilayoka niEama A@ll~`hi [ I praise to thee, or mention to thee with thanks, the favours of God ]: (L in art. Hmd :) [but there are many explanations of $akara beside those given above: its meanings will be more fully shown by what here follows:] $ukorN is the thanking a benefactor; or praising, eulogizing, or commending, him, (S, A,) for a benefits: (S:) or the being grateful, or thankful; or acknowledging beneficence; and speaking of it largely; and [in the copies of the K, “ or, ” but this is evidently a mistake,] it is only on account of favour received; (K;) and $ukoraAnN is [the same, being] contr. of kuforaAnN : (S:) $ukorN [sometimes] differs from HamodN ; (Msb in art. Hmd ;) for $kr is only on account of favour received; whereas Hmd is sometimes because of favour received, (Th, Az, TA in art. Hmd , and Msb ubi suprà,) and sometimes form other causes; (Th ubi suprà;) [and thus] the latter is of more common application than the former; (S in art. Hmd ;) therefore you do not say $akarotuhu EalaY $ajaAEatihi , but you say Hamidotuhu ElY $jAEth : (Msb ubi suprà:) or $ukorN is more common than HamodN with respect to its kinds and means, and more particular with respect to the objects to which it relates; and the latter is more common with respect to the objects to which it relates, and more particular with respect to the means; for the former is, with the heart, the being humble, or lowly, and submissive; and with the tongue, the act of praising, eulogizing, or commending; and acknowledging beneficence; and with the members, the act of obeying, and submitting one's self; and the object to which it relates is the benefactor, exclusively of his essential qualities; therefore one does not say $akaronaA A@ll~`ha EalaY HayaAtihi [ we thanked God for his existence, or praised Him, &c. ]; but He is maHomuwd on that account, like as He is for his beneficence; and $ukorN is also for beneficence: thus HamodN relates to every object to which, as an object, $ukorN relates; but the reverse is not the case: and everything whereby is Hmd , thereby is $kr ; but the reverse is not the case; for the latter is by means of the members, or limbs, and the former is by means of the tongue: $ukorN is of three kinds; with the heart, or mind, which is the forming an [ adequate ] idea of the benefit; and with the tongue, which is the praising, eulogizing, or commending, the benefactor; and with the members, or limbs, which is the requiting the benefit according to its desert: it rests upon five foundations; humility of him who renders it towards him to whom it is rendered; his love of him; his acknowledgment of his benefit; the eulogizing him for it; and his not making use of the benefit in a manner which he [who has conferred it] dislikes: it is also explained as devotion of the heart to love of the benefactor, and of the members to obey him, and the employment of the tongue in mentioning him and eulogizing him: [and there are several other explanations of it which it is unnecessary to add:] some say that it is formed by transposition from ka$orN , the “ act of uncovering, or exposing to view: ” others, that it is from EayonN $akoraY “ a full fountain, or eye; ” accord. to which etymology it would signify the being full of the praise of the benefactor. (B, TA.) ― -b2- $ukorN on the part of God signifies (tropical:) The requiting and commending [a person]: (K:) or (assumed tropical:) the forgiving a man: or (tropical:) the regarding him with content, satisfaction, good will, or favour: and hence, necessarily, (tropical:) the recompensing, or rewarding, him: the saying $akara A@ll~`hu saEoyahu signifies (tropical:) May God recompense, or reward, his work, or labour. (TA.) -A2- $akirato , aor. , (S, K,) inf. n. $akarN , (S,) (tropical:) Her (a camel's) udder became full (S, K, TA) of milk: (S, TA:) or she (a camel) obtained a good share of leguminous herbage, or [ other ] pasturage, and in consequence abounded with milk after having had little milk: (T, TA:) and she (a beast;) became fat, (K, TA,) and her udder became full of milk. (TA.) ― -b2- And $akira (tropical:) He was, or became, liberal, or bountiful, (A, K,) after having been niggardly: (A:) or he gave largely after having been niggardly. (K.) -A3- $akirato said of a tree ( $ajarapN ), (Fr, S, A, K,) aor. , inf. n. $akarN , (S,) (assumed tropical:) It produced, or put forth, what are termed $akiyr , (Fr, S, K,) i. e. what grow around it, from its A^aSol [i. e. root, or base, or stem ]; (S;) as also ↓ A$krt , (Fr, TA,) and ↓ A$tkrt : (Sgh, TA:) or its $akiyr , i. e. sappy twigs or shoots, from its stem, or small leaves beneath the large, became abundant. (A.) ― -b2- And $akira , aor. , (K,) inf. n. $akarN ; (TA;) and $akara , aor. ; and ↓ A$kr ; (K;) said of palm-trees ( naxolN ), (assumed tropical:) They had many $akiyr , i. e. offsets, or suckers. (AHn, K, * TA.) ― -b3- And $akara and ↓ A$kr and ↓ A$tkr are all verbs from $kiyrN . (K.) [It is said in the K that these verbs are from $kyr in all of certain significations there mentioned; app. meaning, all that are there mentioned after the next preceding verb: and hence they seem to have the significations here following: ― -b4- said of palmtrees ( naxol ), (assumed tropical:) They put forth leaves around their branches: : ― -b5- and, said of trees in general $ajara , (assumed tropical:) They put forth branches : ― -b6- and (assumed tropical:) They produced bark : ― -b7- and, said of a grape-vine, (assumed tropical:) it grew from a shoot planted: ― -b8- in the TA it seems to be implied that, said of a vine, they signify (assumed tropical:) It put forth long shoots, or upper shoots. ]
