Hmd , and Msb ubi suprà,) and sometimes form other causes; (Th ubi suprà;) [and thus] the latter is of more common application than the former; (S in art. Hmd ;) therefore you do not say $akarotuhu EalaY $ajaAEatihi , but you say Hamidotuhu ElY $jAEth : (Msb ubi suprà:) or $ukorN is more common than HamodN with respect to its kinds and means, and more particular with respect to the objects to which it relates; and the latter is more common with respect to the objects to which it relates, and more particular with respect to the means; for the former is, with the heart, the being humble, or lowly, and submissive; and with the tongue, the act of praising, eulogizing, or commending; and acknowledging beneficence; and with the members, the act of obeying, and submitting one's self; and the object to which it relates is the benefactor, exclusively of his essential qualities; therefore one does not say $akaronaA A@ll~`ha EalaY HayaAtihi [ we thanked God for his existence, or praised Him, &c. ]; but He is maHomuwd on that account, like as He is for his beneficence; and $ukorN is also for beneficence: thus HamodN relates to every object to which, as an object, $ukorN relates; but the reverse is not the case: and everything whereby is Hmd , thereby is $kr ; but the reverse is not the case; for the latter is by means of the members, or limbs, and the former is by means of the tongue: $ukorN is of three kinds; with the heart, or mind, which is the forming an [ adequate ] idea of the benefit; and with the tongue, which is the praising, eulogizing, or commending, the benefactor; and with the members, or limbs, which is the requiting the benefit according to its desert: it rests upon five foundations; humility of him who renders it towards him to whom it is rendered; his love of him; his acknowledgment of his benefit; the eulogizing him for it; and his not making use of the benefit in a manner which he [who has conferred it] dislikes: it is also explained as devotion of the heart to love of the benefactor, and of the members to obey him, and the employment of the tongue in mentioning him and eulogizing him: [and there are several other explanations of it which it is unnecessary to add:] some say that it is formed by transposition from ka$orN , the “ act of uncovering, or exposing to view: ” others, that it is from EayonN $akoraY “ a full fountain, or eye; ” accord. to which etymology it would signify the being full of the praise of the benefactor. (B, TA.) ― -b2- $ukorN on the part of God signifies (tropical:) The requiting and commending [a person]: (K:) or (assumed tropical:) the forgiving a man: or (tropical:) the regarding him with content, satisfaction, good will, or favour: and hence, necessarily, (tropical:) the recompensing, or rewarding, him: the saying $akara A@ll~`hu saEoyahu signifies (tropical:) May God recompense, or reward, his work, or labour. (TA.) -A2- $akirato , aor. , (S, K,) inf. n. $akarN , (S,) (tropical:) Her (a camel's) udder became full (S, K, TA) of milk: (S, TA:) or she (a camel) obtained a good share of leguminous herbage, or [ other ] pasturage, and in consequence abounded with milk after having had little milk: (T, TA:) and she (a beast;) became fat, (K, TA,) and her udder became full of milk. (TA.) ― -b2- And $akira (tropical:) He was, or became, liberal, or bountiful, (A, K,) after having been niggardly: (A:) or he gave largely after having been niggardly. (K.) -A3- $akirato said of a tree ( $ajarapN ), (Fr, S, A, K,) aor. , inf. n. $akarN , (S,) (assumed tropical:) It produced, or put forth, what are termed $akiyr , (Fr, S, K,) i. e. what grow around it, from its A^aSol [i. e. root, or base, or stem ]; (S;) as also ↓ A$krt , (Fr, TA,) and ↓ A$tkrt : (Sgh, TA:) or its $akiyr , i. e. sappy twigs or shoots, from its stem, or small leaves beneath the large, became abundant. (A.) ― -b2- And $akira , aor. , (K,) inf. n. $akarN ; (TA;) and $akara , aor. ; and ↓ A$kr ; (K;) said of palm-trees ( naxolN ), (assumed tropical:) They had many $akiyr , i. e. offsets, or suckers. (AHn, K, * TA.) ― -b3- And $akara and ↓ A$kr and ↓ A$tkr are all verbs from $kiyrN . (K.) sourceDefinition: (tropical:) The shoots that grow around a tree, from its A^aSol [i. e. root, or base, or stem ]: (S:) or sappy twigs or shoots, that grow from the stem of a tree: or small leaves beneath the large: (A:) or fresh and tender twigs or shoots, that grow among such as have become thick and tough: and what grow at, or upon, the A^uSuwl [i. e. roots, or bases, or stems, ] of large trees: or small leaves that grow at, or upon, the root, or base, or stem, of a tree: (IAar, TA:) and offsets, or suckers, or sprouts, of palm-trees: (K:) and the leaves that are around the branches of the palm-tree: (Yaa- koob, K:) and plants, and hair, and feathers, and abundant ostrich-feathers ( EifaA=' , K, TA, in the CK EafA' ), such as are small, growing among such as are large: or the first, of herbage, growing after other herbage that has become dried up and dusty: (K:) and downy hair, or down: and any soft, fine hair: (A:) or hair growing among the plaits: pl. $ukurN : and weak hair: (TA:) and hair at the roots of a horse's mane, (K, TA,) like down, and in the forelock: (TA:) and the hair that is next to the face and the back of the neck: (A, K:) and branches: (AHn, K: [in the CK, wAlguSuwni is erroneously put for wAlguSuwnu :]) and the bark ( liHaA=' ) of trees: pl. $ukurN : (K:) and the pl. also signifies the long shoots of a grape-vine: or its higher, or highest, shoots: (AHn, TA:) and the sing., a grape-vine growing from a planted shoot. (AHn, K, TA.) ― -b2- Also (tropical:) Young men: (A:) or young offspring. (TA, from a trad.) ― -b3- And (tropical:) The young ones of camels: (K, TA:) as being likened to the $akiyr of palm-trees. (TA.)

definition: [mentioned above as an inf.
sourceDefinition: [mentioned above as an inf. n.] is a word of well-known meaning; (S;) Desire, or longing, or yearning, of the soul for a thing; (Er-Rághib, Msb, TA;) [meaning for a thing gratifying to sense: or eager, or intense, desire; particularly for such a thing; for] it has a more intensive signification than A_iraAdapN ; and the intelligent agree in opinion that it is not commendable: (M in art. frs :) [being either lawful or unlawful, it may be rendered as above: or appetite: or appetence: or lust: or carnal lust: ] in the present state of existence, it is of two sorts, SaAdiqapN [i. e. true ], and kaA*ibapN [i. e. false ]; the former being that without which the body becomes in an unsound state, as the $ahowap [or desire &c.] for food on the occasion of hunger; and the latter being that without which the body does not become in an unsound state: and sometimes it is applied to the object of desire &c., or thing desired &c.: (Er-Rághib, TA:) and agreeably with this last explanation the first of the following pls. is used in the Kur iii. 12: (Ksh, Bd, Jel:) sometimes also it is applied to the faculty to which a thing is made an object of desire &c.: (Er-Rághib, TA:) [also, to the gratification of venereal lust; thus in the K in art. $fr ; see $afirato and $afirapN :] the pl. is $ahawaAtN (Msb, TA) and A^a$ohiyapN and $uhFY ; the last mentioned by AHei, and a rare instance of a pl. of the measure fuEalN from a sing. of the measure faEolapN having an infirm letter for its last radical, like juhFY pl. of jahowapN [and like qurFY pl. of qaroyapN ]. (TA.) [ Al$~ahowataAni means The two appetites, that of the stomach and that of the generative organ. ] Al$~ahowapu Alxafiy~apu [ The latent desire &c.] mentioned in a trad. is said to be any act of disobedience which one conceives in his mind, and upon which he resolves: or one's seeing a beautiful young woman, and lowering his eyes, then looking with his heart, and imaging her to his mind, and so tempting himself. (JM.) [ $ahowapu AlT~iyni , lit. The longing for clay, is app. used as a general term for malacia: see Hum~aADN .]

[ Al$~ahowataAni means The two appetites, that of the stomach and that of the generative organ. ] Al$~ahowapu Alxafiy~apu [ The latent desire &c.] mentioned in a trad. is said to be any act of disobedience which one conceives in his mind, and upon which he resolves: or one's seeing a beautiful young woman, and lowering his eyes, then looking with his heart, and imaging her to his mind, and so tempting himself. (JM.) [ $ahowapu AlT~iyni , lit. The longing for clay, is app. used as a general term for malacia: see Hum~aADN .]

sourceDefinition: , aor. ya$iyEu , (S, O, Msb, K,) inf. n. $uyuwEN (O, Msb, K) and $ayoEuwEapN (S, O, K) and $ayoEN (K) and $ayaEaAnN and ma$aAEN , (O, K, the last, in the CK, ma$aAEap ,) said of information, an announcement, a piece of news, or a narrative, or story, (TA,) or of a thing, (O, Msb,) It became spread, published, divulged, revealed, made known, or disclosed; (S, O, K, TA;) or it became apparent, or manifest; (Msb, TA;) fiY Aln~aAsi [ among the people ]; so as to reach every one, becoming equally known by the people, not known by some exclusively of others. (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence, app.,] $AE , aor. as above, said of a thing, signifies also (assumed tropical:) It became scattered, or dispersed; like $aE~a . (TA in art. $E .) You say, $AE All~abanu fiY AlmaA='i , (Msb,) or $AEt qaTorapN mina All~abani fiY AlmaA='i , and ↓ t$y~Et , (TA,) (assumed tropical:) The milk, (Msb,) or the drop of milk, (TA,) became dispersed in the water, (Msb, TA,) and mixed: (Msb:) and fiyhi ↓ $ay~aEa likewise signifies it became dispersed in it. (TA.) And $AE Al$~ayobu , inf. n. $ayoEN and $iyaAEN and $ayaEaAnN and $uyuwEN and $uyuwEapN and ma$iyEN , (tropical:) Whiteness of the hair, or hoariness, appeared, and became scattered: and $AE fiyhi Al$~ayobu , inf. n. as above, (tropical:) Whiteness of the hair, or hoariness, spread upon him; as also ↓ t$y~Ehu [or t$y~E fiyhi , agreeably with what has been said above]. (TA.) And $AE AlS~adoEu fiY Alz~ujaAjapi (assumed tropical:) The crack spread, and became dispersed, in the glass, or glass vessel. (Th, TA.) And AlA_ibilu ↓ t$AyEt (assumed tropical:) The camels became scattered, or dispersed; or they scattered, or dispersed, themselves. (TA.) -A2- As trans. by means of bi : see 4, in two places. -A3- [It is also trans. by itself.] $aAEakumu Als~alaAmu is like the saying Ealayokumu Als~alaAmu [ Safety, or peace, &c., be, or light and abide, on you ]; (S, O, K;) but is only said by a man to his companions when he desires to quit them: (S, O:) or it means [ may safety, &c.,] follow you: (O, K:) or, not quit you: (K:) whence, (TA,) one says also $aAEaka Alxayoru may prosperity not quit thee; and in like manner Lebeed says of praise ( HamodN ): (O, TA:) [and J says that] $AEhu , inf. n. $iyaAEN , signifies he, or it, followed him: (S:) or $AEkm AlslAm , (Yoo, O, K,) aor. ya$aAEukum , inf. n. $ayoEN , (Yoo, O,) means [ may safety, &c.,] fill you: (Yoo, O, K:) [app. from what next follows.] ― -b2- One says also $iEotu AlA_inaA='a , (K, TA,) aor. A^a$iyEuhu , inf. n. $ayoEN , (TA,) I filled the vessel. (K, TA.)

definition: -A2- $y~E said of a pastor, He blew in the reed-pipe [ called $iyaAE , by means of which the camels are called together ].
sourceDefinition: : see 1. -A2- $y~E said of a pastor, He blew in the reed-pipe [ called $iyaAE , by means of which the camels are called together ]. (Lth, K, TA.) ― -b2- $y~E biAlA_ibili He (a pastor) called to the camels, whereupon they followed one another; (Msb;) in [some of] the copies of the K, i. q. A$A' bhA , [in the CK Aa$AbahA ,] but correctly bihaA ↓ A^a$aAEa , (TA,) which means he called to the camels, (K in another part of the art., and TA,) when some of them remained, or lagged, behind: (TA:) and [in like manner] biA_ibilihi ↓ $AyE , (S, K,) inf. n. mu$aAyaEapN and $iyaAEN , (S,) he (a pastor, S) shouted and called to his camels, (S, K,) when some of them remained, or lagged, behind: (S:) or $y~E A_ibilahu he (a pastor) called out among his camels, whereupon they went along, following one another: (Mgh:) and $y~E Alganama he urged on the sheep, or goats, (K, * TA,) because of their lagging behind, (TA,) in order that they might follow the others. (K, TA.) [The last two phrases are app. from the second of the explanations here following.] ― -b3- $y~Ehu , inf. n. ta$oyiyEN , also signifies He sent, or sent on, him, or it. (TA.) ― -b4- And He made him, or it, to follow. (TA.) ― -b5- [And He made it to be followed by another thing.] One says, $ay~aEotu ramaDaAna bisit~K mino $aw~aAlK [or rather bisit~apK ] (assumed tropical:) I made [the fasting of] Ramadán to be followed by [the fasting of] six [days] of Showwál expl. by A^atobaEotuhu bihaA [a well-known phrase, of frequent occurrence, but one which I have not found in any of the lexicons, except in explanations; the approved phrase used in its stead being A^atobaEotuhu A_iy~aAhaA , lit. meaning “ I made them to follow it; ” this being virtually the same as “ I made it to be followed by them ”]: (Msb:) [and in like manner, the elliptical phrase] $y~E ramaDaAna , (K,) or $y~E $ahora ramaDaAna , (O, TA,) means He fasted after Rama- dán, or the month of Ramadán, six days; (O, K, TA;) i. e. A^atobaEahu bihaA . (TA.) ― -b6- $ay~aEotuhu Einoda raHiylihi (Lth, * S, O, Msb, K *) I went forth with him (Lth, O, Msb, K) on the occasion of his departure, (O, Msb,) namely, a guest, (Msb,) in order to bid him farewell, and to conduct him to his place of alighting, [app. meaning, to his first place of alighting, ] (Lth, O, K,) or to show honour, or courtesy, to him; and I bade him farewell: (Msb:) or $y~E AlD~ayofa signifies he followed the guest [app. on the occasion of his departure, in order to bid him farewell, &c.]: (Mgh:) or $y~Ehu Einoda raHiylihi he went forth with him on the occasion of his departure, desiring to cheer him by his company to some place: and ↓ $AyEhu signifies the same. (TA.) ― -b7- [ $y~Ehu sometimes signifies He followed him, not coming up with him, but always going behind him ]. See Almu$ay~iEapu , voce mu$ay~aEN . ― -b8- [And He followed, or imitated, him; conformed, agreed, or complied, with him; like $aAyaEahu ]. See 3, in three places. ― -b9- $y~E fulaAnFA (tropical:) He encouraged such a one, and emboldened him, (O, K, TA,) and strengthened him. (TA.) One says, fulaAnN yu$ay~iEuhu EalaY *`lika (tropical:) Such a one strengthens him to do that. (TA.) And $ay~aEa h`*aA bih`*aA (assumed tropical:) He strengthened this with this. (TA.) ― -b10- $y~Ehu Aln~aAra (tropical:) He threw, or put, firewood upon the fire to make it blaze or flame, burn up, or burn brightly or fiercely. (ISk, S, K, TA.) ― -b11- And $y~Ehu biAln~aAri (assumed tropical:) He burned him, or it, with fire. (S, K, TA.) Of anything that has been burned, one says, $uy~iEa . (TA.)

definition: A certain tree, (O, K,) below the stature of a man, having knotted, or jointed, rods, and small, dark-red blossoms, smaller than the jasmine: (O:) the bees feed upon it;

(O.)

definition: A separate, or distinct, party, or sect, (O, K, TA,) of men: this is the primary signification: so called from their agreeing together, and following one another: or, accord.
sourceDefinition: A separate, or distinct, party, or sect, (O, K, TA,) of men: this is the primary signification: so called from their agreeing together, and following one another: or, accord. to some, the Y is originally w , and it is from $uw~aEa qawomahu , which means “ he collected his people or party: ” (TA:) the followers and assistants (S, O, Msb, K) of a man: (S, O, K:) any people that have combined in, or for, an affair: (Msb, TA:) accord. to Az, persons who follow, or conform with, one another, [ though ] not all of them agreeing together: (TA:) and any assistant and partisan of a man: (O, TA:) [for] the word is applied to one and to two and to a pl. number and to the male and to the female, (K, TA,) without variation: (TA:) the pl. is $iyaEN and A^a$oyaAEN , (S, * O, Msb, K,) the latter a pl. pl.; (Msb;) and the former is applied to any people, or party, whose affair, or case, is one, who follow one another's opinion. (S.) The saying, in the Kur [xxxiv. last verse], kamaA fuEila biA^a$oyaAEihimo mino qabolu means As was done with the likes of them, of the same persuasion as they, of the peoples that have gone before: (S, * TA:) and similar to this is the saying in the Kur liv. 51. (TA.) ― -b2- Afterwards, Al$~iyEapu became a name of A particular party [or sect ]; (Msb, K;) being predominantly applied to all who took as their friends, or lords, 'Alee and the people of his house: (K:) those who followed 'Alee, saying that he was the [ rightful ] Imám after the Apostle of God, and believing that the office of Imám should not depart from him and his descendants: (KT:) they are an innumerable people, who are innovators; the extravagant zealots among them are the Imámeeyek, who revile the Two Sheykhs [ Aboo-Bekr and 'Omar ]; and the most extravagant of them call the Two Sheykhs disbelievers: some of them rise to the pitch of [ that misbelief which is termed ] Alz~anodaqap [q. v.]. definition: The thing with which a she-camel's udder is bound: (M, K:) the string which is tied over the she-camel's udder and over the [ piece of wood called ] tawodiyap , in order that her young one may not suck her;
sourceDefinition: The thing with which a she-camel's udder is bound: (M, K:) the string which is tied over the she-camel's udder and over the [ piece of wood called ] tawodiyap , in order that her young one may not suck her; (S;) and in order that it may not make any impression upon her, they smear her teats with fresh [dung of the kind called] baEar : (TA:) or a piece of rag which is bound upon the she-camel's teats, in order that her young one may not such her: (Msb:) pl. A^aSir~apN . (M, A, K.) It is a custom of the Arabs to bind the SrAr upon the udders of their milch camels when they send them to pasture by themselves; and when they return in the evening, they loose the ASr~p , and milk. (IAth.) ― -b2- [Hence,] jaEalotu duwna fulaAnK SiraArFA (tropical:) I put an obstruction, or obstacle, in the way of such a one. (A.) -A2- Also Elevated places over which the water does not come. (S.)

sourceDefinition: (S, M, A, Msb, K) and ↓ SaAruwrapN (S, M, Msb, K) and ↓ SaruwrN and ↓ SaAruwrN (M, K) and ↓ SaraArapN (S, M, K) and ↓ SaruwriY~N (S, M, Msb, K) and ↓ SaAruwriY~N (M) or ↓ SaAruwraA='u , (Sgh, K,) the last like EaA$uwraA='u , mentioned on the authority of Ks, (TA,) A man who has not performed the pilgrimage to Mekkeh: (S, M, A, Msb, K:) so called from Sar~N , signifying the “ act of confining, withholding, hindering, or preventing; ” (TA;) or because the person so called refrains from expending of his property in pilgrimage: (Msb:) you say also, AimoraA^apN SaruwrapN a woman who has not performed the pilgrimage to Mekkeh: (S, Msb:) pl. ↓ SaraArN and ↓ SaraArapN : (K:) [or, rather, the former is a coll. gen. n., of which SaraArapN is the n. of un.; and the latter is a quasi-pl. n., like SaHaAbapN , as well as n. un. of SaraArN :] Fr cites, from certain of the Arabs, ↓ SaraArN as used collectively; and one of the number is termed ↓ SaraArapN : (S:) each of the forms ending with the relative Y receives the dual and pl. and fem. inflections: and accord. to IAar, the forms preceding those receive also the dual and pl. inflections: (M, * TA:) and some say that SawaAriyru is pl. of ↓ SaAruwrapN : (TA:) or ↓ SaAruwrapN and ↓ SaAruwrN , (M,) or SaruwrapN , (Lh, S, M, A, Msb,) as occurring in the poetry of En-Nábighah, (Yaakoob, S,) not used without p , (Lh, M,) or all the sing. forms above mentioned, (K,) signify one who has not married: (M, A, K:) or who has not had intercourse with women: as though he had determined ( A^aSar~a ) upon relinquishing them: (Yaakoob, S, Msb: *) applied in like manner to a woman, and to a plurality of persons: (M, K:) the p in SaruwrapN applied to a man and to a woman is not to denote the fem. gender, but to give the utmost intensiveness to the signification. (IJ, M.) ― -b2- It is said in a trad., laA Saruwrapa fiY AlA_isolaAmi , (S, M,) meaning, accord. to A 'Obeyd, There is no abstinence from intercourse with women in El-Islám: (M, TA:) i. e., no one should say, I will not marry: (TA:) thus he makes Srwrp a noun signifying an accident: but it is better known as an epithet: (M:) and IAth says that the meaning is, he who slays another in the Haram [or sacred territory of Mekkeh] shall be slain: his saying, “ I am a Srwrp ; I have not performed the pilgrimage, and I know not the sacredness of the Haram ; ” shall not be accepted of him: for in the Time of Ignorance, the Kaabeh was a place of refuge. (TA.)

definition: [ An idol: or an idol of a particular kind: ] a wavan : (S:) or a wavan that is worshipped: (K:) or a wavan that is made of stones, and of wood;
sourceDefinition: [ An idol: or an idol of a particular kind: ] a wavan : (S:) or a wavan that is worshipped: (K:) or a wavan that is made of stones, and of wood; as is said on the authority of I'Ab: (Msb:) or a thing well known, that is carved of wood, and that is made of molten and cast silver and copper or brass: (M; and the like is said in the Msb on the authority of IF:) or the Snm is made of metals that melt; and the wvn is made of stone or of wood: (Msb:) or, accord. to Hishám ElKelbee, the former is made of wood or of gold or of silver or of other metal; and the latter, of stones: or, accord. to Ibn-'Arafeh and El-Fihree, the former is an image; and the latter is a shapeless thing: or, as some say, the former is a thing having corporeal from, carved of wood or of stone or of silver, and worshipped; and [the latter (in the TA the Snm , but this I suppose to be a mistake for the wvn ,)] is a incorporeal form: or the former is a thing having the form of a human being; and the latter, a thing having some other form: or the former is a thing having material substance or shape; and the latter, a thing not having material substance or shape: or the former is of stones or other material; and the latter, an embodied form: (TA:) or, accord. to IAth, the latter [?] is anything having corporeal form, made of metal or of wood and stones, like the form of a human being, made, and set up, and worshipped; and the former [?] an incorporeal form: (TA in art. wvn : [from explanations given above, it seems that the reverse of this is the case:]) and Abu-l-'Abbás states, on the authority of IAar, that ↓ SanamapN and naSamapN signify an image ( SuwrapN ) that is worshipped; (TA in the present art.;) each of these two words is thus ( biAlt~aHoriyk ), though it would seem that accord. to the K the latter is naSomapN : (TA in art. nSm :) SanamN (S, K) it is said (S) is an arabicized word, from $aman (S, K) [which is Pers., though SM says,] I know not in what language, for in Pers. it is bt [i. e. buto ]: (TA:) the pl. is A^aSonaAmN ; definition: The herbs, or leguminous plants, became dried up;

definition: as signifying A certain portion of the year is said by ISk to be fem.
sourceDefinition: as signifying A certain portion of the year is said by ISk to be fem.: (TA, voce $itaA='N ; q. v.:) [but by others I find it treated as masc.:] the Sayof as meaning one of the seasons is well known: (M:) Lth says, it is one of the quarters of the year; and is applied by the vulgar to a half of the year [i. e. to the half-year commencing at the vernal equinox; the other half-year being called by them the $itaA=' ]: Az says, it is, with the Arabs, the division which the vulgar in El-'Irák and Khurásán call the rabiyE [i. e. the spring ]; it consists of three months; and the division that next follows it is with the Arabs the qayoZ ; and in it is the jamorap [q. v.] of the qiyoZ ; then, after this, is the division called the xariyf ; and then, after this, the division called the $itaA=' : (TA:) [i. e.] it is the quarter of the year vulgarly called the rabiyE , commencing when the sun enters Aries: but is applied by the vulgar to the qayoZ , which is the [ summer, i. e.] the quarter commencing when the sun enters Cancer: (Msb in art. zmn ; q. v.:) [F says,] the Sayof is the qayoZ [i. e. summer, or the hot season ]; or [the season ] after the rabiyE : (K:) and [Sgh says,] the Sayof is one of the divisions of the year; which is after the rabiyE : (O:) [but unless this explanation in the O denote only a vulgar meaning, and the latter of the two explanations in the K be virtually a repetition, we must suppose that, in each of them, by the rbyE is meant the season of rain thus termed, which ends in March: (see the latter of the two tables which I have inserted voce zamanN :) most probably, I think, both have been faultily transcribed from what here follows; for the S is largely copied in the O, and the S and O are among the principal sources of the K, which generally follows the O when it differs (rightly or wrongly) from the S:] the Sayof is one of the divisions of the year; which is after [ that called ] Alr~abiyEu AlA^aw~alu and before [ that called ] AlqayoZu : (S:) [this admits of two renderings, both of which are correct; namely, the quarter after the season of two months called AlrbyE AlAw~l ( which ends in March ) and before the quarter called AlqyZ ( which is summer ); and also the season of two months after that called AlrbyE AlAw~l and before the similar season called AlqyZ : (see the former of the two tables to which I have referred above:) but probably the latter only was meant by him who first gave. this explanation:] the pl. is A^aSoyaAfN (M, O, K) and SuyuwfN : (M, Msb:) ↓ SayofapN is a more particular term [app. meaning A single Sayof ; (see 2;)]; it is like $atowapN [q. v.]; (O, K;) and its pl. is SiyafN , like bidarN pl. of badorapN . (Fr, O, K.) AlS~ayofa Day~aEoti All~abana is a saying expl. in art. DyE [q. v.]. (O, K.) ― -b2- AlS~ayofu also signifies The rain that comes in the [ season called ] Sayof ; (S, O, Msb, K;) [see, again, the second of the tables to which I have referred above, and see also nawoN ;] and (O, K) so ↓ AlS~ay~ifu ; (M, O, K;) also signifying the herbage thereof: (M:) or, (K,) accord. to Lth, (O,) the latter signifies the rain that falls after the division [a mistake for the rain ] called the rabiyE ; (O, K;) and so the former; (K;) and it is also called ↓ AlS~ayofiY~u ; (O, K;) which likewise signifies the herbage thereof. (TA.) Hence the prov., relating to the completing of the performance of a needful affair, tamaAmu Alr~abiyEi AlS~ayofu [ The completion of the rain called the rbyE is that called the Syf ]: for the rain called the rbyE is the first rain, and the Syf is that which is [next] after it. (TA.) ― -b3- A=yapu AlS~ayofi is [ A verse ] in the end ( A=xir ) of suwrapu Aln~isaA='i [ the 4 th chapter of the Kur-án, but which verse I know not], mentioned in a tradition. (TA.) -A2- Also The female of the buwm [or owl ]. (Kr, M.)

A_iDoEaAfN ; (S, Msb;) all signify the same; (S, K;) i. e. He doubled it, or made it double, or two-fold; (O, K;) [and trebled it, or made it treble, or three-fold; and redoubled it, or made it several-fold, or manyfold; i. e. multiplied it; for] Kh says, Alt~aDoEiyfu signifies the adding to a thing so as to make it double, or two-fold; or more [i. e. treble, or threefold; and several-fold, or many-fold ]; (S, O, Msb;) and so AlA_iDoEaAfu , and AlmuDaAEafapu ; (S, Msb;) and ↓ DaEafahu , without teshdeed, signifies the same as DAEfhu . (Ham p. 257.) The saying, in the Kur [xxxiii. 30], yuDaAEafo lahaA AlEa*aAbu DiEofayoni , (Mgh, O, K,) in which AA read ↓ yuDaE~afo , (TA,) accord. to AO, (Mgh, O,) means, The punishment shall be made to her three punishments; (Mgh, O, K;) for, he says, she is to be punished once; and when the punishment is doubled twofold, [or is repeated twice,] the one becomes three: (TA:) he adds, (O,) and the tropical meaning of yuDaAEafo ( majaAzu yuDaAEafo [for which majAzN yuDaAEafu is erroneously put in the CK]) is two things' being added to a thing so that it becomes three: (O, K:) but Az disapproves this, saying that it is peculiar to the tropical and the common conventional speech, whereas the skilled grammarians state the meaning to be, she shall be punished with twice the like of the punishment of another; (Mgh;) [so that it may be rendered the punishment shall be doubled to her, made two-fold; and in like manner] Ibn-'Arafeh explains it as meaning she shall have two shares of punishment. (O.) fayuDaAEifuhu lahu A^aDoEaAfFA kaviyrapF [ And He will multiply it to him many-fold, or, as some read, fayuDaAEifahu that He may multiply it, ] is another phrase occurring in the Kur [ii. 246]. (O, TA.) And one says, Alv~awaAba liloqawomi ↓ A^aDoEafotu [ I doubled, or multiplied, the recompense to the people, or party ]. (Msb.) And Alqawomu ↓ A^uDoEifa The people, or party, had a doubling, or multiplying, [of their recompense, &c.,] made to them; (Msb;) [and so, app., A^aDoEafuwA ; (see muDoEifN ;)] i. q. DuwEifa lahumo . (S, O, K.)

(Kull p. 56.) ― -b3- [In the CK, a signification belonging to DuEof is assigned to DaEof .]

definition: signifies The like of the thing, (AO, Zj, S, O, Msb, K, TA,) that doubles it ( yuDoEifuhu );
sourceDefinition: signifies The like of the thing, (AO, Zj, S, O, Msb, K, TA,) that doubles it ( yuDoEifuhu ); (Zj, TA;) and DiEofaAhu , twice the like of it; (AO, S, O, Msb, K;) and A^aDoEaAfuhu , the likes of it: (S, Msb:) AlD~iEofu in the [proper] language of the Arabs means the like: this is the original signification: (Az, Msb:) and (K, TA, but in CK “ or, ”) then, by a later [and conventional] usage, (Az, Msb,) the like and more, the addition being unlimited: (Az, Msb, K:) one says, h`*aA DiEofu h`*aA i. e. This is the like of this: and h`*aAni DiEofaAhu i. e. These two are twice the like of it: and it is allowable in the language of the Arabs to say, h`*aA DiEofuhu meaning This is twice the like [i. e. the double ] of it, and thrice the like [i. e. the treble ] of it, [and more, ] because the DiEof is an unlimited addition: (Az, Msb: [and the like is said in the O, on the authority of Az:]) and one says, laka DiEofuhu meaning Thou shalt have twice the like of it, (Zj, O, K,) using the sing. form, though the dual form is better, (Zj, O,) and meaning also thrice the like of it, and more without limit: (K:) and AlAivonaAni DiEofu AlwaAHidi [i. e. AlAvnAn is the double of AlwAHd ]: (M and K in art. vnY :) and if one say in his will, A^aEoTuwhu DiEofa naSiybi waladiY , twice the like of the share of his child is given to him; and if he say DiEofayohi , thrice the like thereof is given to him; so that if the share of the son be a hundred, he [the legatee] is given two hundred in the former case, and three hundred in the latter case; for the will is made to accord with the common conventional language, not with the niceties of the [proper] language: (Az, Msb: [and the like is said, but less fully, in the Mgh:]) the pl. is A^aDoEaAfN only. (TA.) A_i*FA laA^a*aqonaAka DiEofa AlHayaApi waDiEofa AlmamaAti , in the Kur [xvii. 77], means DiEofa AlEa*aAbi Hay~FA wamay~itFA , (S,) or DiEofa Ea*aAbi AlHayaApi waDiEofa Ea*aAbi AlmumaAti , (O, Jel,) i. e. [ In that case we would assuredly have made thee to taste ] the like [or, as some explain it, the double ] of the punishment of others in the present world and [ the like or the double thereof ] in the world to come: (Jel:) [Sgh adds, app. on the authority of Ibn-'Arafeh,] the meaning is, the punishment of others should be made two-fold, or more, ( yuDaAEaf ,) to thee, because thou art a prophet. (O.) In the saying, faA^uwlaAy^ika lahumo jazaA='u A@lD~iEofi bimaA EamiluwA , in the Kur [xxxiv. 36], by AlD~iEofi is meant AlA^DoEaAfi [i. e. For these shall be the recompense of the likes for what they have done ]; and it is most properly held to denote ten of the likes thereof, because of the saying in the Kur [vi. 161], “ Whoso doth that which is good, for him shall be ten of the likes thereof. ” (O.) In the saying, faA=tihimo Ea*aAbFA DiEofFA , in the Kur [vii. 36], by DiEofFA is meant muDaAEafFA [i. e. Therefore do Thou recompense them with a doubled, or a double, punishment ]: Ea*aAbN DiEofN meaning a punishment as though doubled, one part of it upon another. (TA.) ― -b2- A^aDoEaAfu AlkitaAbi means (tropical:) The interspaces of the lines, (S, O, K, TA,) or of the margin, (S, O,) or and of the margins, (K, TA,) of the writing, or book: (S, O, K, TA:) so in the saying, waq~aEa fulaAnN fiY A^aDoEaAfi kitaAbihi (tropical:) [ Such a one made an entry of a note or postil or the like, or entries of notes &c., in the interspaces of the lines, &c., of his writing, or book ]: (S, O, TA:) and ↓ taDaAEiyfu AlkitaAbi signifies the same as A^aDoEaAfuhu . (TA.) ― -b3- And A^aDoEaAfu Aljasadi (assumed tropical:) The limbs, members, or organs, ( A^aEoDaA=' ,) of the body: (O, K:) or the bones thereof: (AA, K:) or the bones thereof having flesh upon them: (TA:) sing. DiEofN . (K.) Hence the saying of Ru-beh, waA@ll~`hu bayona Alqalobi waAlA^aDoEaAfi (assumed tropical:) [ And God is between the heart and the limbs, &c.]. (TA.) And it is said of Yoonus, [the prophet Jonah,] kaAna fiY A^aDoEaAfi AlHuwti (tropical:) [ He was amid the members of the fish ]. (TA.)

(TA.) ― -b5- The saying of a man who had found a thing dropped on the ground ( wajada luqaTapF ), faEar~afotuhaA DaEiyfFA , means And I made it known in a suppressed, or low, [or weak, ] voice. (Mgh in art. nfr .)

definition: A man whose beast, (S, K, and Mgh in art.
sourceDefinition: A man whose beast, (S, K, and Mgh in art. kfA^ ,) or whose camel, (O,) is weak, (S, Mgh, O, K,) or untractable. (O.) (Mgh in art. kfA^ .) -A2- faA^uwlaAy^ika humu A@lomuDoEifuwna , in the Kur [xxx. 38], means These are they who shall have their recompense doubled, or multiplied: (Az, Bd, TA:) or those who double, or multiply, their recompense (Bd, Jel) and their possessions, (Bd,) by the blessing of their almsgiving: (Bd, Jel: *) but some read AlmuDoEafuwna . (Bd.) ― -b2- AlmuDoEifu also signifies mano fa$ato DayoEatuhu wakavurato [ He whose property has become wide-spread and abundant ]. (Ibn-' Abbád, O, L, K.)

sourceDefinition: A certain small creeping thing, ( duwayob~apN , S, K, TA,) in form like [ the species of lizard, or reptile, called ] A^um~ Hubayon , [see art. Hbn ,] but more slender ( A^aloTafu ) than this latter, that raises its tail like as does the pregnant camel, and, when bidden to grind, by the children of the Arabs of the desert, grinds with itself the ground until it becomes concealed in the soft soil; and one never sees it but in a tract of ground such as is termed bal~uwqap : Az says that ↓ TuHanapN signifies a certain small creeping thing ( dwyb~p ) like the [ beetle called ] juEal ; and that TuHanN is the pl.: [but, properly speaking, the latter is a coll. gen. n., and the former is the n. un.:] As says that it is [ a creature ] smaller than the hedge-hog, that comes into existence in the sands, appearing sometimes, and turning round as though grinding, and then diving [ into the sand ]: (TA: [see also EawaAnapN :]) and, (K,) accord. to Aboo-Kheyreh, (TA,) the TuHan is what is called layovu Eifir~iyna [q. v. in art. Efr ], (K, TA, in the CK layovu Eiforiyna ,) resembling the pistachio-nut, in colour like the dust, that buries itself in the earth. sourceDefinition: a word of well-known meaning, (S, Msb, K, TA,) of which ↓ TaAnN is a dial. var.; (TA;) Clay, earth, mould, soil, or mud: (MA, KL, &c.:) it differs in different layers, or strata, of the earth; the best is the pure, unmixed with sand, remaining after the subsiding of the waters; and the best of this is that of Egypt, which has a peculiar property of preventing plague, or pestilence, and the corruption of water into which it is thrown: it is of several sorts; among which are AlT~iynu Almaxotuwmu [ Terra sigillata, or Lemnian earth ], and AlT~iynu AlA^aromaniY~u [ Armenian bole ], &c.: (TA:) ↓ TiynapN has a more particular signification, (S, Msb,) meaning a piece, or portion, thereof, (K, TA,) [as a piece of clay ] with which a [ writing of the kind termed ] Sak~ and the like are sealed. definition: , (S, Msb, K, &c.
sourceDefinition: , (S, Msb, K, &c.,) aor. , (Msb,) inf. n. ZuhuwrN , (S, Mgh, Msb, K, &c.,) [ It was, or became, outward, exterior, external, extrinsic, or exoteric: and hence,] it appeared; became apparent, overt, open, perceptible or perceived, manifest, plain, or evident; (S, Mgh, Msb, K, TA;) after having been concealed, or latent: (Msb, TA:) and ↓ tZAhr signifies the same. (Har p. 85.) Hence the phrase Zahara liY raA^oYN (assumed tropical:) [ An idea, or opinion, occurred to me ], said when one knows what he did not know before. (Msb.) [And h`*aA maA yaZoharu liY (assumed tropical:) This is what appears to me to be the case, or to be the right way or course; or this is my opinion. ] Zahara AlHamolu , inf. n. as above, means Pregnancy became apparent, or manifest: it is said that this is not the case in less than three months. (Msb.) And it is said in a trad. of 'Áïsheh, kaAna yuSal~iY AlEaSora fiY HujoratiY qabola A^ano taZohara i. e. [ He used to perform the prayer of the afternoon in my chamber ] before it (meaning the sun) became high and apparent: (TA:) or waAl$~amosu fiY HujoratiY lamo taZoharo baEodu i. e. [ when the sun was in my chamber, ] it not having risen high so as to be on the flat roof [thereof]: referring to the Prophet. (O. [But AlEaSora must be a mistranscription for Alfajora , i. e. the prayer of the dawn. ]) The saying in the Kur [xxiv. 31], walaA yubodiyna ziynatahun~a A_il~aA maA Zahara minohaA [which is app. best rendered And that they discover not their ornature except what is external thereof ] has been expl. in seven different ways, most correctly as meaning the clothes: (O, TA:) accord. to 'Áïsheh, it means the bracelet ( Alqulob ) and the ring ( Alfataxap ): and accord. to I'Ab, the hand and the signet-ring and the face. (TA.) ― -b2- Also He went forth, or out, (Mgh, TA,) to the outside of a place. (O, TA.) ― -b3- And He (a bird) migrated, or went down, from one country or region to another: used in this sense by AHn in relation to the vulture, migrating to Nejd. (L.) ― -b4- Zahara Eanohu , said of a vice, or fault, (O, TA,) or a disgrace, (JK, A, O,) (tropical:) It did not cleave to him; (A, O, TA;) it was remote from him; (TA;) it quitted him, or departed from him. (JK.) ― -b5- Zaharotu bihi , (O, TA,) inf. n. ZahorN , (K,) (assumed tropical:) I gloried, or boasted, by reason of it. (O, K * TA.) [Respecting a meaning assigned to Zahara bifulaAnK in the K, see 4.] ― -b6- A^akala Alr~ajulu A^ukolapF Zahara minohaA ZahorapF means (assumed tropical:) [ The man ate some food ] in consequence of which ] he became fat. (TA.) -A2- Zaharahu He mounted it; went, or got, upon it, or upon the top of it; (S, A, * Mgh, O, Msb, K;) as also Zahara Ealayohi ; (O;) namely, a house, (S,) or a house-top, (A, Mgh, O,) and a mountain, (A,) and a wall; (O, Msb;) properly, he became upon its back: (Mgh:) and [in like manner] one says, fulaAnN najodFA ↓ Zah~ara , inf. n. taZohiyrN , Such a one mounted, or went up, upon the high region ( Zahor ) of Nejd. (O.) ― -b2- Hence, (Mgh, Msb,) Zahara Ealayohi (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K) and bihi , (K,) inf. n. ZuhuwrN (Bd in xxiv. 31) and ZahorN also, (Ham p. 301,) He overcame, conquered, subdued, overpowered, or mastered, him; gained the mastery or victory, or prevailed, over him; (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K;) namely, his enemy; (Msb;) and in like manner, [ he conquered, won, achieved, or attained, it, i. e.] a thing. (O, TA.) [The saying fulaAnN laA yaZoharu Ealayohi A^aHadN is expl. in the L and TA by the words AY lA yasolam , and said to be tropical: but Ibr D thinks that the correct reading is lA yusal~imu , from Alt~asoliymu ; and that it is said of one who will not give up, or resign, what is in his hand; so that the meaning is, (tropical:) Such a one is a person whom no one will overcome in respect of that which he holds in his possession. ] ― -b3- And [hence also] Zahara Ealayohi , (Msb, TA,) inf. n. ZuhuwrN , (TA,) He knew, became acquainted with, or got knowledge of, him, or it. (Msb, TA.) So in the Kur xxiv. 31, waA@lT~ifolu A@l~a*iyna lamo yaZoharuwA EalaY EaworaAti A@ln~isaA='i [ And the young children ] who have not attained knowledge of the EwrAt , (Bd, Jel,) meaning [ pudenda, or] parts between the navel and the knee, (Jel,) of women, by reason of their want of discrimination: (Bd:) or (tropical:) who have not attained to the generative faculty; (O, Bd, * TA;) from AlZ~uhuwru in the sense of Algalabapu . (Bd.) So too in the Kur [xviii. 19], A_ino yaZoharuwA Ealayokumo If they get knowledge of you. (O, TA.) ― -b4- And [hence] Zahara Ealayohi , (Fr, A, O, TA,) and ↓ AstZhrhu , (S, A, O, K,) (tropical:) He knew it, or learned it, by heart; namely, the Kur-án; (A, O, TA;) and he recited it by heart: (A, * TA; and so in the S and O in explanation of the latter:) or [simply] he recited it by heart; namely, the Kur-án; as also ↓ AZhrhu : (O, K, TA:) in the copies of the K we find A^aZoharotu EalaY AlquroA=ni and A^aZoharotuhu ; but the former is a mistake for Zaharotu , aor. . (TA.) -A3- For another signification of Zahara Ealayohi , see 3. -A4- Zahara biHaAjatiY , (S, A, K,) aor. , (TA,) inf. n. ZahorN ; (TK;) and ↓ Zh~rhA , (K, TA,) in some copies of the K ZaharahaA ; (TA;) and ↓ AZhrhA , (K,) inf. n. A_iZohaArN ; (TA;) and ↓ AiZ~aharahaA , (K,) of the measure AifotaEala ; (TA;) (tropical:) He held the object of my want in little, or light, estimation, or in contempt; (S, A;) [lit.] he put it behind [ his ] back; (S, K;) as though he put it away, [ out of his sight, ] and paid no regard to it. (S, TA.) One says also, yaZoharuwna bihimo walaA yalotafituwna A_ilaY A^aroHaAmihimo [ They hold them in contempt, and do not pay any regard to their ties of relationship ]. (S.) ― -b2- See also 10, in three places. -A5- Zaharahu , (O, K,) aor. , inf. n. ZahorN , (K,) He struck, or smote, (TA,) or hit, or hurt, (O, K,) his back. (O, K, TA.) -A6- Zahira , (S, O, K,) aor. , (K,) inf. n. ZaharN , (O, K,) He (a man, S, O) had a complaint of his back. (S, O, K.) -A7- Zahura , (JK, O, L,) or Zahara , (K, [but this is app. a mistranscription,]) inf. n. ZahaArapN , (S, O, L, K,) said of a camel, (JK, S, O,) He was, or became, strong (JK, S, O, L, K) in the back. (L, K.)

(TA.) ― -b2- ZAhr bihi : see 10. ― -b3- ZAhr bayonahumaA , (K,) i. e. (TA) bayona vawobayoni , (S, A, Mgh, TA,) and diroEayoni , (A, Mgh, TA,) and naEolayoni , (TA,) i. q. TaAraqa bayonahumaA , (S, TA,) or TaAbaqa , (A, K, TA,) i. e. (TA) He put them on, or attired himself with them, [namely, two garments, and two coats of mail, and two sandals or soles, or rather, when relating to two soles, he sewed them together, ] one over, or outside, the other: (Mgh, TA:) app. from taZaAhurN in the sense of “ mutual aiding or assisting. ” (IAth.) The phrase ZAhr bidiroEayoni requires consideration; and the b in it should be regarded as meant to denote conjunction; not as a part of the necessary complement of the verb. (Mgh.) ZAhr Ald~iroEa is said to signify laA^ama baEoDahaA EalaY baEoDK [app. meaning He folded over and fastened one part of the coat of mail upon another ]. (TA.) And ZAhr Ealayohi jilaAlFA means He threw upon him (i. e. a horse) housings or coverings [ one over another ]. (TA in art. Hn* .) -A2- ZAhr mini A@moraA^atihi , (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K,) inf. n. ZihaArN (S, Mgh, Msb, K) and muZaAharapN ; (JK, TA;) and minohaA ↓ tZAhr , (A, Mgh, O, TA,) and ↓ AiZ~aAhara ; (Mgh;) and mnhA ↓ tZh~r , (S, Msb, K,) and ↓ AiZ~ah~ara ; (O, TA;) and mnhA ↓ Zh~r , (S, O, K,) inf. n. taZohiyrN ; (S;) signify the same; (O;) He said to his wife A^anoti EalaY~a kaZahori A^um~iY [ Thou art to me like the back of my mother ]; (S, Mgh, Msb, K;) [as though he said rukuwbuki HaraAmN EalaY~a ;] meaning rukuwbuki liln~ikaAHi HaraAmN EalaY~a karukuwbi A^um~iY liln~ikaAHi ; the back being specified in preference to the baTon or faxi* or faroj because the woman is likened to a beast that is ridden, and the act of nikaAH to that of rukuwb : the phrase being a form of divorce used by the Arabs in the Time of Ignorance. (Msb, * TA.) In the Kur lviii. 2 [and 4], some read ↓ yaZ~ah~aruwna ; some ↓ yaZ~aAharuwna ; and 'Ásim read yuZaAhiruwna . (Bd.) The verb is made trans. by means of min because the man who uttered this sentence estranged himself from his wife. (IAth.)

definition: He made it apparent, overt, open, perceptible or perceived, manifest, plain, or evident;
sourceDefinition: He made it apparent, overt, open, perceptible or perceived, manifest, plain, or evident; he showed, exhibited, manifested, displayed, discovered, revealed, or evinced, it; or put it forth: (S, O, K:) [it is also used in relation to a saying, and an action, and the like, as meaning it showed, &c., as above, or it bespoke, it: ] and Mtr relates his having heard from one worthy of reliance of the people of Baghdád, that they say ↓ tZAhrtu bihi in the place of A^aZoharotuhu , and scarcely ever employ AZhr in its usual sense. (Har p. 85.) [Hence, AZhr Alt~aDoEiyfa He made the doubling of a letter distinct; as in laHiHato ; which, accord. to a general rule, should be laH~ato : opposed to A^adogama . And AZhr lahu ka*aA He showed, &c., to him such a thing: and he made a show of, professed, pretended, or feigned, to him such a thing: as, for instance, love.] ― -b2- A^aZoharotu bifulaAnK means A^aEolayotu bihi [a phrase which I have not found except in this instance, app. I elevated, or exalted, such a one: like A^aEolayotuhu , which has this meaning]: (S, IKtt, L, TA:) or A^aEolanotu bihi [app. meaning I made such a one to be, or become, publicly known ]: (So in the O:) [but the former explanation seems to be regarded by SM as the right; for he remarks that,] accord. to all the copies of the K, the explanation is A^aEolana bihi , and refers to Zahara bifulaAnK [instead of A^aZohara ]; so that what its author says in this case differs in two points of view from what is found in the “ Kitáb el-Abniyeh ” of IKtt, in which the Y in A^aEolayotu has been marked as correct, and in the L [as well as in the S]. (TA.) -A2- AZhrhu A@ll~`hu EalaY Eaduw~ihi means God made him to overcome, conquer, subdue, overpower, master, gain the victory over, or prevail over, his enemy. (S, A, O, TA.) ― -b2- And [hence] AZhrhu Ealayohi He (God) made him to know it, or become acquainted with it: you say, A^aZoharaniY A@ll~`hu EalaY maA suriqa min~iY God made me to know [or discover ] what had been stolen from me. (TA.) -A3- See also 1, last quarter, in two places. -A4- And see 2. -A5- AZhr signifies also He entered upon the time called the Zahiyrap : (A, Msb, K:) or the time called the Zuhor . (Msb.) And He went, or journeyed, in the time called the Zahiyrap ; as also ↓ Zh~r , (K,) inf. n. taZohiyrN : (TA:) or the time called the Zuhor . (S, O.)

definition: He sought aid, or assistance, in, or by means of, him, or it, (S, O, Msb, K, TA,) Ealayohi [ against him, or it ];
sourceDefinition: He sought aid, or assistance, in, or by means of, him, or it, (S, O, Msb, K, TA,) Ealayohi [ against him, or it ]; as also AstZhrhu . (TA.) [In the CK, after the explanation of AstZhr bh , is an omission, to be supplied by the insertion of waqaraA^ahu .] One says, AstZhr biA@loginaY EalaY Aln~awaAy^ibi [ He sought aid in wealth against calamities, or afflictions ]. (Msb.) And bihi ↓ ZAhr signifies the same as AstZhr [in this sense or in another of the senses expl. in what follows]. (TA.) ― -b2- And AstZhrtu biAl$~aYo'i , and bihi ↓ Zaharotu , and ↓ Zaharotuhu , I put the thing behind my back for protection, or security. (Har p. 265.) ― -b3- And AstZhr He prepared for himself a camel, or two camels, or more, for future need: (T:) and AstZhrhu , and bihi ↓ Zahara , He prepared him, namely, a camel, for future need: (K:) and AstZhr bibaEiyrayoni Zihoriy~ayoni He prepared for himself two camels for future need. (T. [See ZihoriY~N .]) ― -b4- Hence, (T,) AstZhr signifies also He used precaution (T, Msb) with respect to anything: (T:) he secured himself, ( Aisotawovaqa ,) by using precaution; as, for instance, a woman does by remaining three days, before she performs the ablution termed gusol , and prays, after the usual period of the menses. (T, L.) One says, yusotaHab~u AlAisotiZohaAru bigasolapK vaAniyapK wavaAlivapK The using precaution by a second and a third washing, to make sure of being pure, is approved. (Er-Ráfi'ee, Msb.) And AstZhrtu fiY Talabi Al$~aYo'i I adopted the most fit, or proper, way, and used precaution, in seeking to attain the thing. (Msb.) ― -b5- See also 1, in the middle of the latter half.

sourceDefinition: The back; contr. of baTonN : (S, A, O, Msb, K:) in a man, from the hinder part of the kaAhil [or base of the neck ] to the nearest part of the buttocks, where it terminates: (TA:) in a camel, the part containing six vertebræ on the right and left of which are [ two portions of flesh and sinew called the ] matonaAni : (AHeyth, T, O:) of the masc. gender: (Lh, A, K:) pl. [of pauc.] A^aZohurN , and [of mult.] ZuhuwrN and ZuhoraAnN . (Msb, K.) ― -b2- rajulN xafiyfu AlZ~ahori (tropical:) A man having a small household to maintain: and vaqiylu AlZ~ahori (tropical:) having a large household to maintain. (K, * TA.) ― -b3- A^anot EalaY~a kaZahori A^um~iY Thou art to me like the back of my mother: said by a man to his wife. (S, Mgh, Msb, K.) [This has been expl. above: see 3.] ― -b4- EadaA fiY Zahorihi (tropical:) He stole what was behind him: (A:) [or he acted wrongfully in respect of what was behind him: for] liS~N EaAdiY ZahorK is expl. by the words EadaA fiY ZahorK fasaraqahu [so that it app. means (tropical:) A thief who has acted wrongfully in respect of what was behind one, and stolen it ]. (O, K.) ― -b5- A^aqoraAnu AlZ~ahori (S, O, K) and AlZ~uhuwri (O, TA) Adversaries who come to one from behind his back, in war, or fight. (S, O, K, * TA.) In the copies of the K, yuHib~uwnaka is erroneously put for yajiyw^uwnaka . (TA.) You say also, fulaAnN qironu AlZ~ahori Such a one is an adversary who comes to one from behind, unknown. (IAar, As.) ― -b6- qatalahu ZahorFA He slew him unexpectedly; he assassinated him; syn. giylapN . (IAar, TA.) ― -b7- jaEalaniY biZahorK (tropical:) He cast me off. (TA.) And jaEaltu HaAjatahu biZahorK (tropical:) I cast his want behind my back: (AO, K:) and ↓ jaEalahaA Zihoriy~apF signifies the same: (S:) and ↓ Ait~axa*ahaA Zihoriy~FA , (K,) and ↓ Zihoriy~apF : (TA:) or the former of the last two phrases signifies he held it in contempt; as though Zhry~A were an irreg. rel. n. from ZahorN : (TA:) or ↓ Ait~axa*ahu Zihoriy~FA signifies he neglected, or forgot, (S, O, * Msb,) him, as in the Kur xi. 94, (S, O,) or it, namely, what was said. (Msb.) And laA tajoEalo HaAjatiY biZahorK (tropical:) Forget not thou, or neglect not, my want: (S:) and ↓ jaEalahu Zihoriy~FA signifies he forgot it; as well as jElh biZahorK . (A.) And jaEalotu h`*aA AlA^amora biZahorK , and ramayotuhu biZahorK , (tropical:) I cared not for this thing. (Th, O.) ― -b8- fulaAnN mino waladi AlZ~ahori (assumed tropical:) Such a one is of those who do not belong to us: or of those to whom no regard is paid: (TA:) or of those who are held in contempt, and to whose ties of relationship no regard is paid. (S, TA.) ― -b9- huwa A@bonu Eam~ihi ZahorFA (tropical:) [ He is his cousin on the father's side, ] distantly related: contr. of dinoyFA [ and laH~FA ]. (As, A, O, TA.) ― -b10- rajaEa EalaY Zahorihi [ He receded, retired, or retreated ]. (K in art. vbjr .) ― -b11- huwa naAzilN bayona Zahorayohimo , and ↓ byn ZahoraAnayohimo , (S, A, O, Msb, K, *) in which latter the A and n are said by some to be added for corroboration, (Msb,) and for which one should not say ZahoraAniyhimo , (IF, S, O, Msb, K,) and byn A^aZohurihimo , (Msb, K,) (tropical:) He is making his abode in the midst of them; in the main body of them: (K, TA:) originally meaning he is making his abode among them for the purpose of seeking aid of them and staying himself upon them: as though it meant that the back of one of them was before him, and that of another behind him, so that he was defended in either direction: afterwards, by reason of frequency of usage, it came to be employed to signify abiding among a people absolutely. (IAth, Msb.) You say also huwa bayona Zahorayohi , and ↓ bayona ZahoraAnayohi , meaning It (anything) is in the midst, or main part, of it, namely, another thing. (TA.) ― -b12- laqiytuhu bayona AlZ~ahorayoni , and ↓ bayona AlZ~ahoraAnayoni , (S, O, Msb, K,) (tropical:) I met him during the day, (Msb,) or during the two days, (S, O, K,) or during the three days, (K,) or the days: (S, O, Msb:) from the next preceding phrase. (TA.) And A^atayotuhu mar~apF bayona AlZ~aharoyni (tropical:) I came to him one day: or, accord. to Aboo-Fak'as, on a day between two years. (Fr.) And All~ayoli ↓ raA^ayotuhu bayona ZahoraAnaYi (tropical:) I saw him between nightfall and daybreak. (TA.) And Aln~ahaAri ↓ jiy^otuhu bayona ZahoraAnaYi (tropical:) [ I came to him between the beginning and end of the day ]. (A.) ― -b13- taqal~aba ZahorFA libaTonK (assumed tropical:) It turned over and over, or upside down, (lit. back for belly, ) as a serpent does upon ground heated by the sun. (S and TA in art. qlb .) [Hence,] qalabotu AlA^aroDa ZahorFA libaTonK (tropical:) [ I turned the earth over, upside-down ]. (A.) And [hence,] qal~aba A^amorahu ZahorFA libaTonK , (O, * TA,) and Zahorahu libaTonK , and Zahorahu libaTonihi , and Zahorahu lilobaToni , which last form is preferred by El-Farezdak to the second, because [as in the third form] the second of the two words is determinate like the first word, (tropical:) He meditated, or managed, the affair with forecast, and well. (O, * TA.) ― -b14- The Arabs used to say, h`*aA Zahoru Als~amaA='i and h*A baTonu Als~amaA='i , both meaning (tropical:) This is the apparent, visible, part of the sky. (Fr, Az.) And the like is said of the side of a wall, which is its baTon to a person on the same side, and its Zahor to one on the other side. (Az.) ― -b15- maA nazala mina AlquroA=ni A=yapN A_il~aA lahaA ZahorN wabaTonN , [part of] a saying of Mohammad, [of which see the rest voce muT~alaEN ,] means (assumed tropical:) Not a verse of the Kur-án has come down but it has a verbal expression and an interpretation: (K, * TA:) or a verbal expression and a meaning: or that which has an apparent and a known [or an exoteric ] interpretation and that which has an intrinsic [or esoteric ] interpretation: (TA:) or narration (K, TA) and admonition: (TA:) or [ it is to be read and to be understood and taught; for] by the Zhr is meant the reading; and by the bTn , the understanding and teaching. (TA.) [See also baTonN .] ― -b16- ZahorN signifies also (tropical:) Camels on which people ride, and which carry goods; (S, * A, * O, K, * TA;) camels that carry burdens upon their backs in journeying: (TA:) [or] a beast: or a camel for riding: (Mgh:) pl. ZuhoraAnN . (TA.) It is said in a trad. of 'Arfajeh, fatanaAwala Als~ayofa mina AlZ~ahori And he reached, or took in his hand, the sword from the camels for carrying burdens and for riding: and in another, A^ataA^o*anu lanaA fiY naHori ZahorinaA Dost thou permit us to slaughter our camels which we ride? (TA.) And one says also, huwa EalaY ZahorK (tropical:) He is determined upon travel: (K:) as though he had already mounted a beast for that purpose. (TA.) ― -b17- [Hence, app.,] (assumed tropical:) Property consisting of camels and sheep or goats: (TA:) or much property. (K, TA.) ― -b18- (assumed tropical:) The short side [or lateral half ] of a feather: (S, O, K:) pl. ZuhoraAnN : (S, M, K, TA, &c.:) opposed to baTonN , sing. of buTonaAnN , (TA,) which latter signifies the “ long sides: ” (S, TA:) and ↓ ZuhaArN signifies the same as ZahorN , (K,) or the same as ZuhoraAnN , being an irregular pl.; and this is meant by the saying AlZ~uhaAru biAlD~ami AljamaAEapu , mentioned in a later place in the K [in such a manner as to have led to the supposition that ZuhaArN is also syn. with jamaAEapN ]: (TA:) AO says that among the feathers of arrows are the ZuhaAr , which are those that are put [ upon an arrow ] of the Zahor [or outer side ] of the Easiyb [app. here meaning the shaft ] of the feather; (S, TA;) i. e., the shorter side, which is the best kind of feather; as also ZuhoraAn : sing. ZahorN : (TA:) ISd says that the ZuhoraAn are those parts of the feathers of the wing that are exposed to the sun and rain: (TA:) Lth says that the ZuhaAr are those parts of the feathers of the wing that are apparent. (O, TA.) One says, ri$o sahomaka biZuhoraAnK walaA tari$ohu bibuTonaAnK [ Feather thine arrow with short sides of feathers, and feather it not with long sides of feathers ]. (S, TA.) [De Sacy supposes that ZuhuwrN and buTuwnN are also pls. of ZahorN and baTonN thus used: (see his “ Chrest. Arabe, ” sec. ed., tome ii., p. 374:) but his reasons do not appear to me to be conclusive.] ↓ ZuhaArN and ZuhoraAnN are also used as epithets: you say, riy$N ZuhaArN and riy$N ZuhoraAnN . (TA.) ― -b19- [ Zahoru Alkaf~i and ↓ ZaAhiruhaA mean (assumed tropical:) The back of the hand. And in like manner, Zahoru Alqadami and ↓ ZaAhiruhaA mean (assumed tropical:) The upper, or convex, side, or back, of the human foot, corresponding to the back of the hand, including the instep: opposed to baTon and baATin . And Zahoru All~isaAni means (assumed tropical:) The upper surface of the tongue. ] ― -b20- And ZahorN also signifies (tropical:) A way by land. (S, M, O, Msb, K.) This expression is used when there is a way by land and a way by sea. (M.) You say, saAruwA fiY Tariyqi AlZ~ahori (tropical:) They journeyed by land. (A.) ― -b21- And (assumed tropical:) An elevated tract of land or ground; as also ↓ ZaAhirpN : (A:) or rugged and elevated land or ground; (JK, K;) as also ↓ ZaAhirapN : (JK:) opposed to baTonN , which signifies “ soft and plain and fine and low land or ground: ” (TA:) and ↓ ZawaAhiru [pl. of. ZaAhirapN ] signifies (assumed tropical:) elevated tracts of land or ground: (S, K:) you say, haAjato ZawaAhiru AlA^aroDi , meaning, (assumed tropical:) the herbs, or leguminous plants, of the elevated tracts of land, or ground, dried up: (As, S, L:) and ↓ ZaAhirN signifies (assumed tropical:) the higher, or highest, part of a mountain; (ISh, L, TA;) whether its exterior be plain or not: (TA:) and ↓ ZaAhirapN , the same, of anything: (L:) when you have ascended upon the Zahor of a mountain, you are upon its ZaAhirap . (TA.) ― -b22- saAla waAdiyhimo ZahorFA means (assumed tropical:) Their valley flowed with the rain of their own land: opposed to duro'FA , meaning, “ from other rain: ” (IAar, O, K: *) or the former signifies their valley flowed with its own rain: and the latter, “ with other than its own rain: ” (TA:) and some say ↓ ZuhorFA , which Az thinks the better form. (O, TA.) ― -b23- [Hence, probably,] A^aSabotu minohu maTara ZahorK (assumed tropical:) I obtained from him, or it, much good. (Sgh, O, K.) ― -b24- And another signification of ZahorN is What is absent, or hidden, or concealed, from one. (O, K.) ― -b25- It is sometimes prefixed to another noun to give plainness and force to the expression; as in Zahoru Algayobi and Zahoru Alqalobi , meaning nafosu Algayobi and nafosu Alqalobi : (Msb:) or it is redundant in these instances. (Mgh.) Lebeed says, describing a [wild] cow going about after a beast of prey that had eaten her young one, watasam~aEato riz~a AlA^aniysi faraAEahaA Eano Zahori gayobK waAlA^aniysu saqaAmuhaA [ And she heard the sound of man, and it frightened her, from a place that concealed what was in it; for man is her malady; i. e., a cause of pain and trouble and death to her ]: (TA:) meaning, she heard the sound of the hunters, &c. (TA in art. gyb .) And you say, tanaAwalahu biZahori Algayobi bimaA yasuww^uhu He carped at him behind the back, or in absence, by saying what would grieve him. (TA in art. gyb .) And takal~amotu bihi Eano Zahori Algayobi (A, O) or En Zahori gayobK (TA) [app., (tropical:) I spoke it by memory; in the absence of a book or the like; as one says in modern Arabic, EalaY AlgaAy^ib . See also gayobN .] And qaraA^ahu Eano Zahori Alqalobi (tropical:) He recited it by heart, or memory; without book: (L, K: [in the latter, mino is put in the place of Eano ; but the right reading is that in the L: and in the CK is an omission here, to be supplied by the insertion of waqaraA^ahu :]) and ↓ qrA^h ZaAhirFA and qrA^h EalaY Zahori lisaAnihi [signify the same]. (K.) And Hamala AlquroA=na EalaY Zahori lisaAnihi like HafiZahu EalaY Zahori qalobihi (tropical:) [ He knew the Kur-án by heart ]. (A, * O, TA.) ― -b26- One says also, fulaAnN yaA^okulu EalaY Zahori yadi fulaAnK (tropical:) Such a one eats at the expense of such a one. (A, O, K. *) And in like manner, AlfuqaraA='u yaA^okuluwna EalaY Zahori A^ayodiY Aln~aAsi (tropical:) The poor eat at the expense of the people. (A, TA.) And A^aEoTaAhu Eano Zahori yadK (tropical:) He gave him originally; without compensation. (O, * K; but in some copies of the K we find mino in the place of Eano .) It is said [in a trad.], A^afoDalu AlS~adaqapi maA kaAna Eano Zahori ginFY (tropical:) The most excellent of alms is that which is [ derived ] from competence; Zhr : (Msb:) or simply Eano ginFY , the word Zhr being here redundant: (Mgh:) or from manifest competence upon which one relies, and in which he seeks aid against calamities, or afflictions: or from what remains after fight: (Msb:) or from superfluous property. (TA.) -A2- See also ZahiyrN -A3- qidoru ZahorK means (assumed tropical:) An old cooking-pot: (O, K: *) pl. quduwru ZuhuwrK : (O:) as though, because of its oldness, it were thrown behind the back. (TA.)

[De Sacy supposes that ZuhuwrN and buTuwnN are also pls. of ZahorN and baTonN thus used: (see his “ Chrest. Arabe, ” sec. ed., tome ii., p. 374:) but his reasons do not appear to me to be conclusive.] ↓ ZuhaArN and ZuhoraAnN are also used as epithets: you say, riy$N ZuhaArN and riy$N ZuhoraAnN . (TA.) ― -b19- [ Zahoru Alkaf~i and ↓ ZaAhiruhaA mean (assumed tropical:) The back of the hand. And in like manner, Zahoru Alqadami and ↓ ZaAhiruhaA mean (assumed tropical:) The upper, or convex, side, or back, of the human foot, corresponding to the back of the hand, including the instep: opposed to baTon and baATin . And Zahoru All~isaAni means (assumed tropical:) The upper surface of the tongue. ] ― -b20- And ZahorN also signifies (tropical:) A way by land. (S, M, O, Msb, K.) This expression is used when there is a way by land and a way by sea. (M.) You say, saAruwA fiY Tariyqi AlZ~ahori (tropical:) They journeyed by land. (A.) ― -b21- And (assumed tropical:) An elevated tract of land or ground; as also ↓ ZaAhirpN : (A:) or rugged and elevated land or ground; (JK, K;) as also ↓ ZaAhirapN : (JK:) opposed to baTonN , which signifies “ soft and plain and fine and low land or ground: ” (TA:) and ↓ ZawaAhiru [pl. of. ZaAhirapN ] signifies (assumed tropical:) elevated tracts of land or ground: (S, K:) you say, haAjato ZawaAhiru AlA^aroDi , meaning, (assumed tropical:) the herbs, or leguminous plants, of the elevated tracts of land, or ground, dried up: (As, S, L:) and ↓ ZaAhirN signifies (assumed tropical:) the higher, or highest, part of a mountain; (ISh, L, TA;) whether its exterior be plain or not: (TA:) and ↓ ZaAhirapN , the same, of anything: (L:) when you have ascended upon the Zahor of a mountain, you are upon its ZaAhirap . (TA.) ― -b22- saAla waAdiyhimo ZahorFA means (assumed tropical:) Their valley flowed with the rain of their own land: opposed to duro'FA , meaning, “ from other rain: ” (IAar, O, K: *) or the former signifies their valley flowed with its own rain: and the latter, “ with other than its own rain: ” (TA:) and some say ↓ ZuhorFA , which Az thinks the better form. (O, TA.) ― -b23- [Hence, probably,] A^aSabotu minohu maTara ZahorK (assumed tropical:) I obtained from him, or it, much good. (Sgh, O, K.) ― -b24- And another signification of ZahorN is What is absent, or hidden, or concealed, from one. (O, K.) ― -b25- It is sometimes prefixed to another noun to give plainness and force to the expression; as in Zahoru Algayobi and Zahoru Alqalobi , meaning nafosu Algayobi and nafosu Alqalobi : (Msb:) or it is redundant in these instances. (Mgh.) Lebeed says, describing a [wild] cow going about after a beast of prey that had eaten her young one, watasam~aEato riz~a AlA^aniysi faraAEahaA Eano Zahori gayobK waAlA^aniysu saqaAmuhaA [ And she heard the sound of man, and it frightened her, from a place that concealed what was in it; for man is her malady; i. e., a cause of pain and trouble and death to her ]: (TA:) meaning, she heard the sound of the hunters, &c. (TA in art. gyb .) And you say, tanaAwalahu biZahori Algayobi bimaA yasuww^uhu He carped at him behind the back, or in absence, by saying what would grieve him. (TA in art. gyb .) And takal~amotu bihi Eano Zahori Algayobi (A, O) or En Zahori gayobK (TA) [app., (tropical:) I spoke it by memory; in the absence of a book or the like; as one says in modern Arabic, EalaY AlgaAy^ib . See also gayobN .] And qaraA^ahu Eano Zahori Alqalobi (tropical:) He recited it by heart, or memory; without book: (L, K: [in the latter, mino is put in the place of Eano ; but the right reading is that in the L: and in the CK is an omission here, to be supplied by the insertion of waqaraA^ahu :]) and ↓ qrA^h ZaAhirFA and qrA^h EalaY Zahori lisaAnihi [signify the same]. (K.) And Hamala AlquroA=na EalaY Zahori lisaAnihi like HafiZahu EalaY Zahori qalobihi (tropical:) [ He knew the Kur-án by heart ]. (A, * O, TA.) ― -b26- One says also, fulaAnN yaA^okulu EalaY Zahori yadi fulaAnK (tropical:) Such a one eats at the expense of such a one. (A, O, K. *) And in like manner, AlfuqaraA='u yaA^okuluwna EalaY Zahori A^ayodiY Aln~aAsi (tropical:) The poor eat at the expense of the people. (A, TA.) And A^aEoTaAhu Eano Zahori yadK (tropical:) He gave him originally; without compensation. (O, * K; but in some copies of the K we find mino in the place of Eano .) It is said [in a trad.], A^afoDalu AlS~adaqapi maA kaAna Eano Zahori ginFY (tropical:) The most excellent of alms is that which is [ derived ] from competence; Zhr : (Msb:) or simply Eano ginFY , the word Zhr being here redundant: (Mgh:) or from manifest competence upon which one relies, and in which he seeks aid against calamities, or afflictions: or from what remains after fight: (Msb:) or from superfluous property. definition: A camel prepared for future need;
sourceDefinition: A camel prepared for future need; (T, S, O, K;) taken, by way of precaution, to bear the burden of any camel that may happen to fail in a journey: sometimes two or more unladen camels are taken for this purpose: some say that such a camel is thus called because its owner puts it behind his back, not riding it nor putting any burden upon it: (T, TA:) the word appears to be an irreg. rel. n. from ZahorN : (ISd, TA:) pl. ZahaAriY~N , imperfectly decl., because the rel. Y retains its place in the sing. [inseparably; there being no such word as Zihor : but if it be a rel. n., this pl. is irreg., like mahaAriY~N ]. (S, O, K.) ― -b2- See ZahorN , first quarter, in five places, for examples of ZihoriY~N and Zihoriy~apN used tropically.

definition: The point of midday: (M, A, K:) or only in summer: (M, K:) or i.
sourceDefinition: The point of midday: (M, A, K:) or only in summer: (M, K:) or i. q. haAjirapN [i. e. midday in summer or when the heat is vehement: or the period from a little before, to a little after, midday in summer: or midday, when the sun declines from the meridian, at the Zuhor : or from its declining until the EaSor ]: (S, O, TA:) or the haAjirap , which is when the sun declines from the meridian: (Msb:) or the vehement heat of midday: (IAth, TA:) or i. q. ZuhorN [q. v.]: (Az, TA:) pl. ZahaAy^iru . (TA.) You say, A^atoyotuhu Had~a AlZ~ahiyrapi [ I came to him at the point of midday in summer; &c.]: and Hiyna qaAma qaAy^imu AlZ~ahiyrapi [ when the sun had become high, and the shade had almost disappeared: so expl. in art. qwm ]. (S, O.) And A^aborido Eanoka mina AlZ~ahiyrapi Stay thou until the middayheat shall have become assuaged, and the air be cool. (L in art. fyH .) And hence, in a trad. of 'Omar, when a man came to him complaining of gout in the feet, he said, ka*abatoka AlZ~ahaAy^iru , meaning Take thou to walking during the heat of the middays in summer. (TA.)

And $ariba Alfarasu ZaAhirapF The horse drank every day, at noon. (TA.) ZaAhirapu Algib~i [ The coming to the water at noon on alternate days ] is for sheep or goats; scarcely ever, or never, for camels; and is a little shorter [in the interval] than what is called [simply] Algib~u . (O, TA.)

Ea*oqN , (S, O,) He appended to the sheep, or goat, a sign whereby the latter might be known, termed ↓ Ea*oqapN (S, O, K) and ↓ Ei*oqapN , (K,) being a flock of wool, (S, O,) differing in colour from the animal: (S, O, K:) some particularize the animal to which this is done as being a goat: (TA:) and ↓ AE*qhA signifies the same. (S, K.) ― -b2- Hence the saying, mano Eu*iqato bihi AlA^aEomaAlu A^uEoliqato bihi AlA=maAlu (assumed tropical:) [ The person to whom offices of administration are assigned, to him hopes are made to cling ]. (Har p. 489.) ― -b3- Hence also, (O, TA,) Ea*aqa Alr~ajula , (S, O,) or Ea*aqahu bi$ar~K or biqabiyHK , (K,) (tropical:) He reproached him, or upbraided him, with a thing that was bad, evil, abominable, or foul, (S, O, K, TA,) and stigmatized him with it, (S, O, TA,) so that he became known thereby. (TA.) ― -b4- And Ea*aqahu A_ilaY ka*aA i. e. nasabahu A_ilayohi [commonly meaning nasaba A_ilayohi ka*aA (assumed tropical:) He attributed, or imputed, to him such a thing ]. (Ibn-'Abbád, O, K.) -A2- Ea*aqotu Aln~axolapa I cut off the branches of the palm-tree: (S, O:) and [in like manner one says] ↓ Ea*~aqotu , with teshdeed to denote muchness [of the action] or multiplicity [of the objects]. (S.) -A3- Ea*aqa said of the [species of sweet rush called] A_i*oxir , It put forth its fruit; as also ↓ A^aEo*aqa : (S, O, K:) or the latter, accord. to IAth, it had Eu*uwq [pl. of Ei*oqN ] and $uEab [pl. of $uEobapN , i. e. bunches, or sprigs ]: or, as some say, it blossomed. (TA.) And, said of the [species of tree, or plant, called] saxobar , It grew tall. (IAar, O, TA.) -A4- Ea*aqa AlfaHolu Eani AlA_ibili , (O, K,) aor. , (K,) inf. n. Ea*oqN , (TA,) The stallion [ camel ] repelled from the [ she- ] camels, and drew them together. (O, K.) -A5- And Ea*aqa AlbaEiyru The camel voided his dung in a thin state. (Ibn- 'Abbád, O, K.)

definition: , (S, O, Msb, K, &c.
sourceDefinition: , (S, O, Msb, K, &c.,) aor. , (O, K,) inf. n. maEorifapN (S, O, K) and EirofaAnN (S, O, Msb, K) and Eirif~aAnN (K) and EirofapN , (Msb, K,) or maEorifapN is a simple subst., (Msb,) He knew it; he had cognition of it; or he was, or became, acquainted with it; syn. Ealimahu : (K:) or he knew it ( Ealimahu ) by means of any of the five senses; (Msb;) [and also, by mental perception: ] Er-Rághib says, AlmaEorifapu is the perceiving a thing by reflection, and by consideration of the effect thereof [ upon the mind or sense ], so that it has a more special meaning than AlEilomu , and its contr. is AlA_inokaAru ; and one says, fulaAnN yaEorifu A@ll~`ha warasuwlahu [ Such a one knows God and his apostle ], but one does not say yaEolamu A@ll~`ha , making the verb [thus] to have a single objective complement, since man's maEorifap [or knowledge] of God is [the result of] the consideration of his effects, without the perception of his essence; and one says, Aall~`hu yaEolamu ka*aA , but not yaEorifu k*A , since AlmaEorifapu is used in relation to Eilom [or knowledge] which is defective, to which one attains by reflection: it is from Earafotuhu meaning I found, or experienced, its Earof i. e. odour; or as meaning I attained its Eurof i. e. limit: (TA:) it is said in the B that AlmaEorifapu differs from AlEilomu , in meaning, in several ways: the former concerns the thing itself [which is its object;] whereas the latter concerns the states, or conditions, or qualities, thereof: also the former generally denotes the perceiving a thing as a thing that has been absent from the mind, thus differing from the latter; therefore the contr. of the former is AlA_inokaAru , and the contr. of the latter is Aljaholu ; and the former is the knowing a thing itself as distinguished from other things; whereas the latter concerns a thing collectively with other things: (TA in art. Elm :) and sometimes they put ↓ AEtrf in the place of Earafa ; (S, O;) [i. e.] AEtrf Al$~aYo'a signifies Earafahu : (Mgh, K:) and so, sometimes, does ↓ AstErfuh . (Har p. 486.) ― -b2- And Earafa is also used in the place of AEtrf [in the first of the senses assigned to the latter below]. (S, O.) See the latter verb, in four places. ― -b3- Earafahu also signifies He requited him. (O, K.) Ks read, (O, K,) and so five others, (Az, TA,) in the Kur [lxvi. 3], (O,) Earafa baEoDahu , meaning He requited her, namely, Hafsah, for part [ thereof, i. e.] of what she had done: (Fr, O, K:) and he did so indeed by divorcing her: (Fr, TA:) or it means he acknowledged part thereof: (K:) but others read baEoDahu ↓ Ear~afa , which, likewise, has the former of the two meanings expl. above: (Bd:) or this means he told Hafsah part thereof. (Fr, O, Bd, * TA. [See also 2.]) As first expl. above, this phrase is like the saying to him who does good or who does evil, A^anaA A^aEorifu lA^aholi AlA_iHosaAni waA^aEorifu liA^aholi AlA_isaA='api , (O,) or lilomuHosini waAlmusiYo'i , (K,) [ I know how to requite the doer of good and the doer of evil, ] i. e. the case of the doer of good and that of the doer of evil are not hidden from me nor is the suitable requital of him. (O, K.) laA^aEorifan~akahaA Eanoda rasuwli A@ll~`hi occurs in a trad., meaning I will assuredly requite thee for it in the presence of the Apostle of God so that he shall know thy evil-doing: and is used in threatening. (TA.) -A2- Earafa Alfarasa , (S, O, K,) aor. , (O,) inf. n. EarofN , (O, K,) He clipped the Eurof [i. e. mane ] of the horse. (S, O, K.) -A3- Earafotu EalaY Alqawomi , aor. , inf. n. EiraAfapN , I was, or became, Eariyf over the people, or party; i. e., manager, or orderer, of their affairs; as also Earufotu Ealayohimo : (Msb:) or Earufa , inf. n. EaraAEapN , signifies he was, or became, an Eariyf ; (S, O, K;) as also Earafa , aor. ; (K;) i. e., a naqiyb : (S, O:) and when you mean that he acted as an Eariyf , you say, Earafa EalayonaA siniyna , aor. , inf. n. EiraAfapN , [ he acted over us as an Eryf during some years, ] like kataba , aor. yakotubu , inf. n. kitaAbapN . (S, O, K. *) -A4- Earafa liloA^amori , aor. , He was patient in relation to the affair, or event; (K;) as also ↓ AEtrf , (O, K,) as some say. (O.) And Eurifa Einoda AlmuSiybapi He was patient on the occasion of the affliction, or misfortune. (TA.) ― -b2- And Earafa He was, or became, submissive, or tractable; (Ibn-'Abbád, O, TA;) and so ↓ AEtrf , (IAar, O, K,) said of a man, (IAar, O,) and of a beast that one rides. (O.) -A5- Earufa , inf. n. EaraAfapN , He (a man) was, or became, pleasant, or sweet, in his odour. (TA.) And ↓ AErf , said of food, It was sweet in its Earof , i. e. odour. (TA.) ― -b2- Earifa He (a man, TA) made much use of perfume. (IAar, O, K.) ― -b3- And He relinquished, or abstained from, perfume. (IAar, O.) -A6- Eurifa , (S, O, K,) inf. n. EarofN , (K, TA,) accord. to one or more of the copies of the K EirofaAnN , (TA,) He (a man, S, O) had a purulent pustule, termed Earofap , come forth in the whiteness [or palm ] of his hand. (S, O, K.)

Elm :) and sometimes they put ↓ AEtrf in the place of Earafa ; (S, O;) [i. e.] AEtrf Al$~aYo'a signifies Earafahu : (Mgh, K:) and so, sometimes, does ↓ AstErfuh . (Har p. 486.) ― -b2- And Earafa is also used in the place of AEtrf [in the first of the senses assigned to the latter below]. (S, O.) See the latter verb, in four places. ― -b3- Earafahu also signifies He requited him. (O, K.) (Fr, O, Bd, * TA. [See also 2.]) As first expl. above, this phrase is like the saying to him who does good or who does evil, A^anaA A^aEorifu lA^aholi AlA_iHosaAni waA^aEorifu liA^aholi AlA_isaA='api , (O,) or lilomuHosini waAlmusiYo'i , (K,) [ I know how to requite the doer of good and the doer of evil, ] i. e. the case of the doer of good and that of the doer of evil are not hidden from me nor is the suitable requital of him. (O, K.) laA^aEorifan~akahaA Eanoda rasuwli A@ll~`hi occurs in a trad., meaning I will assuredly requite thee for it in the presence of the Apostle of God so that he shall know thy evil-doing: and is used in threatening. (TA.) ― -b2- And Earafa He was, or became, submissive, or tractable; (Ibn-'Abbád, O, TA;) and so ↓ AEtrf , (IAar, O, K,) said of a man, (IAar, O,) and of a beast that one rides. (O.) -A5- Earufa , inf. n. EaraAfapN , He (a man) was, or became, pleasant, or sweet, in his odour. (TA.) And ↓ AErf , said of food, It was sweet in its Earof , i. e. odour.
