EarofN , (K, TA,) accord. to one or more of the copies of the K EirofaAnN , (TA,) He (a man, S, O) had a purulent pustule, termed Earofap , come forth in the whiteness [or palm ] of his hand. (S, O, K.)

definition: signifies The making to know;
sourceDefinition: signifies The making to know; syn. A_iEolaAmN : (S, O, K, TA:) [or rather it has a more restricted signification than the latter word, as is indicated in the preceding paragraph:] and in this sense its verb may have two objective complements: one says, Er~fhu AlA^amora He made him to know the affair, or case; syn. A^aEolamahu A_iy~aAhu : [or he acquainted him with it; or told him of it: ] and Er~fhu bayotahu He made him to know, or acquainted him with, the place of his house, or tent; syn. A^aEolamahu bimakaAnihi : (TA:) [and] one says Ear~afotuhu bihi , meaning I made him to know it by means of any of the five senses [or by mental perception; as also Ear~afotuhu A_iy~aAhu ]. (Msb.) See also 1, former half. And see 4. ― -b2- Also The making known; contr. of tanokiyrN . (O, K.) Ear~afa baEoDahu , in the Kur [lxvi. 3], has been expl. as meaning He made known part thereof. (TA. [For other explanations, see 1.]) And Ear~afotuhu bizayodK means I made him known by the name of Zeyd; like the phrase sam~ayotuhu bizayodK . (Sb, TA.) ― -b3- [Hence, The explaining a term: and an explanation thereof: thus used, its pl. is taEoriyfaAtN : it has a less restricted meaning than Had~N , which signifies the “ defining, ” and “ a definition. ” ― -b4- And The making a noun, or a nominal proposition, determinate. ― -b5- Hence also,] The crying a stray-beast, or a beast or some other thing that has been lost; (S, TA;) the mentioning it [ and describing it] and seeking to find him who had knowledge of it. (TA.) ― -b6- And [hence likewise,] Er~fhu bi*anobihi He branded him, or stigmatized him, with his misdeed. (TA.) -A2- Also The rendering [a thing] fragrant; (S, O, * K, * TA;) from AlEarofu : (S:) and the adorning [it], decorating [it], or embellishing [it]. (TA.) Ear~afahaA lahumo , in the Kur [xlvii. 7], is said to mean He hath rendered it fragrant [i. e. Paradise ( Aljan~ap )] for them: (S, O:) or it means He hath described it to them so that, when they enter it, they shall know it by that description, or so that they shall know their places of abode therein: (O:) or He hath described it to them, and made them desirous of it: (Er-Rághib, TA:) [and the like is said by Bd:] or He hath defined it for them so that there shall be for every one a distinct paradise. (Bd.) ― -b2- One says also, Er~f raA^osahu biAld~uhoni He moistened the hair of his head abundantly with oil, or with the oil; syn. raw~aAhu . (TA.) ― -b3- And Er~f TaEaAmahu He made his food to have much seasoning, or condiment. (TA.) -A3- Also The halting [of the pilgrims] at 'Arafát. (S, O, K.) You say, Er~fwA , (S, Mgh, O, Msb,) inf. n. as above, They halted at 'Arafát; (Mgh, Msb;) or they were present at 'Arafát; (S, O.) And [hence], in a postclassical sense, They imitated the people of 'Arafát, in some other place, by going forth to the desert and there praying, and humbling themselves, or offering earnest supplication; (Mgh;) or by assembling in their mosques to pray and to beg forgiveness: (Har p. 672:) the first who did this was Ibn-'Abbás, at El-Basrah. (Mgh, and Har ubi suprá.) And Er~f biAlhadoYi He brought the animal for sacrifice to 'Arafát. (Mgh.) -A4- Er~f Al$~ar~a bayonahumo He excited evil, or mischief, between them, or among them: the verb in this phrase being formed by permutation from A^a ~a va . (Yaakoob, TA.)

definition: It was, or became, known.
sourceDefinition: It was, or became, known. (Har p. 6.) ― -b2- And tEr~f A_ilayohi He made himself known to him; (TA;) [and so ↓ AstErf ; for] you say, A^atayotu mutanak~irFA vum~a A@sotaEorafotu i. e. [ I came disguising myself, or assuming an unknown appearance, then ] I made known who I was: (L:) and Aiy^oti fulaAnFA faA@sotaEorifo A_ilayohi Hat~aY yaEorifaka [ Come thou to such a one and make thyself known to him, that he may know thee ]. (S, O, K. *) [See also 8.] ― -b3- [Hence,] one says, tEr~f A_ilaY A@ll~`hi biAlEibaAdaAti waAlA^adoEiyapi [ He made himself known to God by religious services and prayers ]. (Er-Rághib, TA.) And taEar~afo A_ilaY A@ll~`hi fiY Alr~axaA='i yaEorifoka fiY Al$~id~apa , occurring in a saying of the Prophet to Ibn-'Abbás, [may be rendered Make thyself known to God by obedience in ampleness of circumstances, then He will acknowledge thee in straitness: or] means render thou obedience to God [&c., then] He will requite thee [&c.]. (O.) -A2- tEr~fhu [ He acquainted himself, or made himself acquainted, with it, or him; informed himself of it; learned it; and discovered it: often used in these senses: for an instance of the last, see tafar~asa : it is similar to taEal~amahu , but more restricted in meaning. ― -b2- And] He sought the knowledge of it: (Har p. 6:) [or he did so leisurely, or repeatedly, and effectually: ] you say, taEar~afotu maA Einoda fulaAnK I sought leisurely, or repeatedly, after the knowledge of what such a one possessed until I knew it. (S, O, K. *) ― -b3- And tEr~fhu AlmakaAna , and fiY AlmakaAni , He looked at it, endeavouring to obtain a clear knowledge thereof, in the place; syn. taA^am~alahu bihi . (TA.) -A3- [ taEar~ufN is also expl. in the KL by the Pers. words bErf kArY krdn , app. meaning The acting with Eurof i. e. goodness, &c.: but Golius has hence rendered the verb “ convenienter opus fecit. ”]

(TA.)

definition: He acknowledged it, or confessed it, (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K,) namely, a misdeed, (S, O,) or a thing;
sourceDefinition: He acknowledged it, or confessed it, (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K,) namely, a misdeed, (S, O,) or a thing; (Mgh, Msb;) and so bh ↓ Earafa and lahu , namely, his misdeed [&c.]; (K;) [for] sometimes they put Earafa in the place of AEtrf ; (O;) and so ↓ Earafahu : (Ksh and Bd and Jel in xvi. 85:) [ AlA_iHosaAni ↓ EirofaAnu (occurring in the K voce $ukorN &c.) means The acknowledgment, or confession, of beneficence; thankfulness, or gratitude: ] and one says, lA^iaHadK yaSoraEuniY ↓ maA A^aEorifu (S, O, TA) i. e. mA A^aEotarifu , (S, O,) meaning I do not acknowledge [ any one that will throw me down ]: this was said by an Arab of the desert. (TA.) ― -b2- AEtrf A_ilaY~a He acquainted me with his name and condition. (K.) And AEtrf lahu He described himself to him in such a manner as that he would certify himself of him thereby. (TA.) [See also 5.] ― -b3- AEtrf also signifies He described a thing that had been picked up, and a stray-beast, in such a manner as that he would be known to be its owner. sourceDefinition: An odour, whether fragrant or fetid, (S, O, K, TA,) in most instances the former, (K, TA,) as when it is used in relation to Paradise: (TA:) and ↓ EarofapN signifies [the same, i. e.] riyHN (K, TK) and raAy^iHapN . (TK.) One says, mA A^aToyaba Earofahu [ How fragrant is its odour! ]. (S, O.) And laA yaEojizu masoku Als~awo'i Eano Earofi Als~awo'i [ The bad hide will not lack the fetid odour ]; (S, O, K;) a prov.; (S, O;) applied to the low, ignoble, mean, or sordid, who will not cease from his evil doing; he being likened to the hide that is not fit for being tanned; (O, K;) wherefore it is cast aside, and becomes fetid. (Ibn-'Abbád, O, L.)

definition: [ Acknowledgment, or confession;
sourceDefinition: [ Acknowledgment, or confession; ] a subst. from AlAiEotiraAfu , (S, O, K, TA,) as meaning AlA_iqoraAru . (TA.) Hence, (S, O,) you say, (K,) lahu EalaY~a A^alofN EurofFA , meaning AiEotiraAfFA [i. e. A thousand is due to him on my part by acknowlegment, or confession ]; (S, O, * K;) the last word being a corroborative. (S, O.) ― -b2- Also i. q. ↓ maEoruwfN ; (S, O, Msb, K;) as also ↓ EaArifapN , (S, O, K,) of which the pl. is EawaArifu ; (O, K;) EurofN being contr. of nukorN , (S, O, K,) and ↓ maEoruwfN being contr. of munokarN [as syn. with nukorN ]; (S, Mgh, O, K;) i. e. Goodness, or a good quality or action; and gentleness, or lenity; and beneficence, [ favour, kindness, or bounty, ] or a benefit, a benefaction, or an act of beneficence [or favour or kindness ]: (Msb:) EurofN is also expl. as signifying liberality, or bounty; (K, TA;) and so ↓ EurufN , which is a dial. var. thereof: (TA:) and a thing liberally, or freely, bestowed; or given: (K:) and ↓ maEoruwfN is expl. as signifying liberality, or bounty, when it is with moderation, or with a right and just aim: [and sometimes it means simply moderation: ] and sincere, or honest, advice or counsel or action: and good fellowship with one's family and with others of mankind: it is an epithet in which the quality of a subst. predominates: (TA:) and signifies any action, or deed, of which the goodness is known by reason and by the law; and munokarN signifies the contr. thereof. (Er-Rághib, TA.) It is said in the Kur [vii. 198], waA^omuro biA@loEurofi , (O,) meaning [ And enjoin thou goodness, &c., or] what is deemed good, or approved, of actions. (Bd.) And you say, A^awolaAhu EurofFA , (S, O,) or ↓ EaArifapF , (TA,) meaning ↓ maEoruwfFA [i. e. He did to him, or conferred upon him, a benefit, &c.]. (S, O, TA.) walilomuTal~aqaAti ↓ mataAEN biA@lomaEoruwfi [in the Kur ii. 242] means [ And for the divorced women there shall be a provision of necessaries ] with moderation, or right and just aim, and beneficence. (TA.) And ↓ qawolN maEoruwfN wamagofirapN xayorN mino SadaqapK yatobaEuhaA A^a*FY [in the same, ii. 265,] means Refusal with pleasing [or gracious ] speech, (Bd, Jel, TA,) and prayer [expressed to the beggar, that God may sustain him,] (TA,) and forgiveness granted to the beggar for his importunity (Bd, Jel) or obtained by such refusal from God or from the beggar, (Bd,) are better than an alms which annoyance follows (TA) by reproach for a benefit conferred and for begging. (Jel.) And mano kaAna faqiyrFA faloyaA^okulo ↓ biA@lomaEoruwfi [in the same, iv. 6,] means [ And such as is poor, let him take for himself (lit. eat )] according to what is approved by reason and by the law, (TA,) or according to his need (Bd) and the recompense of his labour. (Bd, Jel.) ― -b3- [ AlEurofu , in lexicology, signifies The commonly-known, commonly-received, or common conventional, language; common parlance, or common usage: mostly meaning that of a whole people; in which case, the epithet AlEaAm~u is sometimes added: but often meaning that of a particular class; as, for instance, of the lawyers. Hence the terms HaqiyqapN EurofFA and majaAzN EurofFA , expl. in arts. Hq and jwz . See also mutaEaArafN : and see EaAdapN .] -A2- Also The Eurof of the horse; (S, O;) [i. e. the mane; ] the hair (Mgh, Msb, K) that grows on the ridge (Msb) of the neck of the horse (Mgh, Msb, K) or similar beast; (Msb;) as also ↓ EurufN : (K:) [see also maEorafapN :] or the part, of the neck, which is the place of growth of the hair: [see again maEorafapN :] and the part, of the neck [of a bird], which is the place of growth of the feathers: (TA:) [or the feathers themselves of the neck; used in this sense in the K and TA in art. brl , as is shown by the context therein:] and the [ comb or] elongated piece of flesh on the upper part of the head of a cock; to which the baZor of a girl is likened: (Msb:) pl. A^aEoraAfN [properly a pl. of pauc.] (O, TA) and EuruwfN . (TA.) As used it in relation to a man, explaining the phrase jaA='a fulaAnN muboravil~FA lil$~ar~i as meaning naAfi$FA Eurofahu [i. e. (assumed tropical:) Such a one came as though ruffling the feathers of his neck to do evil, or mischief ]. (TA.) And [hence] it is said in a trad., jaAw^uwA kaA^an~ahumo EurufN (assumed tropical:) [ They came as though they were a mane ], meaning, following one another. (TA.) And one says, jaA=' Alqawomu EurofFA EurofFA (assumed tropical:) [ The people, or party, came ] one after another: like the saying, TaAra AlqaTaA EurofFA (assumed tropical:) [ The sand-grouse flew ] one after another. (K.) And hence, waA@lomurosalaAti EurofFA , (S, O, K,) in the Kur [lxxvii. 1], a metaphorical phrase, from the Eurof of the horse, meaning (tropical:) [ By the angels, or the winds, that are sent forth ] consecutively, like [ the several portions of ] the Eurof [or mane ] of the horse: (S, O:) or the meaning is, sent forth biA@lomaEoruwfi , (S, O, K, TA,) i. e. with beneficence, or benefit: (TA:) [for further explanations, see the expositions of Z and Bd or others: and see also art. rsl :] some read EarofFA [expl. in the next preceding paragraph]. (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence also,] (tropical:) The waves of the sea. (K, TA.) ― -b3- And (assumed tropical:) Elevated sand; as also ↓ EurufN and ↓ EurofapN : pl. (of the last, TA) EurafN and (of the first, TA) A^aEoraAfN : (S, O, K:) and all signify likewise (assumed tropical:) an elevated place: (K:) and the first, (assumed tropical:) the elevated, or overtopping, back of a portion of sand, (K, TA,) and of a mountain, and of anything high: and (assumed tropical:) an elevated portion of the earth or ground: and [the pl.] A^aEoraAfN (assumed tropical:) the Harov [meaning land ploughed, or prepared, for sowing ] that is upon the [ channels for irrigation that are called ] fulojaAn [pl. of falajN ] and qawaAy^id [pl. of qaAy^idN ]. (TA.) ― -b4- [The pl.] AlA^aEoraAfu , (S, O, K,) mentioned in the Kur [vii. 44 and 46], (S, O,) is applied to (assumed tropical:) A wall between Paradise and Hell: (S, O, K:) so it is said: (S, O:) or the upper parts of the wall: or by EalaY AlA^aEoraAfi may be there meant EalaY maEorifapi A^aholi Aljan~api waA^aholi Aln~aAri [i. e., app., and possessing knowledge of the people of Paradise and of the people of Hell: for it seems that muHotawuwna , or the like, is to be understood before ElY ]. (Zj, TA.) [And hence it is the name of The Seventh Chapter of the Kur-án. ] By A^aSoHaAbu AlA^aEoraAfi [ The occupants of the AErAf ], there mentioned, are said to be meant persons whose good and evil works have been equal, so that they shall not have merited Paradise by the former nor Hell by the latter: or prophets: or angels. (Zj, TA.) ― -b5- See also EurofapN . ― -b6- [The pl.] A^aEoraAfN also signifies (tropical:) The higher, or highest, (K, TA,) and first, or foremost, (TA,) of winds; (K, TA;) and likewise of clouds, and of mists. (TA.) ― -b7- And EurofN signifies also, (As, O, K,) in the speech of the people of El-Bahreyn, (As, O,) A species [or variety ] of palm-trees; (As, O, K;) and so [the pl.] A^aEoraAfN (O, K) is expl. by IDrd: (O:) or when they first yield fruit, or edible fruit, or ripe fruit; (K, TA;) or when they attain to doing so: (TA:) or a [ sort of ] palmtree in El-Bahreyn, also called buro$uwm ; (K, TA;) but this is what is meant by As and IDrd. (TA.) ― -b8- And The tree of the A^utoruj~ [i. e. citrus medica, or citron ]. (K.) -A3- Also pl. of EaruwfN : ― -b2- and of A^aEorafu and EarofaA='u . (K.)

(assumed tropical:) Such a one came as though ruffling the feathers of his neck to do evil, or mischief ]. (TA.) definition: The place [or mountain ] where the pilgrims halt (Mgh, O, Msb, K) on the day of Earafap [above mentioned], (O, K,) [described by Burckhardt as a granite hill, about a mile, or a mile and a half, in...
sourceDefinition: The place [or mountain ] where the pilgrims halt (Mgh, O, Msb, K) on the day of Earafap [above mentioned], (O, K,) [described by Burckhardt as a granite hill, about a mile, or a mile and a half, in circuit, with sloping sides, rising nearly two hundred feet above the level of the adjacent plain,] said to be nine miles, (Msb,) or twelve miles, (K,) from Mekkeh; (Msb, K;) said by J to be a place in, or at, Minè, but incorrectly, (K, TA,) unless thereby be meant near Minè; (TA;) also called by some ↓ Earafapu ; (Mgh, Msb;) but the saying nazalonaA Earafapa , (S, O, K,) or nazalotu biEarafapa , (Msb,) [ We, or I, alighted at Earafap ,] is like a post-classical phrase, (S, O, K,) and (S, O) it is said to be (Msb) not genuine Arabic: (S, O, Msb:) EarafaAtN is a [proper] name in the pl. form, and therefore is not itself pluralized: (S, O, K:) it is as though the term EarafapN applied to every distinct portion thereof: (TA:) as Fr says, it has, correctly, no sing.; (S, O;) and it is determinate as denoting a particular place; (Sb, S, O, K, TA;) and therefore not admitting the article Al ; (Sb, TA;) differing from Alz~ayoduwna [because this is a proper name common to a number of persons]: you say, h`w^ulaA='i EarafaAtN HasanapF [lit. These are 'Arafát, in a good state ], putting the epithet in the accus. case because it is indeterminate [as a denotative of state, like muSad~iqFA in the saying wahuwa AlHaq~u muSad~iqFA limaA maEahumo , in the Kur ii. 85]: (S, O:) it is decl. ( maSoruwfapN [more properly muEorabapN ]) because the t is equivalent to the Y and w in musolimiyna and musolimuwna , (S, O, K,) the tenween becoming equivalent to the n , therefore, being used as a proper name, it is left in its original state, like as is musolimuwna when used as a proper name: (Akh, S, O, K:) [i. e.,] it is decl. in the manner of musolimaAtN and muw^ominaAtN , the tenween being like that which corresponds to the masc. pl. termination n , not the tenween of perfect declinability, because it is a proper name and of the fem. gender, wherefore it does not admit the article Al . (Msb.) EarafaAtN was thus named because Adam and Eve knew each other ( taEaArafaA ) there (IF, O, K, TA) after their descent from Paradise: (TA:) or because Gabriel, when he taught Abraham the rites and ceremonies of the pilgrimage, said to him “ Hast thou known? ” ( A^aEarafota ), (O, K,) and he replied “ I have known ” ( Earafotu ): (K:) or because it is a place sanctified and magnified, as though it were rendered fragrant ( Eur~ifa i. e. Tuy~iba ): (O, K:) or because the people know one another ( yataEaArafuwna ) there: or, accord. to Er-Rághib, because of men's making themselves known ( nitaEar~ufi AlEibaAdi ) there by religious services and prayers. (TA.)

definition: ― -b2- [Hence,] One who knows his companions: pl.
sourceDefinition: : see EaArifN , first sentence. ― -b2- [Hence,] One who knows his companions: pl. EurafaA='u . (O, K.) The chief, or head, (Mgh, K, TA,) of a people, or party; (K, TA;) because he knows the states, or conditions, of those over whom he acts as such; (Mgh;) or because he is known as such [so that it is from the same word in the last of the senses assigned to it in this paragraph]; (K;) or because of his acquaintance with the ordering, or management, of them: (TA:) or the naqiyb [or intendant, superintendent, overseer, or inspector, who takes cognizance of, and is responsible for, the actions of a people], who is below the ray^iys : (S, O, K:) or the manager and superintendent of the affairs, who acquaints himself with the circumstances, or a tribe, or of a company of men; of the measure faEiylN in the sense of the measure faAEilN : (IAth, TA:) or the orderer, or manager, of the affairs of a people, or party; as also ↓ EaArifN : (Msb:) pl. as above: (S, IAth, Msb:) it is said that he is over a few persons, and the manokib is over five EuraqaA=' , then the A^amiyr is over these. (Msb.) It is said in a trad. that the EurafaA=' are in Hell, as a caution against undertaking the office of chief, or head, on account of the trial that is therein; for when one does not perform the duty thereof, he sins, and deserves punishment. (TA.) ― -b3- [It is now used as meaning A monitor in a school, who hears the lessons of the other scholars. ] -A2- See also maEoruwfN , with which it is syn.

definition: A kaAhin [or diviner ]: (S, O, Msb, K:) or the former is one who informs of the past, and the latter is one who informs of the past and of the future: (Msb:) or, accord.
sourceDefinition: A kaAhin [or diviner ]: (S, O, Msb, K:) or the former is one who informs of the past, and the latter is one who informs of the past and of the future: (Msb:) or, accord. to Er-Rághib, [but the converse of his explanation seems to be that which is correct,] the former is one who informs of future events, and the latter is one who informs of past events. (TA.) Hence the saying of the Prophet, that whoso comes to an Er~Af and asks him respecting a thing, prayer of forty nights will not be accepted from him. (O.) ― -b2- And (Msb) An astrologer, (IAth, Mgh, Msb,) who lays claim to the knowledge of hidden, or invisible, things, (IAth, Mgh,) which God has made to belong exclusively to Himself: (IAth:) and this is [said to be] meant in the trad. above mentioned. (Mgh.) ― -b3- And A physician. (S, O, K.) ― -b4- And One who smells [for ysm I read ya$um~u ] the ground, and thus knows the places of water, and knows in what country, or district, he is. (ISh, in TA, art. HzY .)

definition: and ↓ EariyfN are syn.
sourceDefinition: and ↓ EariyfN are syn., (S, O, K,) like EaAlimN and EaliymN , (S, O,) signifying Knowing; [&c., agreeably with the explanations of the verb in the first quarter of the first paragraph of this art.;] as also ↓ EaruwfapN , (S, O, K,) but in an intensive sense, which is denoted by the p , (S, O, TA,) meaning [ knowing, &c., much, or well; or] knowing, or acquainted with, affairs, and not failing to know [or recognise ] one that has been seen once; (TA;) as in the phrase, biAlA^umuwir ↓ rajulN EaruwfapN [ A man much, or well, acquainted with affairs ]. (S, O.) ― -b2- For the first, see also EariyfN . ― -b3- It also signifies particularly [ Skilled in divine things; ] possessing knowledge of God, and of his kingdom, and of the way of dealing well with Him. (TA.) ― -b4- See also maEoruwfN . -A2- Also, the first, [ Patient; or] very patient, or having much patience; syn. SabuwrN ; (AO, S, O, K;) and so ↓ EaruwfN ; (S, O, K;) of which latter the pl. is EurofN . (K.) One says, A^uSiyba fulaAnN fawujida EaArifFA [ Such a one was smitten, or afflicted, and was found to be patient ]. (S, O.) And Habasotu nafosFA EaArifapF , meaning SaAbirapF [i. e. I restrained a patient soul, or mind ]: (O, TA:) like the phrase Sabarotu EaArifapF in a verse of 'Antarah [cited in the first paragraph of art. Sbr ]. (S, * O.) And ↓ nafosN EaruwfN means [ A soul, or mind, ] enduring; very patient; that endures an event, or a case, when made to experience it. (TA.) EawaArifu [is pl. of EaArifapN , and] means Patient she-camels. (IB, TA.)

definition: is mentioned in “ the Book ” of Sb as used in the phrase h`*aA A^aEorafa mino h`*aA [meaning This is more known than this ]: irregularly formed from maEoruwfN , not from EaArifN .
sourceDefinition: is mentioned in “ the Book ” of Sb as used in the phrase h`*aA A^aEorafa mino h`*aA [meaning This is more known than this ]: irregularly formed from maEoruwfN , not from EaArifN . (ISd, TA.) -A2- Also A thing having what is termed Eurof [i. e. a mane, or the like ]: (S, O, K:) fem. EarofaA='u : pl., masc. and fem., EurofN . (K.) It is applied to a horse, (Mgh, K, TA,) meaning Having a full mane, or much hair of the mane. (Mgh, TA.) And to a serpent (O, K) such as is termed $ayoTaAn [which is described as having an Eurof ]. (O.) And the fem. is applied to a she-camel, (K, TA,) meaning High in the hump: or resembling the male: or long in her Eurof [or mane ]: (TA:) or having what resembles the Eurof by reason of her fatness: or having, upon her neck, fur like the Eurof . (Ham p. 611.) ― -b2- The fem. is also used as meaning The DabuE [i. e. hyena, or female hyena ], because of the abundance of its hair (S, O, K, TA) of the neck, (O, K, TA,) or because of the length of its Eurof . (TA.) ― -b3- And one says sanaAmN A^aEorafu A long, or tall, camel's hump, having an Eurof . (TA.) And jabalN A^aEorafu (assumed tropical:) A mountain having what resembles the Eurof . (TA.) And qul~apN EarofaA='u (tropical:) A high mountain-top. (TA.) And HazonN A^aEorafu (assumed tropical:) High rugged ground. (TA.)

definition: (S, O, K [in one of my copies of the S written muEar~afN ]) and maEorifN also (Ham p.
sourceDefinition: (S, O, K [in one of my copies of the S written muEar~afN ]) and maEorifN also (Ham p. 47) sing. of maEaArifu , which means The face [and faces ], and any part thereof that appears; as in the saying AimoraA^apN Hasanapu AlmaEaArifi [ A woman beautiful in the face, or in the parts thereof that appear ]; (S, O, K;) because the person is known thereby: (TA:) or, as some say, no sing. of it is known: (Har p. 146:) and some say that it signifies the beauties, or beautiful parts, of the face. (TA.) Er-Rá'ee says, mutalaf~imiyna EalaY maEaArifinaA navoniY lahun~a HawaA$iYa AlEaSobi [ Muffling our faces, or the parts thereof that appeared, we fold, or folding, to them the selvages of the EaSob (a sort of garment).] (S, O: but the latter has mutalav~imiyna .) And one says, Hay~aA A@ll~`hu AlmaEaArifa , meaning [ May God preserve ] the faces. (O, K.) And qado haAjato maEaArifu fulaAnK The features of such a one, whereby he was known to me, have withered, like as the plant withers: said of a man who has turned away, from the speaker, his love, or affection. (TA.) And huwa mina AlmaEaArifi He is of those who are known; [or of those who are acquaintances; ] (O, K;) as though meaning mino *awiY AlmaEaArifi , i. e. of those having faces [ whereby they are known ]: (O:) or maEaArifu Alr~ajuli means Those who are entitled to the man's love, or affection, and with whom he has acquaintance; [and simply the acquaintances of the man; ] and is pl. of ↓ maEorifapN . (Har p. 146.) maEaArifu AlA^aroDi means The faces, and known parts, of the land. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: [inf. n. of EaSila , q. v.:] A twisting in the Easiyb [or bone, or slender part, or part where the hair grows, ] of the tail (S, O, K) of the horse, (K,) so that a portion of the inner side upon which is no hair appears, (S, O,) or so that it hits [ the flesh of the part of the thigh that is called ] his kaA*ap and [ the flesh upon the socket of the hip, or the vein in the thigh, that is called ] his faAy^il . (K, TA. [In the CK, qaAy^ilahu is erroneously put for faAy^ilahu .]) And Crookedness with hardness: (K:) or crookedness and strength or hardness of a canine tooth. (S, O.) -A2- Also sing. of A^aEoSaAlN signifying The intestines into which the food passes from the stomach; (As, S, O, K;) and it (the sing.) is also pronounced ↓ EiSolN . (K.) ― -b2- And Wreathed, or twisting, and curved, sands: occurring in this sense in a trad. (TA.) ― -b3- And Certain trees which, when the camel eats thereof, cause him to void thin dung: (S, O:) or the trees called difolaY [q. v.]: (K:) or certain trees resembling the difolaY , which the camels eat, and after which they drink water every day: or, as some say, [ trees of the kind called ] HamoD that grow upon, or at, the waters: (TA:) a single tree thereof is called EaSalapN . (S, O, K. [See also EaDalapN , in art. EDl .]) [Accord. to Forskål (Flora Aegypt. Arab. pp. cxiv. and 110) now applied to a species of Ocymum which he terms serpyllifolium. ]

AlbaSalu Albar~iY~u ; (O, K;) also called baSalu AlfaA^ori ; (K;) [see art. bSl ;] and a vinegar is prepared from it: (S, TA:) IAar says that it is a certain plant in the deserts, of which they assert that longing pregnant women desire it and eat it, and that it is what is called AlbaSalu Albar~iY~u : AHn says, it consists of leaves like the leek, appearing extended and lank: and in one place he says, it is a certain tree [or plant ] of the plain, or soft, tracts, growing in places of water and moisture, in like manner as does the mawozap [?], and it has a blossom like that of the white sawosan [or lily ], of which the bees eat, and make honey; and the oxen, in cases of drought, eat its leaves, which are mixed for them in the fodder: (TA:) it is good for the alopecia, and hemiplegia ( AlfaAlij ), and sciatica; and the vinegar thereof, for chronic cough, and asthma, and the rattles; and strengthens the weak body: (K:) the pl. is EanaASilu . (S, O.) ― -b2- A^axa*a fiY Tariyqi AlEunoSulayoni (S, O) and Tryq AlEunoSuli , (S,) [ He entered upon, or took to, the road of AlEnSlyn and AlEnSl ,] a road from El-Yemámeh to El-Basrah, is said of a man as meaning (assumed tropical:) he went astray: (S, O:) but AHát says that he asked As respecting Tryq AlEnSlyn , and he pronounced the latter word with fet-h to the S ; adding that it should not be pronounced with damm; and that the saying originated from ElFarezdak's mentioning, in his poetry, a man who went astray in this road. (O.) One says also, salaka Tariyqa AlEnSlyni , meaning (assumed tropical:) He pursued that which was false, vain, or futile. (TA.)

EaqoSN , (Lth, S, Mgh, IAth, Msb,) She (a woman, Lth, Msb) twisted her hair, and inserted the ends thereof into the parts next the roots: (Mgh, IAth, Msb:) this is the primary signification: (IAth:) or she took each lock of her hair, and twisted it, then tied it, so that there remained in it a twisting, and then let it hang down; (Lth, O; *) each of the said locks is termed EaqiySapN : (Lth:) and she tied her hair upon the back of her neck: (TA:) and she plaited her hair: (Msb:) or EaqoSu Al$~aEari signifies the gathering of the hair together upon the head: (Mgh:) or the plaiting of the hair: and the twisting it upon the head: (S:) and you say, EaqaSa $aEarahu , aor. as above, (and so the inf. n., O,) meaning, he plaited his hair: and he twisted it. (A, O, K.) -A2- EaqiSa , (S, TA,) aor. , (TA,) inf. n. EaqaSN , [q. v.], (S, O, TA,) (tropical:) He was, or became, niggardly, or close-handed, (S, O, * TA,) and evil in disposition. (S.) ― -b2- And EaqiSato EalaY~a Ald~aAb~apu [as also EakiSato ] (tropical:) The beast became restive, or refractory, to me, and stopped. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: A string with which the ends of the *awaAy^ib [or locks of hair hanging down loosely from the middle of the head to the back ] are tied: (O, Msb, K:) or a thong with which the hair is gathered together: (Mgh:) pl. (O, * TA.)

definition: A portion of a woman's hair which is twisted, and of which the ends are inserted into the parts next the roots;
sourceDefinition: A portion of a woman's hair which is twisted, and of which the ends are inserted into the parts next the roots; (IAth, * Msb;) as also ↓ EiqoSapN : (Msb:) or a lock of a woman's hair which she twists, then ties, so that there remains in it a twisting, and then lets hang down: (Lth, A:) [i. e., a twisted lock of a woman's hair, which either has its end inserted into the part next the roots, or is tied, and left to hang down: ] or i. q. DafayrapN ; as also ↓ EiqoSapN ; (S, O, K;) the latter on the authority of A'Obeyd: (S:) pl. (of the former, S, A, Msb, TA) EaqaAy^iSu , (S, A, Msb, K,) and (of the latter, S, Msb) EiqaSN , (S, O, Msb, K,) and (of the former also, S, Msb, and of the latter also, S, TA) EiqaASN , (S, O, Msb, K,) of which A'Obeyd cites the following ex. in a verse of Imra-el-Keys: gadaAy^iruhu musota$oziraAtN A_ilaY AlEulaY taDil~u AlEiqaASu fiY muvan~FY wamurosali [ Its pendent locks being twisted upwards, the twists becoming concealed among hair doubled and hair made to hang down ]: or, as some say, it [ EqAS ] signifies what a woman makes, of her hair, like a pomegranate; each lock of which is termed EaqiySapN ; the pl. being EiqaASN and EaqaAy^iSu . (S, O.) [See also EiqaASN as expl. by IAar, above.] EiqaASN is also used in the sense of *awaAy^ibu [or Locks of hair hanging down loosely from the middle of the head to the back ]. (Mgh. [But this is said in relation to an instance of its occurrence in which it may with propriety be regarded as pl. of EaqiySapN or EiqoSapN in any of the senses before explained.])

definition: , (S, Mgh, O, Msb, TA,) aor.
sourceDefinition: , (S, Mgh, O, Msb, TA,) aor. , (Msb,) inf. n. EalaqN (S, O, Msb, KL, TA) and EalqapN (L, TA) [and app. EuluwqN also, as will be seen from what follows]; and ↓ tEl~q , (S, MA, Mgh, O, Msb,) and ↓ AEtlq ; (O, Msb, KL;) It hung to it; it was, or became, suspended to it: (so the first and last accord. to the KL, and the second accord. to the MA and common usage: [in the S and Mgh and O, it is merely said that the first and second signify the same:]) [and] it clung, caught, clave, adhered, held, or stuck fast, to it; (Msb in explanation of all, and TA * in explanation of the first;) and so ↓ tEl~qhu . (S, * O, * TA.) It is said in a prov., (S, O, TA,) asserted in the K to have been mentioned before, which is not found to be the case, (TA,) waSar~a Aljunodabu ↓ Ealiqato maEaAliqahaA (S, O, K, [in the CK, erroneously, muEAliqahA ,]) [ It (the bucket, Ald~alowu , Z, TA) has become suspended in its places of suspension, and the jndb (accord. to the S and K a species of locust) has creaked ]: originating from the fact that a man went to a well, and suspended his well-rope to the rope thereof, and then went to the owner of the well, and claimed to be his neighbour [and therefore to have a right to the use of the well]; but the owner refused his assent, and ordered him to depart; whereupon he uttered these words, meaning The heat has come, [see Sar~a Aljunodabu in art. jdb ,] and I am not able to depart. (S, O. [See more in Freytag's Arab. Prov. ii. 91.]) And one says, Ealiqa Al$~awoku biAlv~awobi , aor. , inf. n. EalaqN ; and bihi ↓ tEl~q ; meaning The thorns clung, caught, &c., to the garment. (Msb.) And ZuforiY biAl$~aYo'i ↓ AEtlq My nail clung, caught, &c., to the thing. (Msb.) And Ealiqa AlZ~aboYu fiY AlHibaAlapi , (S, O,) or AlS~ayodu ; (K;) or Ealiqa AlwaHo$u biA@loHibaAlapi , inf. n. EuluwqN , (Msb,) [ The gazelle, or the animal of the chase, became caught, or stuck fast, in the snare; or the wild animal became caught, or held fast, thereby, or] became withheld from getting loose [ thereby ]: whence the saying, Ealiqa AlxaSomu bixaSomihi and bihi ↓ tEl~q [ The antagonist became held fast, or withheld from getting loose, by his antagonist; and also the antagonist clung, or held fast, to his antagonist ]. (Msb.) [― -b2- The primary significations are those mentioned above in the first sentence: and hence several other significations here following. ― -b3- Ealiqa EalaY ka*aA and Ealayohi ↓ tEl~q It depended upon such a thing, as a condition. ― -b4- Ealiqa bihi and ↓ tEl~q It pertained to him, or it: it concerned him, or it. And He had a hold upon it: he had a concern in it. ] ― -b5- EaliqahaA , (S, O,) or Ealiqahu , (K,) and Ealiqa bihaA , (S, O,) or bihi , (K,) inf. n. EuluwqN (S, O, K) and EalaqN (K [and mentioned also in the S and O but app. as a simple subst.]) and EiloqN [but see this below voce EalaqN ] and EalaAqapN , (K,) [ He became attached by love to her, or to him; ] he loved (S, O, K) her, (S, O,) or him; (K;) and so Ealiqa Hub~uhaA biqalobihi ; (S, O;) and ↓ tEl~qhA , and tEl~q bihaA ; [the former of these two phrases being used for the latter, agreeably with a saying of IAmb cited in the TA in art. ArY , that taEal~aqotu fulaAnFA is for tEl~qt bifulaAnK ;] like ↓ AEtlq [i. e. AEtlqhA and AEtlq bhA ], (K,) or AEtlqhu , (S,) or AEtlq bihi ; (TA;) and ↓ Eul~iqahaA , (S, * O, * K, TA,) from EalaAqapu AlHub~i , (S, O, TA,) and bihaA ↓ Eul~iqa , (TA,) [but this last verb is more commonly trans. by itself, for ex.,] El-Aashà says, Eul~iqotuhaA EaraDFA waEul~iqato rajulFA gayoriY waEul~iqa A^uxoraY gayorahaA Alr~ajulu [ I became attached to her accidentally, and she became attached to a man other than me, and the man became attached to another female, other than her ]. (S, O. [See also another ex., in a verse of 'Antarah, cited voce zaEama .]) [See also EalaqN , below.] ― -b6- ↓ Ealiqato minohu kul~a maEolaqK [which may be rendered She captivated him wholly ] occurs in a trad. as [virtually] meaning he loved her, and was vehemently desirous of her. (TA.) ― -b7- Ealiqato nafosuhu Al$~aYo'a His soul, or mind, clung to the thing persistently. (L, TA.) ― -b8- ↓ qado Ealiqa Alkibaru maEaAliqahu [app. meaning Old age has taken hold in its holding places, or, agreeably with what is said in the next sentence, has had its effects ], in which mEAlq is pl. of maEolaqN , is said to an old man. (TA.) And of everything that has had its effect [so I here render waqaEa mawoqiEahu , but see art. wqE ], one says, Ealiqa ↓ maEaAliqahu . (TA, and Ham p. 172.) ― -b9- Ealiqato maraAsiyhaA bi*iY ramoraAmK [ Their anchors have clung to a place having the species of herbage called rmrAm , meaning they are abiding therein, (see mirosaApN , in art. rsw ,)] is said of camels when they are at rest, or at ease, and their eyes are refreshed by the pasturage; and is a prov., applied to persons in the like condition by reason of their means of subsistence. (TA.) ― -b10- Ealiqa bihi , inf. n. EalaqN , He contended with him in an altercation [as though clinging to him]; disputed with him; or litigated with him. (TA.) ― -b11- laA yaEolaqu bika means lA yaliyqu bk [ It will not be suitable to thee; it will not befit thee ]. (S and K in art. lyq .) ― -b12- Ealiqa yafoEalu ka*aA He set about, began, or betook himself to, doing such a thing. (S, O, K.) faEaliquwA wajohahu DarobFA occurs in a trad., meaning They set about, or betook themselves to, smiting his face. (TA.) And a rájiz says, Ealiqa HawoDiY nugarN mukib~u [ Nughar (a species of birds) bending down their heads ] betook themselves to coming for the purpose of drinking to my HwD [or watering-trough ]: or, as some say, liked it, and frequented it. (S, O.) ― -b13- And maA Ealiqotu A^aqowluhu means I did not cease saying it; like mA na$ibotu . (A in art. n$b .) [Thus Ealiqa has two contr. meanings.] ― -b14- Ealiqati AlA_ibilu AlEiDaAha , (S, O, K,) aor. ; (K;) and Ealaqat likewise, aor. ; (S, O, K;) inf. n. EaloqN ; (S, O, K; *) The camels fed upon the upper, or uppermost, portions of the [ trees called ] EDAh , (S, O, K,) reaching them with their mouths: (S and O in explanation of the latter verb:) and yaEolaqu AlEiDaAha , said of a camel, he plucks from the EDAh , [as though] hanging from it, by reason of his tallness: (S: in one of my copies of the S, and in the TA, yaEoluqu :) or one says, of camels, Ealaqato mina Al$~ajari , aor. , inf. n. EaloqN and EuluwqN , meaning they ate of the trees with their mouths: and Ealiqato fiY AlwaAdiY , aor. , they pastured, or pastured where they pleased, in the valley: (Msb:) accord. to Lh, Ealaqato , aor. , inf. n. EaloqN , said of beasts, means they ate the leaves of the trees: and accord. to As, Ealaqato , aor. , inf. n. EuluwqN , means they reached and took with their mouths. (TA.) Hence, (TA,) it is said in a trad., A^arowaAHu Al$~uhadaA='i fiY HawaASili TayorK xuDorK taEoluqu mino waraqi Aljan~api , (S, Msb, *) or mino vimaAri Aljan~api , (TA,) and, as some relate it, taEolaqu , (Msb, TA,) [both as meaning The souls of the martyrs are in the crops of green birds that eat of the leaves, or fruits, of Paradise, ] but the former relation is that which should be followed, because the latter requires that one should say fiY wrq Aljn~p [or fY vmAr Aljn~p ], though the latter is said to be the more common. (Msb.) One says also, Ealiqati AlA_ibilu , aor. , inf. n. EalaqN , meaning The camels ate of the Euloqap of the trees, i. e., of the trees that remain in the winter and of which the camels are fed until they attain to the rabiyE [meaning spring, or springherbage ]; as also ↓ tEl~qt . (TA.) And Ealaqa , inf. n. EalaAqN and EuluwqN , He ate. (TA.) And AlS~abiY~u yaEoluqu The child sucks his fingers. (TA.) ― -b15- Ealaqahu bilisaAnihi [inf. n. EaloqN ] He blamed, or censured, him; he said to him that which he disliked, or hated. (Lh, K, * TA.) ― -b16- Ealiqa A^amorahu He knew his affair. (K.) ― -b17- Ealiqati AlmaroA^apu , (S, Mgh, O, K,) inf. n. EuluwqN , (Mgh,) or EalaqN , (TA,) The woman conceived, or became pregnant. (S, Mgh, O, K.) Hence the saying, AlgiraAsu tabad~alu biAlEuluwqi (tropical:) [ The set, or shoot that is planted, becomes changed by pullulating ]; a metaphorical phrase; meaning that what is planted becomes changed because it increases and rises when it clings to the earth and germinates. EaloqN ] He blamed, or censured, him; he said to him that which he disliked, or hated. (Lh, K, * TA.) ― -b16- Ealiqa A^amorahu He knew his affair. sourceDefinition: , (S, O, Msb, K,) i. e. Al$~aYo'a , (S, O, Msb,) inf. n. taEoliyqN ; (S, O, K;) and ↓ AElqhu , (S, * O, * Msb,) and ↓ tEl~qhu ; (S, O, K;) signify the same. (S, O, Msb, K.) You say, El~q Al$~aYo'a biAl$~aYo'i , (Mgh, Msb, K,) inf. n. as above, He hung, or suspended, the thing to the thing; and so mina Al$~aYo'i , and Ealayohi : (TA:) [and] he made the thing to cling, catch, cleave, adhere, hold, or stick fast, to the thing; as also bihi ↓ AElqhu . (Msb.) [For ex.,] one says, Eal~aqotu ri$aAy^iY biri$aAy^ika [ I have suspended my well-rope to thy well-rope ]: and ri$aA='ahu biri$aA='i Albiy^ori ↓ A^aEolaqa [ He suspended his well-rope to the rope of the well ]. (S, O.) [See also an ex. of the latter verb in a verse cited voce raAfiDN .] And El~qhu EalaY Alwatidi [ He hung it on the peg ]: and in like manner, El~q Al$~aYo'a xalofahu [ He hung the thing behind him ]; as, for instance, a Haqiybap , &c., behind the camel's saddle. (TA.) And maEaA*apF ↓ tEl~q He hung ( Eal~aqa ) upon himself an amulet. (S, O.) And biAlgarobi baEiyrayoni ↓ AElq He coupled two camels to the end of the well-rope [ to the other end of which was attached the large bucket ]. (IF, K.) [And in like manner they say in the present day, El~q Alxayola fiY AlEarabapi He harnessed, or attached, the horses to the carriage. ] And A^aZofaArahu fiY Al$~aYo'i ↓ AElq He made his nails to cling, catch, or cleave, to the thing. (S, TA.) And [in like manner,] El~q yadahu and ↓ AElqhA [ He made his hands to cling, &c.], followed by fY before the object: both signify the same. (TA.) And El~q Ald~aAb~apa , meaning El~q EalayohaA [for El~q ElyhA AlmixolaApa , agreeably with modern usage, i. e. He hung upon the beast the nose-bag containing barley, or the like; or he supplied the beast with Ealiyq , which means barley, or the like, that is hung upon the beast ]. (TA.) [And hence, as is indicated in the T and TA, El~q signifies, by a metaphor, (tropical:) He supplied with Ealiyq as meaning wine. ] And El~q raAHilatahu He loosed the halter, or leading-rope, from the muzzle of his riding-camel and threw it [or hung it ] upon her shoulders, to give her ease. (TA.) ― -b2- [The primary significations are those mentioned in the second sentence of this paragraph: and hence several other significations here following. ― -b3- El~qhu bika*aA , and EalaY ka*aA , He made it to depend upon such a thing, as a condition. ] You say, Eal~aqotu Eitoqa EabodiY bimawotiY [ I made the freedom of my slave to depend upon my death ]. (TA in art. dbr .) ― -b4- A_ino A^anoTiqo A^uTal~aqo waA_ino A^asokuto A^uEal~aqo , in the story of Umm-Zara, means [ If I speak, I am divorced; and if I be silent, I am left in suspense, i. e.,] he leaves me like that which is suspended, (O, TA,) neither retained nor divorced. (TA.) [And similar to this is the phrase taEoliyqu A^afoEaAli Alquluwbi The suspending of the verbs significant of operations of the mind from government, as to the letter but not as to the meaning: ] see muEal~aqN . ― -b5- [ El~q AlbinaA='a He made the building, or structure, pensile, i. e. supported above the ground, or above a stage or floor, by pillars or piers or otherwise. Hence,] the saying naqabuwA AlHaAy^iTa waEal~aquwhu means They dug beneath the wall [or made a hole through it ] and left it [or rendered it ] muEal~aqFA [i. e. pensile, or supported above the ground, being partially hollowed beneath]. (Mgh.) ― -b6- [ El~q fiY HaA$iyapi kitaAbK He appended a note in the margin of a book or writing. ] ― -b7- El~q baAbFA He set up, and fixed, a door, (Mgh, TA,) EalaY daArihi [ upon, or to, his house ]. (Mgh.) ― -b8- And (TA) He closed, or made fast, a door, with a kind of latch, or sliding bolt; syn. A^azolajahu , (O, TA,) or A^arotajahu ; (K;) as also ↓ AElqhu . (TA.) [See miEolaAqN .] ― -b9- Eul~iqahaA , and Eul~iqa bihaA , in which the pronoun denoting the object relates to a woman: see 1, former half. ― -b10- Eal~aqa fulaAnN dama fulaAnK [app. meaning Such a one attached to himself responsibility for the blood of such a one ] is said when the former is the slayer of the latter. (TA. [Thus I find the phrase there written: but perhaps the right reading is Eul~iqa .]) ― -b11- Eal~aqahu also signifies He joined him, and overtook him. (TA.) ― -b12- And He learned it, and took it or received it [from another]. (TA.) ― -b13- Eal~iquwA ramaqahu bi$aYo'K Give ye to him something that shall stay, or arrest, what remains in him of life. (Z, TA.) ― -b14- Eal~aqotu maEa fulaAnK EaliyqapF , (S, TA,) and maEa Alqawomi , (TA,) I sent with such a one, (S, TA,) and with the people, or party, (TA,) a camel for the purpose of bringing corn for me upon it. (S, TA. [See EaliyqapN .]) AiroDa mina Almarokabi biAlt~aEoliyqi is a prov., said to a man who is thereby enjoined to be content with a part of that which he wants, instead of the whole thereof; like him who rides the camel termed Ealiyqap one time after another time: [so that it means Be thou content, instead of the riding constantly, or instead of the beast that is ridden only, with the sending a camel to bring corn, upon which thou mayest ride occasionally:] (TA:) or the meaning may be, be thou content, instead of thy riding, with the hanging of thy goods upon the beast: or the meaning may be, be thou content, in respect of the beast that is ridden, with the hanging [thy goods] upon him in thy turn. (Meyd.) ― -b15- And one says, Eal~iqo linaAqatiki , meaning Go thou from thy she-camel ( Aimo$i EanohaA ). (O.)

definition: Anything hung, or suspended.
sourceDefinition: Anything hung, or suspended. (K.) ― -b2- The suspensory [ cord ] of the bakorap [or pulley of a well ]; (K;) the apparatus of the bikorap , by which it is suspended: (S, O:) and the bakorap [or pulley ] itself; (K, TA;) as some say; and the pl. is A^aEolaAqN : (TA:) or [in the CK “ and ”] the wellrope and the large bucket and the miHowar [or pin on which the sheave of the pulley turns ] (K, TA) and the pulley, (TA,) all together; (K, TA;) so says Lh: (TA:) or all the apparatus for drawing water by means of the pulley; comprising the two pieces of wood at the head of the well, the two upper extremities of which are connected by a rope and then fastened to the ground by means of another rope, the two ends of this being extended to two pegs fixed in the ground; the pulley is suspended to the upper parts of the two pieces of wood, and the water is drawn by means of it with two buckets by two drawers: it signifies only the saAniyap [here meaning the large bucket with its apparatus ] and all the apparatus consisting of the xuT~aAf [or bent piece of iron which is on each side of the sheave of the pulley and in which is the pin whereon the sheave turns ] and the miHowar [or pin itself ] and the sheave and the naEaAmataAni [app. here meaning the two pieces of wood mentioned above, agreeably with an explanation mentioned voce zuronuwqN ,] and the ropes thereof: so says As, on the authority of Arabs: (TA:) or the rope that is suspended to the pulley: (K:) or, as some say, the rope that is at the upper part of the pulley. (TA.) ― -b3- And The suspensory of a qirobap [or water-skin]; i. e. Ealaqu Alqirobapi signifies the strap by which the qrbp is suspended; (TA;) i. q. EaraquhaA : (S, O, K, TA:) or the thing with which it is tied and then suspended: or what has remained in it of the grease with which it is greased. (TA.) One says, ja$imotu A_ilayoka Ealaqa Alqirobapi [expl. in arts. j$m and Erq ]. (S, O.) ― -b4- Also [ Leeches; ] certain worms, (S,) or certain things resembling worms, (Mgh, Msb,) or certain small creeping things, (O,) or a [ species of ] small creeping thing, (K,) black, (Mgh, Msb,) or red, (TA,) found in water, (S, O, Msb, K,) and having the property of sucking blood, (S, O, K, TA,) and employed to suck the blood from the throat and from sanguineous tumours: (TA:) they cling (Mgh, Msb) to the Hanak [q. v.] (Mgh) or to the fauces (Msb) of the beast when he drinks, (Mgh, Msb,) and suck the blood: (Msb:) one thereof is termed EalaqapN . (S, O, Msb.) ― -b5- And Clay that clings to the hand. (K.) ― -b6- And Blood, in a general sense: or intensely red blood: (K:) or thick blood: (S, O, K:) or clotted blood, (K, TA,) before it becomes dry: (TA:) or clotted, thick, blood; because of its clinging together: (Mgh:) and EalaqapN signifies a portion thereof: (S, Mgh, O, K:) or this signifies a little portion of thick blood: (Jel in xcvi. 2:) or a portion [or lump ] of clotted blood: (TA:) or the seminal fluid, after its appearance, when it becomes thick, clotted, blood; after which it passes to another stage, becoming flesh, and is what is termed muDogapN . (Msb. [See Kur xxiii. 14.]) -A2- Also [ Attachment, as meaning] tenacious love: (K:) and [simply] love, or desirous love, (Lh, S, O, K, TA,) of a man for a woman: (Lh, TA:) or love cleaving to the heart; (TA;) and so ↓ EalaAqpN and ↓ EilaAqapN ; or the former of these two relates to love and the like and the latter relates to a whip and the like [as will be expl. below under the two words]. (K.) [In this sense it is originally an inf. n., of which the verb is Ealiqa .] One says, A_in~ahu la*uw EalaqK fiY fulaAnapa Verily he is one having love, or desirous love, for such a woman: (Lh, TA:) thus made trans. by means of fY . (TA.) And naZorapN mino *iY EalaqK A look from one having love, or desirous love: (S, O, TA:) a prov. (TA.) ― -b2- See also EalaAqapN , first quarter. ― -b3- Also Pertinacious contention in an altercation; or such disputation or litigation. (K. [In this sense it is originally an inf. n., of which the verb is Ealiqa . And EalaAqapN , q. v., has a similar signification.]) ― -b4- See also EuloqapN , second sentence. -A3- And see EaloqN . -A4- Also The main [or middle ] part [or beaten track ] of a road. (Ibn-'Abbád, O, K.) [See an ex. of the pl. ( A^aEolaAqN ) in a verse cited voce EamoqN .]

definition: A small garment, (S, O,) the first garment that is made for a boy: (S, O, K:) or a shirt without sleeves: or a garment in which is cut an opening for the head to be put through it, [ so that nearly...
sourceDefinition: A small garment, (S, O,) the first garment that is made for a boy: (S, O, K:) or a shirt without sleeves: or a garment in which is cut an opening for the head to be put through it, [ so that nearly one half of it falls down before the wearer and the corresponding portion behind, ] not having its two sides sewn [ together ]; it is worn by a girl; (K, TA;) like the Sudorap ; she uses it for service and work; (TA;) and it extends to the place of the waist-band: (K, TA: [see also A_itobN :]) or a garment held in high estimation; (K, TA;) like EiloqN [mentioned before]; worn by a man: one says of him who has not upon him costly garments, maA Ealayohi EiloqapN [ He has not upon him costly attire ]. (TA.) ― -b2- And A shield. (Ibn- 'Abbád, O, TA. [This last meaning is also assigned to EiloqN , as mentioned before.]) -A2- And A certain tree, used for tanning. (K.) -A3- A_ibil layosa bihaA EliqapN is a phrase mentioned by Ibn-'Abbád, (O, TA,) as meaning [app.] ASrp . (TA. [This word, in the TA, is blurred: and in the O, the place that it occupied has perished: I think that it is most probably A^aSir~apN , pl. of SiraArN ; and therefore that the phrase means Camels not having upon them strings, or pieces of rag, bound upon their udders or teats, to prevent their young ones from sucking: for one says Sar~a biAln~aAqapi as well as Sar~a Aln~aAqapa ; and in like manner, I suppose, one may say layosa bihaA A^aSir~apN : and hence, perhaps, it may mean not having milk: see the phrase maA biAln~aAqapi EaluwqN .]) -A4- [For the phrase AisotaA^oSala A@ll~`hu EiloqaAtahuimo , see the next paragraph but one.]

definition: , (S, O, K,) like sakoraY , (K,) A certain plant: (S, O, K:) accord.
sourceDefinition: , (S, O, K,) like sakoraY , (K,) A certain plant: (S, O, K:) accord. to Sb, (S, O,) it is used as sing. and pl.; (S, O, K;) and its alif [written Y ] is to denote the fem. gender, therefore it is without tenween: but others say that its alif is to render it quasi-coordinate [to the quadriliteral-radical class], and is with tenween, the n. un. being EaloqaApN : (S, O:) IJ says that the alif in EaloqaApN is not to denote the fem. gender, because it is followed by p ; but when they elide the p , they say EaloqaY , without tenween: (L, TA: [in both of which, more is added, but with some mistranscription or omission rendering it inconsistent:]) its twigs are slender, difficult to be broken, and brooms are made of it: (K: [but this is taken from what here follows:]) Aboo-Nasr says, the ElqY is a tree [or plant ] of which the greenness continues during the hot season, and its places of growth are the sands, and the plain, or soft, tracts: and he says, an Arab of the desert showed me a plant which he asserted to be the ElqY ; having long and slender twigs, and delicate leaves; called in Pers. xulowaAm [?]; those who collect [ the dung used for fuel called ] jal~ap make of it brooms for that purpose: to which he adds, and it is said, on the authority of the early Arabs, that the ElqAp is a certain tree [or plant ] which is found in the sands, green, having leaves, but in which is no good: (O:) [it is said, however, that] the decoction thereof is drunk for the dropsy. (K.)

sourceDefinition: A thing that clings, cleaves, or sticks fast, ( yaEolaqu , [in the CK taEal~aqa ,]) to a man. (S, O, K.) ― -b2- And [hence,] Death, or the decree of death; syn. maniy~apN ; (S, O, K;) as also ↓ Eal~aAqapN , (S, TA,) accord. to the K, erroneously, EalaAqap [without teshdeed]: in a verse in which it occurs, some explain AlEal~aAqapu as meaning thus; and some, as meaning the serpent, because of its clinging. (TA.) El-Mufaddal En-Nukree says, waqado Ealiqato bivaEolabapa AlEaluwqu [ When death, or the decree of death, had clung to Thaalebeh ]. (S, O.) The pl. of EaluwqN , in this sense, and in the sense next following, as mentioned before, in the paragraph commencing with the word Eulaqa , is EuluqN , with two dammehs. (TA. See that paragraph.) ― -b3- And [hence, likewise,] A calamity, or misfortune. (O, K.) It occurs in a trad. in this sense, applied to what is termed Eu*orap , or to the operation performed upon it. (O, TA. [See 4.]) ― -b4- See also EawolaqN . -A2- Also Pasture upon which camels feed. (S, O, K.) And Trees that are eaten by the camels that have been ten months pregnant, (O, K,) in consequence of which they assume a red hue. (O.) El-Aashà speaks of it [in a verse of which I find four different read- ings] as occasioning a redness in she-camels: but some say that he means thereby The young in the bellies; and by the redness, the beauty of their colour on the occasion of conceiving. (S, O.) And some say that, as used by El-Aashà, it means The sperma of the stallion; a signification mentioned by AHeyth; because the she-camels become altered in colours, and red, when they conceive. sourceDefinition: [is originally an inf. n.: and as a simple subst. signifies An attachment, a tie, or a connection; as also ↓ EuloqapN , mentioned in the TA, in art. rbT , together with wuSolapN , as syn. with raAbiTapN :] a word relating to things conceived in the mind; as love, and contention in an altercation: ↓ EilaAqapN relating to things extrinsic to the mind; as a bow, and a whip: (Kull p. 262:) see EalaqN , last quarter. ― -b2- [Hence, as denoting an attachment, or a tie,] Love, and friendship; or such as is true, or sincere; syn. Hub~N , and SadaAqapN : (K, TA:) [or as expl. voce EalaqN , last quarter:] or it means EalaAqapu Hub~K [ an attachment, or a tie, or a clinging, of love ]: (S, O:) Lh mentions, on the authority of Ks, and as known to As, the saying lahaA fiY qalobiY EalaAqapu Hub~K [i. e. There is to her, in my heart, an attachment, or a tie, or a clinging, of love ]; and likewise, on the authority of the former, but as unknown to As, Hub~K ↓ Eiloqu and Hub~K ↓ EilaAqapu , though As knew the phrase Hub~K ↓ Ealaqu : (TA:) or EalaAqapu Hub~K means love to which one clings. (Msb.) ― -b3- And A contention in an altercation; a dispute; or a litigation: (K: [see also EalaqN , near the end of the paragraph:]) or it means EalaAqapu xuSuwmapK [app. one's connection in such a contention ]: (S, O:) or EalaAqapu xuSuwmapK means the proportion [or share ] that one holds [ in such a contention; or what pertains to one thereof; or one's concern therein ]: (Msb:) [for] ― -b4- EalaAqapN also signifies A thing upon which one has, or retains, a hold; like ↓ EuloqapN in the saying kul~u bayoEK A^aboqaY EuloqapF fahuwa biATilN i. e. [ Every sale that leaves remaining ] a thing upon which the seller retains a hold [ is null ]. (Msb.) And one says, maA bayonahumaA EalaAqapN , with fet-h, meaning There is not between them two anything upon which either of them has a hold against the other: and the pl. is EalaAy^iqu . (TA.) And lifulaAnK fiY h`*aA Ald~aAri EalaAqapN , [or rather h`*ihi AldAr ,] with fet-h, i. e. [ There belongs to such a one, in this house, something upon which he has a hold, or in which he has a concern, or] a remaining portion of a share. (TA.) AlEalaAqapu mina Almahori means That [ portion, or amount, of the dowry, or nuptial gift, ] upon which they have a hold against him who takes a woman in marriage: (Sh, K, TA:) pl. EalaAy^iqu [as above]: (K, TA:) whence the saying, in a trad., A^ad~uwA AlEalaAy^iqa i. e., as expl. by the Prophet, [ Pay ye ] what their families have agreed upon; meaning, what attack each one of them [ by an obligation ] to his companion, or fellow, like as a thing is attached to another thing. (TA.) And [the pl.] EalaAy^iqu likewise signifies [ Obligations of bloodwits; or] bloodwits that are attached to a man. (TA.) [See also another explanation in the fourth of the sentences here following.] ― -b5- Also A work, craft, trade, and any other thing [or occupation ], to which a man has attached himself: (K:) or a work or craft &c. as above, or property and a wife and a child, or love, or a contention in an altercation, pertaining to a man ( yataEal~aqu biA_inosaAnK ): pl. as above. (Har p. 372.) ― -b6- See also EuloqapN , in three places. ― -b7- [The pl.] EalaAy^iqu is also expl. by Lh as meaning Articles of merchandise. (TA.) ― -b8- And AlEalaAqapu is said by Sh to signify Alnabolu [evidently, I think, a mistranscription for Alt~abolu , i. e. Blood-revenge; or the seeking for blood-revenge, or the like; though it seems to be better rendered the obligation of bloodrevenge; or the obligation of a bloodwit, attaching to a man, agreeably with an explanation given above]: and by Aboo-Nasr to signify Alt~abaAEudu [which I think to be a mistranscription for Alt~anaAfudu , signifying contention, disputation, or litigation, a meaning mentioned in the former half of this paragraph]: and both of these significations are assigned to it in the saying of Imra-el-Keys, biA^aY~i EalaAqatinaA tarogabuw na Eano dami EamorKw EalaY marovadi [as though meaning By reason of what bloodrevenge, &c., of ours do ye relinquish the claim for the blood of 'Amr resting as a debt upon Marthad? or What is our contention, &c.? Do ye relinquish &c.]: the b [in biA^aY~i ] accord. to the latter explanation being redundant. (TA. [See also De Slane's “ Diwan d'Amro'lkais, ” p. 48, line 4, of the Ar. text. (in which the former hemistich ends with trgbwn and the latter commences with A^aEano ); and see his translation; and a gloss in the notes, p. 126.]) -A2- See also EaliyqapN .

sourceDefinition: [pass. part. n. of 2, Hung, or suspended, &c.: see its verb. ― -b2- Hence, AlmuEal~aqaAtu Als~aboEu or Als~aboEu AlmuEal~aqaAtu The seven suspended odes; accord. to several writers: two reasons for their being thus called are mentioned in the Mz (49th nwE ); one, that “ they were selected from all the poetry, and written upon qabaATiY~ (pieces of fine white cloth of Egypt) with water-gold, and suspended upon the Kaabeh; ” the other, that “ when an ode was deemed excellent, the King used to say, ' Suspend ye for us this, ' that it might be in his repository: ” that these odes were selected from all the poetry, and that any copies of them were suspended collectively upon the Kaabeh, has been sufficiently confuted in Nöldeke's “ Beiträge zur Kenntniss der Poesie der alten Araber, ” pp. xvii. — xxiii.: it is not so unreasonable to suppose that they may have been suspended upon the Kaabeh singly, at different times, by their own authors or by admiring friends, and suffered to remain thus placarded for some days, perhaps during the period when the city was most thronged by pilgrims; but the latter of the two assertions in the Mz seems to be more probable. ― -b3- Hence also muEal~aqu Alqawosi The appendage of the bow, by which it is suspended: see niyaATN and watarN : and see also EilaAqapN .] ― -b4- muEal~aqapN applied to a woman means One whose husband has been lost [ to her ]: (S, TA:) or [ left in suspense; ] neither husbandless nor having a husband; (O;) [i. e.] whose husband does not act equitably with her nor release her, so that she is neither husbandless nor having a husband; (Az, TA;) or neither having a husband nor divorced. (Msb.) It occurs in the Kur iv. 128. (S, TA.) ― -b5- And one says of a man when he does not decide, or determine upon, his affair, nor relinquish it, A^amoruhu muEal~aqN [ His affair is left in suspense ]. (Z, TA.)

definition: The thing by means of which flesh-meat, (S, Mgh, O, Msb,) and other things, (Mgh, Msb,) or grapes, and the like, (S, O,) are suspended;
sourceDefinition: The thing by means of which flesh-meat, (S, Mgh, O, Msb,) and other things, (Mgh, Msb,) or grapes, and the like, (S, O,) are suspended; (S, Mgh, O, Msb;) as also ↓ muEoluwqN : (S, O:) and anything by means of which a thing is suspended (S, O, K) is called its miEolaAq , (S, O,) or is called miEolaAq and ↓ muEoluwq , (K,) which latter is a word of a rare form: (TA:) and ↓ EilaAqapN likewise signifies the miEolaAq by means of which a vessel is suspended: (TA:) pl. of the first [and of the second] maEaAliyqu . (Mgh, Msb.) Also A stirrupleather: pl. as above. (MA.) And AlmiEolaAqaAni signifies miEolaAqaA Ald~alowi wa$ibohihaA [app. meaning The two suspensory cords of the leathern bucket and of the like thereof ]. (IDrd, O, K: but the CK, for miEolaAqaA , has miEolaAqu : and the O has wamaA A^a$obahahaA in the place of wa$ibohihaA [which means the same].) ― -b2- Also A thing suspended to a beast of burden; such as the qirobap and the miToharap and the qumoqumap : pl. as above. (Mgh, Msb: but in the former, only the pl. of mElAq in this sense is mentioned.) ― -b3- [And A pendant of a necklace and of an earring and the like; in which sense its pl. is expl. as follows:] the maEaAliyq of necklaces (O, TA) and of [the ear-rings or ear-drops called] $unuwf (TA) are what are put therein or thereto, [meaning suspended thereto, ] of anything that is beautiful; (O, * TA;) and ↓ AlA^aEaAliyqu , which has no sing., is like AlmaEaAliyqu , each of them signifying what are suspended. (TA.) [See also $anofN .] ― -b4- miEolaAqu AlbaAbi [means A kind of latch, or sliding bolt; ] a thing that is suspended, or attached, to the door, and is then pushed, whereupon it [i. e. the door ] opens; different from the migolaAq , with the pointed g . definition: He (a man) raised the dust;
sourceDefinition: He (a man) raised the dust; (S, Msb, K;) as also ↓ gb~r , (S, K,) inf. n. tagobiyrN . (S.) [Hence,] fiY wajohihi ↓ gab~ara [so, evidently, but written in the TA without any syll. signs, lit. definition: He milked the camel, drawing what remained in her udder;
sourceDefinition: He milked the camel, drawing what remained in her udder; (Z, Sgh, K, TA;) as also ↓ gab~arahaA . (Ham p. 527.) ― -b2- Hence the following saying, of a people who had increased and multiplied, on their being asked how it was that they had increased: kun~aA laA nalotabiy^u AlS~agiyra walaA natagab~aru Alkabiyra (assumed tropical:) We used not to take the first seed of the young, nor the remainder of the seed of the old; meaning the marrying them, from eagerness to procreate. (TA. [But laA is there omitted in both clauses, and nalotabisu is put by mistake for nalotabiy^u .]) [See also art. lbA^ .] ― -b3- And hence, (TA,) tgb~r mina AlmaroA^api waladF (S, K) (assumed tropical:) He got offspring from the woman [ she being old ]. (K.) It is related that a certain man, (S, K, TA,) an Arab of the desert, (Z,) 'Othmán, accord. to the K, but correctly, as in the Genealogies of Ibn-El-Kelbee, Ghanm ( ganomN ) with gheyn moved by fet-h, and a quiescent noon, (TA,) the son of Habeeb (K, TA) the son of Kaab the son of Bekr the son of Yeshkur the son of Wáïl, (TA,) married a woman advanced in age, (S, Z,) Rakáshi the daughter of 'Ámir, (K,) and it was said to him, “ She is old: ” (S, * K, * TA:) whereupon he said, laEal~iY A^atagab~aru minohaA waladFA (S, K) May-be I shall get from her offspring: (TA:) and when a son was born to him, he named him gubaru , (S, K,) like gumaru ; (S;) and he became the father of a tribe. (TA.) -A2- tgb~r also signifies He, or it, became sullied, or sprinkled, with dust; (TA;) as also ↓ gabira . (L.) You say also Alt~amoru ↓ gabira The dates, or dried dates, became dusty. (TA.)

definition: A remain, remainder, remnant, relic, or residue, (S, K,) of a thing;
sourceDefinition: A remain, remainder, remnant, relic, or residue, (S, K,) of a thing; (K;) generally, of the blood of the menses, (K,) and of milk in the udder: (S, K:) as also ↓ gub~arN : (Msb, K:) or ↓ gub~arN is a pl. of guborN : [but if so it is extr.:] (TA:) or the pl. of guborN is A^agobaArN : (S, K:) and ↓ gub~arN is pl. of ↓ gaAbirN [used as an epithet in which the quality of a subst. is predominant]; (A'Obeyd, TA;) and signifies remains, &c.: (A'Obeyd, S, TA:) and ↓ gub~araAtN is a pl. pl.; i. e., pl. of ↓ gub~arN . (A'Obeyd, TA.) You say bihaA guborN mino labanK In her (the camel) is a remain of milk. (S.) And ↓ gub~aru AlHayoDi signifies The remains [of the blood] of the menses; (S;) as also guboruhu . (Ham p. 37.) And AlmaraDi ↓ gub~aru The remains of the disease. (S.) And in like manner, All~ayoli ↓ gub~aru (S) The last part, and the remains, of the night. (TA.) It is said in a trad. of 'Amr Ibn-El-Ás, maA taA^ab~aTatoniY AlA_imaA='u walaA AlmaA=liY ↓ HamalatoniY AlbagaAyaA fiY gub~araAti [ Female slaves did not carry me under their armpits, ] i. e., female slaves did not have the office of rearing me, nor did prostitutes carry me in the remains of the rags used for the menses. (TA.) And in another trad., mino A^aholi AlkitaAbi ↓ falamo yaboqa A_il~aA gub~araAtN , or A^aholi ↓ gub~aru AlkitaAbi , accord. to different relations, i. e. And there remained not save remains of the people of the Scripture, or the remains &c. (TA.) And in a trad. of Mo'áwiyeh, bifanaAy^ihi A^aEonuzN dar~uhun~a guyorN [ In the court of his house were some she-goats whose flow of milk was a mere remain of what it had been,] meaning, little. (L.) [See also gaAbirN .]

definition: A remaining, lasting, or continuance;
sourceDefinition: A remaining, lasting, or continuance; (TA;) and so ↓ magobarN . (Ham p. 225.) ― -b2- [And by some of the grammarians it is used as signifying The future: see also gaAbirN .] -A2- Also A certain disease in the interior of the foot of a camel. (K.) ― -b2- And A morbid affection in a vein, that will hardly, or in nowise, be cured. (TA.) [See also gabirN .] ― -b3- daAhiyapu Algabari (said by A'Obeyd to be from the phrase juroHN gabirN [q. v.], TA) means A calamity, or misfortune, (JK, S, K,) of great magnitude, (S,) which, (JK, S,) or the like whereof, (K,) is such that no way of escape therefrom will be found: (JK, S, * K: *) or a trial, or an affliction, that will hardly, or in nowise, depart: (TA:) or a person who opposes thee, disagreeing with thee, and then returns, or has regard, to thy saying; (K, TA;) whence the saying, mentioned by AZ, A_il~aA liTalabi AlmiraA='i ↓ maA gab~arato . (TA. [See 2, last sentence.]) ― -b4- Sam~aA='u Algabari , occurring in a verse of El- Hirmázee in praise of El-Mundhir Ibn-Járood, to whom it is applied, is expl. by Z as meaning The serpent that dwells near to a small water in a place where it collects and stagnates, and that will not be approached. (TA.) And [it is said that] Algabaru signifies Water little in quantity. (O.) -A3- Also Dust, or earth; syn. turaAbN . (K.) [See also gubaArN .]

And AlEa$oru AlgawaAbiru mino $ahori ramaDaAna The remaining, or last, ten nights of the month of Ramadán. (TA.) sourceDefinition: Dust-coloured; of a colour like dust: (S:) [fem. gaboraA='u : and pl. guborN .] ― -b2- AlA^agobaru (assumed tropical:) The wolf; (K, TA;) because of his [dusty] colour: like AlA^agovaru . (TA.) ― -b3- And AlgaboraA='u (assumed tropical:) The female of the Hajal [or partridge ]. (K.) ― -b4- Also ( AlgaboraA='u ) (tropical:) The earth; (S, IAth, Msb, K;) because of its dusty colour; or because of the dust that is upon it: (TA:) opposed to AlxaDoraA='u , which means “ the sky, ” or “ heaven. ” (IAth.) ― -b5- And you say, jaA='a EalaY gaboraA='i AlZ~ahori (assumed tropical:) He came on foot: (Z, TA:) [i. e.] he came upon the earth, or ground; and so AlZ~ahori ↓ jaA='u EalaY gubayoraA='i : (M, TA:) or the latter means, he returned without his having obtained, or attained, anything: (T, TA:) or he returned without his having been able to accomplish the object of his want. (El-Ahmar, TA.) And tarakahu AlZ~ahori ↓ EalaY gubayoraA='i (assumed tropical:) He left him in the possession of nothing: (M, TA:) accord. to Zeyd Ibn-Kethweh, it is said by one who has contended in an altercation with another and overcome him so as to become master of all that was in his hands: in all the copies of the K, [probably in consequence of an omission by an early transcriber,] it is expl. as meaning he returned disappointed, or unsuccessful; and so trkh ElY gaboraA='i AlZhr . (TA.) ― -b6- banuw AlgaboraA='i (assumed tropical:) The poor, needy, or indigent; (S, IB, K, TA;) [to which is strangely added in one of my copies of the S and the guests; ] so called because of their cleaving to the dust: (IB, TA:) and gaboraA='u Aln~aAsi likewise means the poor of mankind: or, as some say, the former means strangers from their homes: (TA:) or strangers, (K,) or persons, (TA,) who assemble together for [ the drinking of ] beverage, or wine, without mutual acquaintance: (K, TA:) or persons who contribute equally to the expenses which they have to incur in journeys: all of these meanings have been assigned to it in explaining a verse of Tarafeh: [see EM p. 85:] and it is also expl. in the A as meaning persons of whom one knows not to what family, or tribe, they belong: (TA:) and [it is said that] Aibonu gaboraA='a signifies the thief, or robber. (T in art. bnY .) ― -b7- gaboraA='u also signifies (assumed tropical:) Land abounding with coverts of the kind termed xamar [q. v.]: (TA:) and land abounding with trees; (K;) or so A^aroDN gaboraA='u ; (TA;) as also ↓ gabarapN . (K.) ― -b8- Also (assumed tropical:) Herbage in plain, or soft, land. (Sgh, K.) [This is said in the TA to be more probably with v ; but I do not find any meaning like this assigned to gavoraA='u .] ― -b9- And (assumed tropical:) A species of plant. (S. [App. that called gubayoraA='u , q. v.]) ― -b10- waToA^apN gaboraA='u (assumed tropical:) A footstep, or footprint, that is becoming obliterated, or effaced: (S, A, K:) or such as is recent. (K. [See also dahomaA='u , voce A^adohamu .]) ― -b11- And Eiz~N A^agabaru (assumed tropical:) Might departing; (K, TA;) becoming effaced. (TA.) ― -b12- sanapN gaboraA='u (assumed tropical:) A year of drought; (IAth, K;) a year in which is no rain: (TA in art. $hb :) pl. guborN : so called because of the dustiness of the tracts of the horizon therein from paucity [or want] of rain, and of the ground from there being no herbage. (IAth.) ― -b13- And juwEN A^agobaru (assumed tropical:) Severe hanger or famine. (TA.)

definition: signifies The acting, or treating, wrongfully, unjustly, injuriously, or tyrannically: (S, K:) or the taking another's property wrongfully, &c.

(K.) ― -b3- And ga$ama (tropical:) He collected firewood by night, cutting whatever he could get, without consideration, (K, TA,) or, as in the A, without discrimination. (TA.)

definition: Land without cultivation: (K:) or without any way-mark: (Msb:) or without any waymark and without cultivation: (S, O:) or not rained upon: (Ks, S, O:) or unknown;
sourceDefinition: Land without cultivation: (K:) or without any way-mark: (Msb:) or without any waymark and without cultivation: (S, O:) or not rained upon: (Ks, S, O:) or unknown; in which is no known trace; or vestige: and, accord. to the M, a desert, or waterless desert, that causes one to lose his way, wherein is no sign, or mark: (TA:) pl. A^agofaAlN , (S, TA,) syn. with mawaAtN [q. v.]; (S:) and Lh mentions the phrase A^aroDN A^agofaAlN , as though they made every portion thereof to be what is termed gufolN : and bilaAdN A^agofaAlN , meaning [ tracts of country ] wherein are no way-marks by which to be directed. (TA.) ― -b2- Also A road, or way, &c., in which is no sign, or mark, whereby it may be known. (K.) ― -b3- And A gaming-arrow ( qidoHN ) upon which is no mark [or notch to distinguish it ]; (K;) such as has no portion assigned to it, and no fine: (O, K:) [or,] accord. to Lh, one says qidaAHN gufolN , using the sing. form [of the epithet] meaning [ gaming arrows ] in which are no notches, and to which is assigned no portion and no fine: they used to be added to give additional weight to the collection of arrows from fear of occasioning suspicion [of foul play], i. e. to increase the number: and they were four; the first [called] AlmuSad~aru ; the next, AlmuDaE~afu ; the next, AlmaniyHu ; and the next, Als~afiyHu . (TA.) ― -b4- And A beast ( daAb~apN ) having no brand upon it: (S, O, K:) and a she-camel that is not branded, in order that the poor-rate may not be [ considered as ] incumbent for her: and ↓ gufulN is a dial. var. thereof, or is used by poetic license: the pl. is A^agofaAlN . (TA.) The pl. ( A^agofaAlN ) is also applied to Camels, or cattle, ( naEamN ,) that yield no milk. (TA.) ― -b5- And A muSoHaf [or copy of the Kur-án] bare of the [ signs called ] EawaA$ir [pl. of EaA$irapN q. v.] and the like of these. (TA.) ― -b6- And A book, or writing, [ that is anonymous, ] of which the author is not named. (TA.) And Poetry of which the author is unknown. (K.) And A poet unknown (K, TA) and unnamed [or anonymous ]: pl. A^agofaAlN . (TA.) ― -b7- Also A man inexperienced in affairs. (S, O, Msb, TA.) One whose beneficence is not hoped for, nor his evilness feared; (K, TA;) he being like the shackled that is neglected: pl. as above. (TA.) And One having no grounds of pretension to respect or honour: (K, TA:) or, as some say, of whom one knows not what he possesses. (TA.) ― -b8- And The fur (lit. furs, or soft portions of hair, A^awobaAr , [perhaps because long left unshorn,]) of camels. (AHn, K, TA.)

definition: One who speaks [ with a nasal sound, or twang, i.
sourceDefinition: One who speaks [ with a nasal sound, or twang, i. e.] in [or rather through ] his nose; (TA;) who speaks from his xayaA$iym [app. here meaning (as expl. before) the innermost parts of the airpassages of the nose ]: (S, Msb:) or, accord. to AZ, (Mgh, TA,) whose speech flows, (Mgh, K, *) or passes forth, (TA,) in his lahaAp [app. (as expl. voce gun~apN ) the arches, or pillars, of the soft palate, or the furthest part of the mouth ]: (Mgh, K, TA:) fem. gan~aA='u , applied to a woman. (Msb.) ― -b2- It is also applied to a gazelle ( ZaboYN ), meaning Whose cry issues from his xayaA$iym [expl. above]: J has erred in saying that it is applied to Tayor [i. e. birds, or flying things]: (K:) or if by Tyr he mean flies ( *ubaAbN ), his saying thus is not a mistake, for it is applied to them [as meaning making a humming sound ]. (TA.) ― -b3- [Hence,] waAdK A^agan~u (assumed tropical:) A valley abounding with herbs or herbage: for to such the flies constantly keep, and in their sounds is a gun~ap . (S. [See also mugin~N .]) And (for this reason, TA) one says rawoDapN gan~aA='u i. e. (assumed tropical:) [ A meadow, or garden, ] abounding with herbs or herbage: or in which the winds pass with a sound that is not clear, [i. e. with a confused, humming, or murmuring, sound, ] by reason of the denseness of its herbs or herbage. (K, TA.) And [for the same reason one says] Eu$obN A^agan~u (assumed tropical:) Herbs, or herbage, tall, full-grown, or of full height, and in blossom. (TA.) ― -b4- And (hence also, S) qaroyapN gan~aA='u (tropical:) [ A town, or village, ] abounding with inhabitants (S, K, TA) and buildings (K, TA) and herbs or herbage [ so that in it is heard the hum of men and women and of flies &c. ]. (S, TA.) ― -b5- HarofN A^agon~u means A letter from [ the utterance of ] which results what is termed gun~ap [i. e. the nasal sound thus termed ]. (TA.) ― -b6- See also gun~apN , last sentence.

definition: (tropical:) A valley in which is [ heard ] the sound [or humming ] of flies;
sourceDefinition: (tropical:) A valley in which is [ heard ] the sound [or humming ] of flies; these not being in any valley but such as abounds with herbs or herbage; (S;) a valley of which the flies are abundant, by reason of the denseness, or luxuriance, of its herbs or herbage, so that a gun~ap [or humming ] is heard, produced by their flying: the epithet being applied to it, but being properly applicable to the flies. (TA.) [See also A^agan~u .]
